itinerary.cal: The Labor Mountain Fire closure on the Beverly Turnpike and Bean Creek trails has been lifted, as the Cle Elum Ranger District's trail crew reported on September 25, 2026, but FR 9737-112 is washed out and closed to vehicles: add a mile-plus road walk each way, and expect burned forest, downed trees and overgrown tread on the Bean Creek Trail.

days.note: Standard approach starts at the Beverly Turnpike Trailhead (3,600 ft), follows Trail #1391 then forks right up the Bean Creek drainage (1391A) to Earl Pass (6,200 ft) on the Bean/Standup Creek divide. From the pass, pick up intermittent tread on the southwest ridge and follow it up class 2 terrain to the 7,036 ft summit, with views to Mount Stuart and the Stuart Range. Descend by reversing the same ridge and trail.
days.title: Car-to-car via Bean Creek / Beverly Turnpike Trail and Earl Pass

schedule.label: Leave Beverly Turnpike Trailhead
schedule.detail: Trail #1391, then right fork onto 1391A up Bean Creek drainage.

schedule.label: Reach Earl Pass (6,200 ft)
schedule.detail: Steady climb with switchbacks as the trail steepens approaching the pass; designated tent sites here for parties who choose to camp.

schedule.label: Southwest Ridge scramble to summit
schedule.detail: Intermittent boot tread, class 2 scrambling on the ridge crest to the 7,036 ft high point.

schedule.label: Summit break
schedule.detail: Views of Mount Stuart, the Stuart Range, and on clear days Mount Rainier.

schedule.label: Descend, reversing the ascent route
schedule.detail: Ridge back to Earl Pass, then trail back down Bean Creek drainage.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Total car-to-car time roughly 7-9 hours depending on pace and break length.

days.objective: Summit Earl Peak via the Southwest Ridge and return same day

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day car-to-car: about 7.5 miles round trip with 3,650 ft of gain, typically 7-9 hours including a summit break; no camping needed for the standard trip.

itinerary.cal: The approach starts in British Columbia off Chilliwack Lake Road, so the drive needs passports and a Canadian border crossing by car. A North Cascades National Park wilderness permit covers the camps at Ouzel Lake and the Redoubt Glacier saddle. Best from mid-July into September, once the slabs beside Depot Creek Falls are free of snow.

days.note: Walk the old road grade to the border at Monument 65, then follow the unmarked climbers' path through old growth to Depot Creek Falls. Scramble the steep, often wet slabs beside the falls with the help of the fixed handline, cross the outwash plain above, and climb into the basin to camp at Ouzel Lake.
days.title: Depot Creek to Ouzel Lake

schedule.label: Leave the Depot Creek parking
schedule.detail: About 2,350 ft on the spur off Chilliwack Lake Road.

schedule.label: Monument 65
schedule.detail: Cross into the national park.

schedule.label: Depot Creek Falls
schedule.detail: Handline scramble on wet slabs; the approach's main hazard.

schedule.label: Ouzel Lake camp
schedule.detail: About 5,700 ft.

days.objective: Reach the Ouzel Lake camp

days.note: Scramble around the lake and climb onto the Redoubt Glacier, roped, to the broad saddle at about 7,150 ft, the high camp closest to the Mox peaks. A short day that leaves the afternoon to scout the traverse toward the Col of the Wild.
days.title: Ouzel Lake to the Redoubt Glacier saddle
days.objective: Move camp up to the saddle below Mount Redoubt

days.note: Traverse east on snow beneath Easy Mox and climb the loose talus to the Col of the Wild, then scramble through the notch in the Ridge of Gendarmes and find the gully to the high notch on the west ridge. Three short pitches (5.5, then easier) reach the summit tower. Descend by about three single-rope rappels to the high notch, then downclimb or rappel the gully depending on its snow, and reverse the traverse to camp.
days.title: Summit day on Southeast Mox

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Snow traverse toward the Col of the Wild by headlamp.

schedule.label: Col of the Wild
schedule.detail: Helmets on well before the col; the talus is loose.

schedule.label: Gendarme notch
schedule.detail: Ledges lead through the Ridge of Gendarmes.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Three pitches of the West Ridge to the 8,504 ft top.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: After the rappels, the gully and the traverse.

days.objective: Climb the West Ridge and return to high camp

days.note: Descend from the saddle across the Redoubt Glacier to Ouzel Lake, then reverse the approach down the outwash plain, back down the handline slabs beside Depot Creek Falls, and out through the forest to the car. Some parties split this with a second night at Ouzel Lake.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Depot Creek parking

itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day trip from the Depot Creek parking in British Columbia: in to Ouzel Lake, up to a high camp on the Redoubt Glacier saddle, a long summit day on the West Ridge, and out - roughly 20 miles round trip with about 7,200 ft of gain and the same loss.

road.name: Chilliwack Lake Road and the Depot Creek spur (British Columbia)
road.status: Rough, narrow, overgrown dirt spur; high clearance and four-wheel drive recommended. Parties park where the spur becomes impassable, roughly 1.5 miles up at about 2,350 ft, and walk the old road grade to the border.
road.driveNote: From Highway 1 at Chilliwack, BC, follow Chilliwack Lake Road about 30 miles, past the lake toward its south end, and turn onto the unsigned Depot Creek spur just before the gated bridge over Depot Creek.
road.seasonalGate: Snow on the falls slabs and brush on the spur limit the approach window to roughly mid-July through September.

itinerary.cal: Snow often lingers on the Lago traverse into July, and the Slate Pass access road (FR 5400) typically isn't clear until early-mid summer -- check current conditions before a trip.

days.note: From the Buckskin Ridge trailhead at Slate Pass, the trail drops off the ridge into the Middle Fork Pasayten valley and follows it down-valley to the Berk Creek crossing. Most parties carry full overnight packs and camp near Berk Creek to break up the long approach.
days.title: Approach down the Middle Fork to Berk Creek
days.objective: Reach a camp near the Berk Creek crossing

days.note: Climb Berk Creek over the pass above Freds Lake, drop into Eureka Creek, and continue up toward the Lago-Carru col, then drop slightly to camp near the 7,400 ft tarn below Mount Lago's north slopes. This puts you within striking distance of Dot Mountain for a lighter summit day.
days.title: Push to high camp below Mount Lago
days.objective: Reach the 7,400 ft tarn / Lago-Carru col camp

days.note: Leave camp at first light with a light pack and traverse Lago's rocky north slopes past Points 8207 and 8165 to the Dot Mountain summit. Strong parties continue the mile-long ridge to Ptarmigan Peak before retracing the traverse back to high camp; the ridge gets knife-edged with some easy class 3 near Pt. 8165.
days.title: Summit push over Lago's north slopes to Dot

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Light pack, traverse north past Pt. 8207 toward Lago's north slopes.

schedule.label: Cross to Dot Mountain
schedule.detail: Cross the exposed, occasionally knife-edged ridge past Pt. 8165.

schedule.label: Summit Dot Mountain
schedule.detail: Easy walk-up finish; optionally continue the ridge to Ptarmigan Peak.

schedule.label: Reverse traverse
schedule.detail: Retrace the route across Lago's slopes back toward high camp.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Long day; some parties nap before continuing toward the trailhead the next day.

days.objective: Tag Dot Mountain (and optionally Ptarmigan Peak)

days.note: Break camp and reverse the approach back over the Eureka Creek drainage to the trailhead. It's a long descending day with a couple of re-climbs where the trail crosses drainages.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Buckskin Ridge / Slate Pass trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 4-day, roughly 35-mile round trip with about 6,000-7,000 ft of cumulative gain each way; the standard plan backpacks in to a high camp below Mount Lago and tags Dot Mountain (often combined with Ptarmigan Peak) on a long summit day.

itinerary.cal: Since the Olympic Hot Springs Road washed out in November 2017, vehicle access has ended at Madison Falls, adding roughly 7 miles each way of road walking/biking before the old Whiskey Bend trailhead; check NPS Wilderness Trail Conditions for washouts beyond Elkhorn, and get a wilderness camping permit — best conditions are June through August.

days.note: From the trailhead (Madison Falls, since flood damage in November 2017 washed out the Olympic Hot Springs Road and closed it to vehicles beyond there) follow the old road bed and then the Elwha River Trail south through second-growth and old-growth forest. Grade is gentle and the trail is well-graded, so this is mostly a long valley walk.
days.title: Backpack in to lower Elwha camp
days.objective: Reach the Elkhorn area

days.note: A shorter day continuing up-valley along the Elwha River Trail to the Hayes River patrol cabin/camp area, the closest trail camp to Mount Norton. Check current NPS trail-condition reports first — sections between Elkhorn and Hayes River have had flood/landslide damage in recent years.
days.title: Continue to Hayes River
days.objective: Camp near Hayes River Guard Station

days.note: Leave the heavy gear at Hayes River camp and climb steep, brushy off-trail ground to the upper ridge, then follow class 2 talus/heather slopes to the summit. Out-and-back to the same camp same day.
days.title: Summit push

schedule.label: Leave Hayes River camp
schedule.detail: Light day pack, leave tents/food cache set up.

schedule.label: Start the steep off-trail climb
schedule.detail: Brushy, unmaintained, steep — pick the path of least resistance up open timber and heather bands.

schedule.label: Gain the summit ridge
schedule.detail: Terrain eases to class 2 talus and heather.

schedule.label: Reach the summit (6,319 ft)
schedule.detail: Views over the Bailey Range and Elwha/Hayes drainages.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent line; steep terrain is slower and harder to reverse than it looks.

days.objective: Climb Mount Norton and return to camp

days.note: Retrace the Elwha River Trail (and road-walk/bike section from Madison Falls if the road closure is still in effect) all the way back to the car. A long but flat-grade day.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 4-day trip, roughly 38 miles and ~5,000+ ft round trip: two long valley-trail days in, one steep off-trail summit day from a Hayes River camp, and one long day out.

road.name: Olympic Hot Springs Road / Whiskey Bend Road (Elwha access)
road.status: Closed to vehicle traffic due to washout damage; open to pedestrians, bicycles, and leashed dogs
road.driveNote: Vehicle access ends at the Madison Falls trailhead because of a long-standing road washout (closed for roughly a decade); reaching the Whiskey Bend trailhead/Elwha River Trail requires an additional ~7 miles of walking or biking up the closed road. NPS has an environmental assessment for rehabilitating the road, but the road stays closed to vehicles (open to pedestrians, bicycles and leashed dogs) with no end date given as of the Olympic National Park road-conditions page updated August 7, 2026.

access.fees: $8/person/night (16+; free for 15 and under) + $6 non-refundable reservation fee per permit. An optional annual Wilderness Pass ($45/person) covers per-night fees for 12 months but not the $6 reservation fee.
access.notes: No separate climbing cost-recovery fee like Mount Rainier’s $82 — only the standard entrance fee and wilderness camping permit apply.
access.rules: Olympic NP wilderness regulations; approved hard-sided bear canisters are required for ALL overnight stays throughout Olympic Wilderness, plus a wilderness permit for every overnight trip.
access.permit: Overnight wilderness permit required, reserved via Recreation.gov and issued by the Wilderness Information Center (WIC). Off-trail/cross-country zones such as the Elwha interior/Bailey Range are not on the standard trip-planner map and must be booked directly with the WIC at (360) 565-3100.
access.closures: Olympic Hot Springs Road and its Whiskey Bend Road spur (the trailhead for this approach) have been closed to vehicles since a flood washout; the Olympic National Park road-conditions page updated August 7, 2026 still shows no vehicle access past Madison Falls (the road is open to pedestrians, bicycles and leashed dogs) and gives no end date, despite an NPS road-rehabilitation environmental assessment.
access.land_manager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
access.parking_pass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.

overnight_permit.what: Olympic National Park wilderness camping permit, reserved in advance with a nightly per-person fee
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov or by phone with the Wilderness Information Center, and print it from your account; no same-day walk-up sites are held, and Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin and the East Fork Quinault are quota areas.

itinerary.cal: Stafford Creek Trail #1359 has reopened after the Labor Mountain Fire closure, as the Cle Elum Ranger District's trail crew reported on September 25, 2026; expect burned forest along the lower trail.

days.note: From the Stafford Creek trailhead, follow Stafford Creek through meadows to Navaho Pass (~5.5 mi, ~3,000 ft gain), then turn onto the southwest ridge / south slopes for a Class 2 scramble to the summit. Descend by reversing the same route.
days.title: Car-to-car via Stafford Creek and Navaho Pass

schedule.label: Leave Stafford Creek trailhead
schedule.detail: Start early to beat the heat on the exposed upper slopes and finish at a reasonable hour.

schedule.label: Reach Navaho Pass
schedule.detail: ~5.5 miles and ~3,000 ft gained through Stafford Creek Meadows; junction with the old County Line Trail.

schedule.label: Begin southwest ridge / south slopes scramble
schedule.detail: Steep, loose Class 2 terrain for the final ~700-1,000 ft to the summit; snow patches possible into early summer.

schedule.label: Summit Navaho Peak (7,223 ft)
schedule.detail: Small summit with room for only a few people; views of the Enchantments, Alpine Lakes Wilderness, and Rainier.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent route back through Navaho Pass and down Stafford Creek.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Total elapsed time typically 8.5-9 hours car-to-car.

days.objective: Summit Navaho Peak and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day hike/scramble: about 13 miles round trip with roughly 4,200 ft of gain, typically 8.5-9 hours car-to-car via Stafford Creek Trail to Navaho Pass then the southwest ridge/south slopes - not an overnight trip for the standard approach.

itinerary.cal: Harts Pass Road (to the Slate Pass/Buckskin Ridge Trailhead) typically doesn't open until early-mid July depending on snowpack, and high passes like Rolo/Freds can hold snow into July.

days.note: From the Buckskin Ridge Trailhead near Slate Pass (~6,900 ft), follow the Middle Fork Pasayten River / Robinson Creek Trail past Fred's Lake and over Rolo Pass (~7,100 ft), then drop to camp at Lake Doris. Mostly on-trail with a short cross-country stretch near the pass above Fred's Lake if snow lingers.
days.title: Backpack in to Lake Doris
days.objective: Reach high camp at Lake Doris below Osceola's southwest slopes

days.note: An out-and-back scramble straight from Lake Doris up the broad southwest-facing talus slope to the summit. The talus and lichen-covered rock can be slippery when wet, which slows the descent almost as much as the ascent. The rest of the day is free at camp; some parties use the time to scout toward Mt. Rolo or Mt. Carru.
days.title: Climb Osceola Peak via the southwest slopes

schedule.label: Leave camp light
schedule.detail: Cache overnight gear at Lake Doris and climb with just a day pack.

schedule.label: Reach the southwest talus slope
schedule.detail: Broad talus/scree slope; watch for slick, lichen-covered rock when wet.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Sign the register; views over the Pasayten backcountry toward Carru, Lago, and Rolo.

schedule.label: Leave summit
schedule.detail: Descend the same slope; slick sections can make the descent nearly as slow as the ascent.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Rest, refill water, or continue toward Mt. Rolo if extending the trip.

days.objective: Summit Osceola Peak (8,584 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the Day 1 route: Lake Doris, over Rolo Pass, past Fred's Lake, and back down the Middle Fork Pasayten River / Robinson Creek Trail to the trailhead. A long but straightforward exit day, mostly downhill with a couple of short climbs back over the pass.
days.title: Hike out to trailhead
days.objective: Return to the Buckskin Ridge Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, 2-night backpack: roughly 24-25 miles round trip with about 5,600 ft of cumulative gain, and only 2.5-3 hours of actual climbing on summit day from Lake Doris camp.

itinerary.cal: Cascade River Road to the Eldorado Trailhead is gated/washed out at various points early season - check NPS road status before a spring trip; a backcountry permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center is required for the overnight camps.

days.note: Standard Eldorado Trailhead approach: trail through forest then boot track up the Eldorado Glacier's lower slopes to a campsite near or above treeline, carrying full overnight glacier gear.
days.title: Approach to Eldorado high camp
days.objective: Reach a treeline/high camp near or above the Eldorado Glacier

days.note: Rope up for glacier travel across the Eldorado and Inspiration Glaciers to Klawatti Col, weaving around crevasses; camp on rock or snow near the col.
days.title: Cross Eldorado/Inspiration Glaciers to Klawatti Col
days.objective: Camp near Klawatti Col (~7,500-7,800 ft)

days.note: Drop packs or carry light gear across the North Klawatti/McAllister Glacier to the Primus massif, then pick a Class 2-4 line up the south side to the summit before returning to the col camp.
days.title: Traverse to Primus and climb the south side

schedule.label: Leave Klawatti Col camp
schedule.detail: Rope up for the glacier crossing.

schedule.label: Reach base of Primus's south side
schedule.detail: Stow crampons if terrain goes to rock/talus.

schedule.label: Summit Primus Peak
schedule.detail: Class 2-4 scrambling on the south aspect.

schedule.label: Back at Klawatti Col camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the glacier crossing.

days.objective: Summit Primus Peak (8,508 ft) via the Class 2-4 south side

days.note: Reverse the Inspiration/Eldorado Glacier crossing and descend the boot track and trail back to the Eldorado Trailhead; a long day given the elevation lost.
days.title: Return to Eldorado Trailhead
days.objective: Hike/glacier-travel out to the car

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 3-4 day glacier backpack from the Eldorado side: roughly 20 miles round trip with on the order of 8,000 ft of cumulative gain; most parties budget a buffer day for weather and glacier routefinding.

itinerary.cal: North Cascades National Park requires a backcountry permit for the Colonial Basin camp (advance reservation or walk-up at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center); SR 20 typically isn't plowed open until April/May, so early-season attempts depend on the highway opening date.

days.note: From the Pyramid Lake trailhead on SR 20 (~1,150 ft), follow the Pyramid Lake trail then leave it for a steep, brushy, off-trail climbers' path up Pyramid Ridge and into the basin below Colonial Glacier, camping near a tarn at ~6,100 ft. The mileage is modest but steep talus, brush, and route-finding off-trail make it a full day.
days.title: Approach to Colonial Glacier basin camp

schedule.label: Leave Pyramid Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: SR 20 pullout near Diablo Dam, ~1,150 ft.

schedule.label: Reach Pyramid Lake / leave maintained trail
schedule.detail: Begin steep off-trail ascent of Pyramid Ridge.

schedule.label: Arrive Colonial Basin camp
schedule.detail: Flat, rocky benches near the tarn at ~6,100 ft, below the toe of Colonial Glacier.

days.objective: Reach the ~6,100 ft camp below Colonial Glacier

days.note: An alpine start gets the team across the glacier while it's still firm, up class 3 rock on the summit pyramid, and back to camp by midday. Most parties then break camp and hike all the way out the same day rather than adding a third night, making for a long but complete summit-and-out day.
days.title: Summit day and hike out

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light glacier/summit kit; rope up before the bergschrund/crevasse zone.

schedule.label: Top of Colonial Glacier
schedule.detail: Gain the West Ridge notch above the ice.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Class 3 lichen-covered rock on the final pyramid is the crux of route-finding.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Break camp, repack for the hike out.

schedule.label: Reach trailhead
schedule.detail: Reverse Pyramid Ridge and the Pyramid Lake trail to the car.

days.objective: Climb Colonial Glacier and the West Ridge to the summit, then descend all the way to the car

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, 1-night trip: ~6 mi and 5,000 ft to camp on day 1, then a long ~10 mi summit-and-hike-out day (~1,900 ft up / ~7,100 ft down) on day 2; strong parties occasionally push it car-to-car in one very long day instead.

itinerary.cal: The Dosewallips Road has been washed out ~5.4 mi from the old trailhead since 2002 (not slated for repair), so parties bike the abandoned road bed to save time; the route is normally snow-free and done July-September.

days.note: Ride bikes up the washed-out Dosewallips Road to the old Ranger Station, stash them, then continue on foot up the West Fork Dosewallips Trail past Dose Forks and Diamond Meadows to camp. Most parties camp at Honeymoon Meadows; some push on toward Camp Siberia to shorten the summit day.
days.title: Bike-and-hike approach to high camp

schedule.label: Leave the Dosewallips washout trailhead
schedule.detail: Bikes loaded with overnight gear for the ride up the old road.

schedule.label: Reach the former Ranger Station, stash bikes
schedule.detail: ~7 mi and about 1,900 ft of gain riding the abandoned road bed.

schedule.label: Hike the West Fork Dosewallips Trail
schedule.detail: Forested trail past Dose Forks and Diamond Meadows camps.

schedule.label: Make camp at Honeymoon Meadows (3,527 ft)
schedule.detail: ~14-15 mi and roughly 3,500-4,000 ft of hiking gain from the trailhead.

days.objective: Reach camp at Honeymoon Meadows (or Camp Siberia near Anderson Pass)

days.note: Leave camp with a light pack, cross Anderson Pass, then leave the trail for open scree and talus slopes to the summit — Class 2 with no maintained path, so route-finding matters above treeline. Round trip is about 8 miles with roughly 4,000 ft of gain and loss.
days.title: Summit push

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Light daypack; save weight for the off-trail gain.

schedule.label: Reach Anderson Pass (4,464 ft)
schedule.detail: About 950 ft of gain from Honeymoon Meadows.

schedule.label: Ascend open talus/scree toward White Mountain
schedule.detail: Class 2, off-trail; steepest, loosest ground of the day.

schedule.label: Summit White Mountain (6,378 ft)
schedule.detail: Views of Mt Anderson, Mt LaCrosse, and the Anderson/Eel Glaciers.

schedule.label: Descend the same talus slopes back to camp
schedule.detail: Care needed on loose rock, especially if wet.

days.objective: Climb White Mountain (6,378 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Reverse day one: hike back down the West Fork Dosewallips Trail to the old Ranger Station, retrieve bikes, and coast the washed-out road back to the car. Lighter pack and mostly downhill grade make this faster than the trip in.
days.title: Hike-and-bike out
days.objective: Return to the Dosewallips trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~42-mile round trip up the West Fork Dosewallips (extended by the long-standing Dosewallips Road washout): two long bike-and-hike approach days to a high camp near Anderson Pass, bracketing one big scramble day with ~4,000 ft of gain to the remote 6,378 ft summit.

road.name: Dosewallips River Road
road.status: Permanently closed to vehicle traffic since a January 2002 flood washout; open to foot and bicycle travel only. Vehicles reach a road-end parking about 8.5 miles from US-101, with the washout roughly a mile beyond it.
road.driveNote: Bikes can shortcut the ~7-mile, ~1,900 ft-gain closed roadbed to the former Dosewallips Ranger Station before picking up the West Fork Dosewallips Trail toward Honeymoon Meadows.

itinerary.cal: Pasayten Wilderness requires only a self-issued permit at the trailhead; FS Road 51 to the Thirtymile TH and the high, open Boundary Trail slopes near Wolframite often don't fully clear of snow until late June/July.

days.note: From the Thirtymile Trailhead (~3,400 ft), follow the Chewuch River Trail #510 north 8.8 miles to its junction with the Tungsten Creek Trail #534. Gentle, well-graded trail through forest along the Chewuch River; several established campsites near the junction make a natural first-night stop.
days.title: Approach to the Tungsten Creek junction
days.objective: Hike from Thirtymile TH toward Tungsten Mine Camp

days.note: Climb the Tungsten Creek Trail #534 for 6.2 miles to its junction with the Boundary Trail #533 at historic Tungsten Mine Camp (~6,750 ft), site of two old cabins and mining relics on the south side of Wolframite. Most parties arrive by early-to-mid afternoon, leaving time to set up camp, filter water, and scout the west-side scramble line before dark.
days.title: Up to Tungsten Mine Camp
days.objective: Reach Tungsten Mine Camp at the base of Wolframite

days.note: Leave camp with light daypacks, follow the Boundary Trail about 1 mile west to where it bends south, then leave the trail and ascend the broad, gentle west side of Wolframite (sustained Class 2, with occasional Class 3 variations depending on line) to the 8,136 ft summit. Many strong parties use this camp as a base to also tag Apex Mountain or Bauerman Ridge the same day or the next, but a straight Wolframite round trip comfortably fits a single day from camp.
days.title: Summit day: Wolframite Mountain

schedule.label: Leave Tungsten Mine Camp
schedule.detail: Light daypack; follow the Boundary Trail west.

schedule.label: Leave the Boundary Trail
schedule.detail: Trail bends south; begin off-trail ascent up the open west slope.

schedule.label: Reach the summit
schedule.detail: Broad Class 2 slope tops out at 8,136 ft; views into the Pasayten and across the Canadian border.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent line back to the Boundary Trail.

schedule.label: Back at Tungsten Mine Camp
schedule.detail: Rest, dry gear, and pack for the hike out.

days.objective: Climb Wolframite Mountain's west side and return to camp

days.note: Retrace the full approach — Boundary/Tungsten Creek Trail down to the Chewuch River Trail junction and out to Thirtymile TH — in one long, mostly-downhill day. Fit parties often push straight through rather than splitting the exit into two days.
days.title: Hike out to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to Thirtymile TH

itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day, ~34-mile round-trip backpack (net gain/loss roughly 4,600 ft each way) with a layover day for the Class 2 summit climb from Tungsten Mine Camp; very strong parties compress this to 2 days or even a single long car-to-car push.

road.name: West Chewuch Road (County Rd 1213) continuing as FR 51 (Chewuch River Road)
road.status: Mostly paved near Winthrop, then a typical washboarded dirt/gravel forest road; no 4WD required.
road.driveNote: About 29 miles from Winthrop to Thirtymile Trailhead; the trailhead has a vault toilet, picnic tables, and stock ramp/hitch rails but no potable water.
road.seasonalGate: FR 51 is a long gravel road that can hold early-season snow or washouts; check conditions with the Methow Valley Ranger District before driving in. (The high-clearance-only FS-39-300 spur off FR 39 from Loomis serves the separate Chewuch Trailhead, not Thirtymile.)

itinerary.cal: Access requires FR6510/6514/6517, 10.8 mi of forest road beyond Beckler River Road (FR65) - these spur roads can be rough or snow-blocked into early summer, so check current conditions before driving in.

days.note: A short, brisk scramble on King County's Eagle Rock (5,615 ft) near Skykomish. From the high trailhead on FR6517 it's under a mile to the summit: an ascending traverse across talus below the northeast cliffs to about 5,000 ft, then roughly 600 ft of easy class 2 (or class 2/3 up the center) to the top. Most parties are back at the car in well under 3 hours.
days.title: Car-to-car scramble

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Parking on FR6517, about 0.5 mi east of the summit; head west up through brush into open forest.

schedule.label: Reach talus below the NE cliffs
schedule.detail: Trees give way to open talus slopes beneath Eagle Rock's cliffs.

schedule.label: Ascending traverse to the north side
schedule.detail: Counterclockwise traverse across talus to gain the north side of the peak.

schedule.label: Start the summit scramble at ~5,000 ft
schedule.detail: About 600 ft of class 2 on the right side, or class 2/3 straight up the center.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Short stay - the view is the payoff for under an hour of climbing from the base.

schedule.label: Back at the car
schedule.detail: Reverse the scramble and traverse; round trip typically finishes in under 3 hours.

days.objective: Tag the summit via the class 2/3 talus and rock route

itinerary.totalNote: A short single-day scramble: about 1.6 miles and 1,460 ft round trip, typically under 3 hours car-to-car once at the high trailhead.

road.name: US-2 to 0.8 mi east of Skykomish, then Beckler River Road (FR65) 0.6 mi to FR6510, then FR6510 → FR6514 → FR6517 for 10.8 mi to the trailhead parking area (~4,150 ft elevation), about 0.5 mi/0.8 mi short of the summit
road.status: Rough, narrow Forest Service spur roads with a documented history of washouts, downed trees, blown culverts, and sinkholes on this section of the Skykomish Ranger District. The Forest Service's Skykomish District road-damage alert of June 30, 2026 lists FR 6510 (Bolt Creek Road) closed at its gate at milepost 1.0, with a blown-out culvert at MP 1.2 and a bridge out at MP 2, and FR 6514 (Eagle Creek Road) gated closed at milepost 0, with a blown culvert at MP 1.6 and a sinkhole at MP 7.1; no reopening date is given, so no vehicle can reach this trailhead while that stands. Skykomish Ranger District: (360) 677-2414.
road.driveNote: Paved highway (US-2) to gravel/dirt forest roads; narrow and rough in spots, high-clearance vehicle recommended. MBS National Forest's current-conditions reports have noted shoulder damage on FR65 near milepost 7.4 and 12.1 — check current conditions with the Skykomish Ranger Station before driving, especially after storms.

itinerary.cal: Best conditions are typically July–September after the Twin Lakes access road (FS 3065) melts out; earlier in the season the chimney pitches can be snow/ice-choked.

days.note: From Twin Lakes trailhead (~5,200 ft), hike over Low Pass and High Pass, then drop and traverse cross-country toward the boulders and flat spots below the American Border Peak–Mt. Larrabee ridge. About 80% of this is off-trail on talus, scree, and heather; water can be scarce late season so carry enough to camp dry if needed.
days.title: Approach to high bivy
days.objective: Reach a bivy site near the ABP–Larrabee ridge / "3rd bowl"

days.note: An early start gets the technical ground done while rock is cold and other parties haven't kicked rock down. From the bivy, gain the notch/col below the face, traverse in, and climb the 2-pitch chimney system (rated 5.4, though several parties found it stiffer and harder to protect, more like sustained 5.8 in spots). Reverse the route with rappels over the steep steps, retrieve camp, and hike all the way back out to the car.
days.title: Summit push and full descent to trailhead

schedule.label: Leave bivy
schedule.detail: Alpine start to be off the face before afternoon rockfall risk and thunderstorm buildup.

schedule.label: Reach the base of the Southeast Face
schedule.detail: Cross scree/talus to the start of the technical climbing.

schedule.label: Climb the 2-pitch chimney system
schedule.detail: Class 3-4 face climbing into a chimney with a low-5th-class (5.4-5.8) crux; some parties solo, others pitch it out.

schedule.label: Summit (7,998 ft)
schedule.detail: Views to Mt. Larrabee, the Canadian Border Peak, and the Pickets.

schedule.label: Rappel/downclimb back to the col
schedule.detail: Reverse the steep steps with 2-3 rappels; loose rock demands care on the descent.

schedule.label: Back at bivy, break camp
schedule.detail: Pack up and start the long walk out via High Pass and Low Pass.

days.objective: Climb the Southeast Face chimney to the summit, then descend all the way out

itinerary.totalNote: A committing 2-day trip: ~9.7 miles and ~2,800 ft of net gain, but with a long, mostly off-trail approach and 2 pitches of loose, sustained class 4-5.8 climbing — most parties bivy once near the ABP-Larrabee ridge rather than pushing it car-to-car.

road.name: Twin Lakes Road
road.status: Rough high-clearance road, often impassable to standard vehicles near the top
road.driveNote: Upper road requires high-clearance 4WD; many parties walk the last miles
road.seasonalGate: Snow closure in winter/spring

itinerary.cal: North Cascades NP requires a backcountry camping permit for Ouzel Lake (via recreation.gov / Wilderness Info Center); Depot Creek Road is a rough, sometimes washed-out dirt spur off Chilliwack River Road, best driven with high clearance in mid-summer through early fall.

days.note: Hike the Depot Creek Road washout and old trail up the Depot Creek valley, passing Monument 65 and climbing the steep, wet trail alongside Depot Creek Falls (an 8-ft slippery rock step near the top is the crux of the approach). Camp on the sandy, treeless benches at Ouzel Lake (~5,700 ft), the standard base for both Redoubt and Spickard.
days.title: Approach to Ouzel Lake camp
days.objective: Establish high camp at Ouzel Lake

days.note: From camp, cross Depot Creek and scramble the broken buttress southwest of the lake to gain the Redoubt Glacier, then rope up for a mostly gentle glacier walk (a few crevassed/icy sections) around to the south side. Exit the glacier at the low point near the flying buttress (~7,800 ft), kick steps up a steepening snow gully to short class 2-3 rock ribs and chimneys, and finish through the summit block's chimneys/notches (some parties belay or rappel a short section) to the true summit at 8,969 ft.
days.title: Summit day via Redoubt Glacier / South Face

schedule.label: Leave Ouzel Lake camp
schedule.detail: Cross Depot Creek and scramble the buttress to reach the glacier.

schedule.label: Rope up on Redoubt Glacier
schedule.detail: Glacier travel south then west toward the flying buttress notch (~7,800 ft).

schedule.label: Exit glacier, start snow/rock gully
schedule.detail: Steepening snowfield to ~35° gives way to class 2-3 gullies and rock ribs.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Parties report roughly 6 hours camp-to-summit at this pace.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the route; some parties downclimb or make a short rappel through the summit chimneys.

schedule.label: Back at Ouzel Lake camp
schedule.detail: Full round trip typically 10-12 hours car-to-... i.e. camp-to-camp.

days.objective: Climb Mount Redoubt and return to Ouzel Lake

days.note: Break camp and retrace the Depot Creek trail past the falls and Monument 65 back down to the road washout / parking area. Guides suggest allowing at least 3 hours for the descent alone; with breaks it typically runs 4-5 hours car-to-camp in reverse.
days.title: Exit to trailhead
days.objective: Hike out to the vehicle

itinerary.totalNote: A standard 3-day trip: ~17 miles and ~6,400 ft round trip, with one night at Ouzel Lake camp and a long (10-12 hr) glacier/rock summit day in between; some parties extend to 4 days to also tag nearby Mount Spickard from the same camp.

road.name: Depot Creek Road (accessed via Chilliwack Lake Road, British Columbia)
road.status: Rough, overgrown 4WD road; a major washout blocks all vehicle travel at ~1.7 mi / 2,600 ft
road.driveNote: From Chilliwack Lake Road (BC), drive east ~30 mi to a gated yellow steel bridge over Depot Creek; the unmarked Depot Creek Road forks left ~100 yd before the bridge. Do not confuse it with Paleface Creek Road (tandem bridges) about a mile earlier.
road.seasonalGate: No formal gate, but the washout is a de facto year-round stopping point for vehicles; check current BC road status before relying on older trip reports

itinerary.cal: Boulder Creek fords and lingering snow on the glacier approach are easiest from mid-July through August; the road to White River Trailhead is normally clear by late May but the glacier itself is best climbed before it opens up too much in late summer.

days.note: From the White River Trailhead (2,300 ft), hike the White River Trail about 4 miles, then turn up the Boulder Creek/Boulder Pass Trail, fording Boulder Creek where it braids into several shallow channels. Camp in the basin anywhere from about 4,900 to 5,300 ft with a view of Clark Mountain's south side.
days.title: Approach to Boulder Basin camp

schedule.label: Leave White River Trailhead
schedule.detail: Elevation 2,300 ft; follow White River Trail ~4 miles.

schedule.label: Turn onto Boulder Creek/Boulder Pass Trail
schedule.detail: Ford Boulder Creek's braided channels.

schedule.label: Reach Boulder Basin camp
schedule.detail: Campsites spread from about 4,900 to 5,300 ft; set up base camp.

days.objective: Establish base camp in Boulder Basin

days.note: An alpine start from Boulder Basin gains Boulder Pass and the east-ridge bench before dropping onto the Walrus Glacier. Rope up and pick a line up the moderately steep chute on the glacier's left (southern) margin, watching for narrow crevasses, then finish with a Class 3 scramble and a short 45-50 degree snow traverse to the summit block. Reverse the same line back to camp.
days.title: Summit push via Walrus Glacier

schedule.label: Leave Boulder Basin camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start with light day packs; rope and glacier gear carried.

schedule.label: Gain Boulder Pass / east-ridge bench
schedule.detail: Boulder Pass ~6,300 ft, bench ~6,700 ft.

schedule.label: Onto the Walrus Glacier
schedule.detail: Ascend the chute on the glacier's left margin, stepping over crevasses.

schedule.label: Summit block
schedule.detail: Class 3 rock scramble plus a soft 45-50 degree snow traverse to the top.

schedule.label: Back at Boulder Basin camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the glacier and ridge line; full round trip from camp runs roughly 11.5 hours.

days.objective: Climb Clark Mountain (8,602 ft) via the Walrus Glacier and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and retrace the Boulder Creek/Boulder Pass Trail and White River Trail back to the car, re-fording Boulder Creek along the way.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to White River Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day backpack trip: ~7.5 mi/~3,100 ft up to Boulder Basin camp on day 1, an ~8-mile, ~11.5-hour round-trip summit push via the Walrus Glacier on day 2, and the ~7.5-mile hike out on day 3 — roughly 23 miles and 6,500 ft gained/lost total.

road.name: White River Road (Forest Road 6400)
road.driveNote: From Leavenworth, US-2 west ~15 miles to Cole's Corner, then WA-207 (Lake Wenatchee Highway) ~10.5 miles, then White River Road/FS 6400 ~10 miles to the trailhead at road's end; paved/good gravel, generally passable to passenger cars in summer.

itinerary.cal: The White Chuck River Road (FR 23) is closed at milepost 3.7 and its trail is listed as inaccessible, so this trip starts from the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead and crosses Red Pass both ways. Best conditions are typically July-September.

days.note: Up North Fork Sauk Trail #649 through old-growth forest and a long set of switchbacks to the Pacific Crest Trail, then north on the PCT over Red Pass into the upper White Chuck valley.
days.title: North Fork Sauk Trail to the PCT and over Red Pass
days.objective: Reach the PCT and cross Red Pass

days.note: Follow the PCT down the upper White Chuck valley to Sitkum Creek, then take the steep, unsigned climbers' path up the ridge south of the creek to the high camp at Boulder Basin.
days.title: Down the PCT to Sitkum Creek and up to Boulder Basin
days.objective: Reach Boulder Basin (5,500-6,000 ft)

days.note: Rope up from Boulder Basin, climb the heavily crevassed Sitkum Glacier to a saddle near Sitkum Spire (~9,500 ft), then follow the pumice/scree ridge (with one short snow traverse) to the summit before reversing back to camp.
days.title: Summit via the Sitkum Glacier

schedule.label: Leave Boulder Basin
schedule.detail: Rope up for glacier travel.

schedule.label: Reach the ~9,500 ft saddle
schedule.detail: East of Sitkum Spire, at the top of the glacier.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Final stretch is scree/pumice with a short snow-field traverse.

schedule.label: Back at Boulder Basin camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the glacier; watch for softening snow bridges late in the day.

days.objective: Summit Glacier Peak (10,541 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Break camp, descend the climbers' path to the PCT, and walk back up the White Chuck valley and over Red Pass to the North Fork Sauk Trail and the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day trip at minimum. The walk in from the North Fork Sauk trailhead is far longer than the old White Chuck approach and crosses Red Pass in both directions, so many parties allow an extra day.

road.name: North Fork Sauk Road / Sloan Creek Road (FR 49)
road.status: Gravel, with rough and washed-out sections; medium or high clearance is recommended and a low-clearance car may not clear them.
road.driveNote: From Darrington, follow the Mountain Loop Highway about 16.3 miles to Sloan Creek Road (FR 49), then about 6.6 miles to the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead. The White Chuck Road (FR 23) approach from the north is a different start and is closed at milepost 3.7.
road.seasonalGate: The Mountain Loop Highway's Deer Creek to Bedal section is gated through the winter and typically reopens in mid-May; FR 49 can hold snow into early summer in heavy years.

itinerary.cal: Best climbed June-October once the rock is dry; Esmeralda Trailhead access road and the basin can hold snow into early June some years.

days.note: A single long day: hike over Ingalls Pass and past Lake Ingalls to the North/East col, rack up and climb two low-5th-class pitches to the East Peak summit, then rappel back to the col and retrace the trail out. No camping — this is done car-to-car by essentially all parties.
days.title: Car-to-summit day climb

schedule.label: Leave Esmeralda Trailhead
schedule.detail: Early start recommended to beat afternoon thunderstorms and the crowds this popular basin draws on weekends.

schedule.label: Reach Ingalls Pass
schedule.detail: ~3 mi and ~2,300 ft of steady climbing on the Ingalls Way Trail.

schedule.label: Traverse past Lake Ingalls
schedule.detail: Drop slightly to the lake basin, then rock-hop/scramble up talus toward the North/East col.

schedule.label: Reach the North/East col, rack up
schedule.detail: Gear up for the route below the notch separating the North and East summits.

schedule.label: Climb the 2-pitch Southwest Face to the East Peak summit
schedule.detail: Low 5th class climbing on slabs and a gully; loose/dirty rock reported low on the route, cleaner higher up.

schedule.label: Rappel to the col, hike out to trailhead
schedule.detail: Rappel the route through three stations to the col, then retrace the approach through Ingalls Pass.

days.objective: Climb the East Peak Southwest Face (2 pitches) and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A single roadside day out of Esmeralda Trailhead, roughly 9-10 hours car-to-car with about 10 miles and 3,300 ft of gain; no overnight is involved.

itinerary.cal: The Wolf Creek approach crosses old burn with little shade; most parties go mid-July through September once the trail and upper basins are snow-free, and it's worth checking current Wolf Creek Road conditions before driving in.

days.note: From the Wolf Creek Trailhead (~2,950 ft), follow the maintained Wolf Creek Trail #527 roughly 10 miles to Gardner Meadows, then continue off-trail on grassy slopes to a basin camp around 6,000-6,250 ft. Parties note little shade on this stretch (old burn) and occasional blowdown near the meadows, so an early start and full water bottles matter on hot days.
days.title: Approach to Gardner Meadows / Wolf Creek Basin
days.objective: Backpack in to high camp below Gardner's west ridge

days.note: Leave camp pre-dawn and climb the grassy/scree slopes west of the outlet stream to a small basin around 6,200 ft, then work up the west ridge (class 2-3, loose in spots) to Gardner's summit. Strong parties continue the connecting ridge over Point 8,487 - dropping onto snow/scree below cliff bands to bypass exposed sections - to reach North Gardner, then reverse the same line back to camp.
days.title: Gardner Mountain via West Ridge, saddle traverse to North Gardner

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Grassy/scree slopes toward the 6,200 ft basin below the west ridge.

schedule.label: Reach west ridge crest
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 scrambling, loose in places; stay on the whisper of a trail where visible.

schedule.label: Summit Gardner Mountain (8,898 ft)
schedule.detail: Trip reports place summit time for the linked route around 8-9 AM for a 5 AM start.

schedule.label: Saddle traverse toward Point 8,487
schedule.detail: Drop to the low route (~7,400 ft) under the cliff bands rather than the exposed direct ridge crest.

schedule.label: Summit North Gardner Mountain (8,956 ft)
schedule.detail: Optional extension; some parties turn around at Gardner if time/conditions are marginal.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Descent is fast: plunge-step scree, glissade remaining snow, and grass-slope down to the basin.

days.objective: Summit Gardner Mountain and (optionally) North Gardner via the connecting ridge/saddle

days.note: Break camp and reverse the approach: off-trail down to Gardner Meadows and out the Wolf Creek Trail to the trailhead. Mostly descending with minor undulation.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Wolf Creek Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~25-mile round trip with roughly 7,300-8,000 ft of total gain/loss - backpack in to Gardner Meadows (~5,700 ft) or the basin camp above it (~6,200 ft), a long summit day linking Gardner and North Gardner over the connecting ridge/saddle, then hike out. Very fit parties have done both peaks car-to-car in one very long day, but the standard, comfortable plan is 2-3 days.

itinerary.cal: North Cascades Highway (SR-20) access to Colonial Creek Campground is seasonal (typically mid-April to mid-November); a backcountry permit from the NPS is required for the moraine camp, and the route is usually driest/safest July-September.

days.note: Hike the Thunder Creek Trail from Colonial Creek Campground, a long up-valley slog past Skagit Queen Camp to a flat, sandy moraine camp at roughly 6,350 ft just below Park Creek Pass (camping is not permitted at the pass itself). Most parties treat this day as the logistical crux of the trip.
days.title: Approach to moraine camp
days.objective: Reach the moraine camp near Park Creek Pass

days.note: Traverse about 2 miles around a broad ridge to the gentle Fremont Glacier (~8,000 ft), rope up for crevasse hazard, then climb a snow finger/rock gully to a low point on the summit ridge and follow an exposed Class 3-4 ridge to the true summit before reversing the route, including a short rappel off the top.
days.title: Fremont Glacier summit push

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start for the glacier traverse.

schedule.label: Rope up on Fremont Glacier
schedule.detail: Ice/water-filled cracks reported even in good years.

schedule.label: Reach the summit
schedule.detail: Via the Class 3-4 ridge and short rappel.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Descent retraces the glacier and gully.

days.objective: Climb the Fremont Glacier and summit ridge, return to camp

days.note: Reverse the full Thunder Creek Trail back to Colonial Creek Campground — a tired-legs repeat of Day 1's mileage.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Thunder Creek Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A long 3-day trip (~39 mi RT, ~9,600 ft gain) bookended by two grueling 18-mile trail days on the Thunder Creek Trail, with one committing glacier-and-ridge summit day in between.

itinerary.cal: Slate Pass / Harts Pass area access road typically doesn't open until late June or July depending on snowpack, and the Pasayten is prone to wildfire smoke/closures in August-September, so early-mid July through early September is the realistic window.

days.note: From the Slate Pass / Buckskin Ridge trailhead, follow the Robinson Creek Trail down to the Middle Fork Pasayten River, then up past Freds Lake and through the Eureka Creek valley to a camp near Shellrock Pass. Mostly on trail, snow-free by midsummer, with one notable slick-log creek crossing.
days.title: Backpack in to Shellrock Pass camp

schedule.label: Leave Slate Pass trailhead
schedule.detail: Robinson Creek Trail, descending toward the Middle Fork Pasayten River.

schedule.label: Pass Freds Lake turnoff
schedule.detail: Continue up Eureka Creek valley toward Shellrock Pass.

schedule.label: Reach Shellrock Pass camp
schedule.detail: Flat, somewhat exposed camp; some parties build a small wind wall.

days.objective: Establish high camp near Shellrock Pass / Freds Lake basin

days.note: A long day-hike loop from camp along open ridge and talus, class 2 the whole way once past Point 8207/8165 -- widely regarded as the easiest Bulger, little more than a walk. Most parties tag Dot Mountain on the same ridge since it costs little extra; some also add Mount Lago if energy and weather allow.
days.title: Climb Ptarmigan Peak (with Dot Mountain)

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light daypack; head up toward the saddle north of Point 8207.

schedule.label: Traverse Point 8165 and Dot Mountain
schedule.detail: Climbers path bypasses 8207/8165 on the west/left side before the ridge to Dot.

schedule.label: Summit Ptarmigan Peak (8,614')
schedule.detail: Gentle class 2 ridge walk for the final mile; sweeping views over the Lago group and treeless, Scottish-Highlands-like terrain.

schedule.label: Return to Shellrock Pass camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge; parties combining Lago or Dot both ways often return well into the evening.

days.objective: Summit Ptarmigan Peak via the ridge traverse from Shellrock Pass, tagging Dot Mountain en route

days.note: Reverse the Day 1 approach via Eureka Creek and Freds Lake back to the Middle Fork Pasayten River and up to Slate Pass. Some parties split this into two shorter days (4-day trip total) rather than one long exit day.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Slate Pass trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~36-mile round trip from Slate Pass with one moderate approach day, one long summit day (often combined with Dot Mountain and/or Mount Lago), and one exit day; strong parties sometimes compress it to 2 days, and some stretch the exit into 2 days for a 4-day trip.

itinerary.cal: Depot Creek Road is typically washed out well below the trailhead, adding miles/hours to the approach, and the route crosses the US/Canada border near Monument 65, so budget extra logistics time versus a straightforward trailhead start.

days.note: From the Depot Creek Road washout / Monument 65 area, follow the Depot Creek trail through old-growth forest, then talus and moraine benches up to Ouzel Lake (~5,640 ft). The tread fades in and out on talus and slide-alder slopes above the forest, so allow extra time route-finding the upper basin.
days.title: Approach to Ouzel Lake camp
days.objective: Reach Ouzel Lake basecamp

days.note: An alpine start from camp gets you across the talus gully and onto the Southwest Glacier while snow is firm, roped up for crevasses, before finishing on the South Ridge's Class 2-3 shattered rock to the summit. Reports show camp-to-summit in roughly 3.5-4.5 hours with a similar or faster glissade-assisted descent back to camp.
days.title: Summit day: Southwest Glacier / South Ridge

schedule.label: Leave Ouzel Lake camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start while the snow gully and glacier are still firm.

schedule.label: Gain the Southwest Glacier saddle
schedule.detail: Talus gully then heather/moraine benches lead onto the glacier; rope up here.

schedule.label: Cross glacier, reach South Ridge/col
schedule.detail: Roped glacier travel, then transition to Class 2-3 rock on the shattered south ridge.

schedule.label: Summit (8,983 ft)
schedule.detail: Typical camp-to-summit time is 3.5-4.5 hours in trip reports.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Descent often faster via glissade/plunge-step on the snow slopes; afternoon free to rest or break camp.

days.objective: Climb Mount Spickard and return to Ouzel Lake camp

days.note: Reverse the approach back down through the talus benches and forest to the trailhead/road washout. The descent usually runs a bit faster than the way in once the tread and cairns are familiar.
days.title: Hike out to trailhead
days.objective: Descend Depot Creek trail to the car

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, 2-night trip: roughly 20 miles and 7,000 ft round-trip, with both nights spent at Ouzel Lake and an alpine-start summit push (about 4-7 hours round trip) via the Southwest Glacier and South Ridge; strong parties sometimes compress this to 2 days.

road.name: Depot Creek Forest Service Road (BC) to Chilliwack Lake / Depot Creek trail (US side, foot only)
road.status: Rough, high-clearance 4WD recommended on the BC FSR; no vehicle access on the US side above the border — everything past Monument 65 is on foot.
road.driveNote: Roughly 3.5+ hours' drive from the Seattle area to the BC trailhead area, plus extra time for the US-Canada border crossing (add an hour or more depending on wait times); there are washouts and logging damage near the road/trail's end, so plan for a longer approach on foot than older mileages suggest.
road.seasonalGate: Snow can block the Chilliwack Lake Road into early summer; the FSR is typically only reasonably passable once fully snow-free, roughly June onward.

itinerary.cal: The NNE gully and upper basin often hold snow into early-mid summer; an ice axe (and sometimes crampons) can be useful before roughly July, and this route is driven in from the Teanaway side to the Esmeralda trailhead, not up Icicle Creek Road.

days.note: This is done as one long day from the Esmeralda (Longs Pass) trailhead, not a backpack — parties cross Longs Pass, drop to Ingalls Creek, peel off onto a rough climbers' path into the Sherpa-Argonaut basin, climb a class 3-4 gully to the ridge, traverse to the block, do the short 5.7 shoulder-stand/friction move and rappel off the fixed anchor, then reverse the whole approach. Total round trip is roughly 14 miles with about 7,500 ft of gain and loss (trailhead ~4,250 ft to the 8,605 ft high point, with Longs Pass crossed in both directions).
days.title: Car-to-car: Esmeralda TH to the Balanced Rock and back

schedule.label: Leave Esmeralda (Longs Pass) trailhead
schedule.detail: Most parties start pre-dawn by headlamp given the length of the day.

schedule.label: Leave the maintained trail
schedule.detail: Branch onto the unmaintained climbers' path toward Sherpa-Argonaut basin; expect brush and downed timber.

schedule.label: Enter Sherpa-Argonaut basin (~7,000 ft)
schedule.detail: Begin the broad NNE-trending gully toward the ridge crest east of the balanced rock.

schedule.label: Gain the ridge, traverse to the block
schedule.detail: Class 3-4 travel over blocks and sandy benches west along the ridge to the base of the balanced rock.

schedule.label: Climb and rappel the block
schedule.detail: Shoulder-stand/friction pitch (5.7) to the top, then rappel from the fixed anchor back to the ledge.

schedule.label: Reverse the route to the car
schedule.detail: Down the ridge, gully, and basin, back to Ingalls Creek and over Longs Pass to the trailhead, typically finishing in daylight or early evening for parties that keep moving.

days.objective: Tag the Sherpa Balanced Rock summit block via the NNE gully and ridge traverse

itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: about 14 miles round trip with ~7,500 ft of gain and loss, including a short 5.7 shoulder-stand pitch and rappel; fit parties that don't linger finish car-to-car in roughly 10-13 hours.

itinerary.cal: North Cascades Highway (SR-20) over Washington Pass usually opens in April or May and closes with heavy snow, typically between mid-November and early December — prime dry-rock season is June-September.

days.note: Hike the Blue Lake trail then cut up to the base of SEWS's southwest face, climb 7 pitches of low-5th to 5.8 rock to the summit, then downclimb part of the South Arete and make 3 rappels from bolted stations back to the base.
days.title: Car-to-car climb

schedule.label: Leave Blue Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: Popular route — early start beats other parties to the base.

schedule.label: Reach base of Southwest Rib
schedule.detail: About 1 hr of steady uphill approach.

schedule.label: Top out, summit
schedule.detail: 7 pitches of 5.6-5.8.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Downclimb part of the South Arete, then 3 rappels from bolted stations to the base.

days.objective: Climb the Southwest Rib and return to the Blue Lake trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: about 9.5 hrs car-to-car with roughly 2,600 ft gain over 7 pitches.

road.name: Blue Lake Trailhead, SR-20 (North Cascades Highway)
road.status: Paved highway parking at the Blue Lake Trailhead lot; no unpaved road driving required.
road.driveNote: Roughly 3-3.5 hours from Seattle via SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) to the Washington Pass area (~milepost 162).
road.seasonalGate: SR-20 closes seasonally over Washington Pass due to avalanche danger; dates vary by year (in the 2025-26 season it closed Dec 4, 2025 and, after winter storm damage, did not fully reopen until June 14, 2026), so the area is inaccessible by car for a large part of the year.

itinerary.cal: The Slate Peak road (trailhead access, WA's highest drivable road) typically isn't snow-free until early July, and the Pasayten's remoteness means this route is really only a July-September outing.

days.note: From the Buckskin Ridge/Slate Peak trailhead (~6,900 ft), climb over Slate Pass and drop past Fred's Lake, then continue through the Eureka Creek valley and up into Shellrock Basin, camping in the basin below Shellrock Pass (~6,800 ft). Trip reports split this into two shorter days via a Fred's Lake camp, but strong parties do it in one long push.
days.title: Backpack in to Shellrock Basin
days.objective: Reach high camp near Shellrock Pass

days.note: An early start from camp, up onto Shellrock Pass and along Blackcap's northeast ridge — a Class 2-3 scramble with maybe one or two harder moves, finishing on the distinctive black hornfels summit cap. Round trip from camp runs about 5 hours, leaving the afternoon free to rest or tag Mt. Lago/Mt. Carru if water and energy allow.
days.title: Summit day: Blackcap Mountain

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Begin the climb from the Shellrock Pass bivy/camp.

schedule.label: Reach Shellrock Pass
schedule.detail: Gain the ridge crest for morning views before traversing toward Blackcap.

schedule.label: Reach the summit
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 northeast ridge scramble tops out on the black hornfels summit block.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge route back toward camp.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Round trip from camp runs roughly 5 hours.

days.objective: Climb Blackcap via the northeast ridge

days.note: Reverse the approach: down through Eureka Creek, back over the Rolo Pass/Fred's Lake area and Slate Pass, and out to the Buckskin Ridge/Slate Peak trailhead. Some parties split this into two shorter days with a camp on the Pasayten River flats instead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 3-day, roughly 30-34 mile round trip into the Pasayten Wilderness with about 8,000-8,500 ft of cumulative gain; many parties instead stretch it to 4-5 days to also tag nearby Mt. Lago and Mt. Carru from the same Shellrock Basin camp.

itinerary.cal: Typically climbed March-April while ice/névé fills the runnels — outside the May 15-Oct 31 permit season, so no overnight permit is needed to camp at Colchuck Lake, though the approach road may have limited winter access.

days.note: Hike (or skin) the Stuart Lake Trail to Colchuck Lake and camp below the north face; expect firmer, colder travel and possibly a longer walk if the access road isn't fully plowed.
days.title: Winter/spring approach to Colchuck Lake camp
days.objective: Reach camp at Colchuck Lake

days.note: Climb runnels connecting snow bands at the lowest point of the nordwand (between Triple Couloirs and Backbone Arete) — an ice pitch, a snowfield, rambling ice with screw protection, and a thin M4 rock crux — finishing in the third couloir shared with Triple Couloirs. Descend the Aasgard Pass scramble back to camp.
days.title: Climb Gerber-Sink, descend to camp

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: First ice pitch off a sapling/cam belay.

schedule.label: Mixed crux
schedule.detail: Thin, rock-protected M4 section.

schedule.label: Finish in the 3rd couloir
schedule.detail: Shared upper finish with Triple Couloirs.

days.objective: Summit via Gerber-Sink

days.note: Break camp and hike/ski back out to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-3 day trip in shoulder-season ice conditions: camp at Colchuck Lake, then a full mixed/ice day (9-11 hrs) climbing Gerber-Sink to the summit and descending to camp before hiking out.

itinerary.cal: Route sits at ~7,500 ft near Washington Pass, which typically doesn't open (gate/avalanche) until roughly late April-May; parties in early/mid season should expect lingering snow on the approach and gully as seen in the June 2026 report.

days.note: This is a single-day outing, not a backpack — parties drive to the Washington Pass hairpin turnout, hike ~1.5-2 hrs up through forest, meadows, and a boulder/scree gully to Kangaroo Pass and the base of the North Face, climb the 3-pitch route, then rappel the route (3x 60m raps from bolted/chain anchors) and hike back out. Trip reports consistently show 7-11 hours car-to-car depending on party size and snow conditions on the approach.
days.title: Car-to-car climb

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Hairpin-turn turnout ~1 mile past Washington Pass on SR-20; forest/meadow trail toward Kangaroo Pass.

schedule.label: Reach base of North Face
schedule.detail: Boulder field and loose scree gully below Kangaroo Pass; rack up at the north-ridge notch.

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: P1 (5.6) up and left along an angled crack, then broken rock to a belay ledge.

schedule.label: Top out / reach summit
schedule.detail: After P2 traverse and the P3 crux corner/slab pitch; optional 4th-class bonus pitch or scramble to the true summit block.

schedule.label: Begin rappels
schedule.detail: Three single-rope (60m) raps from chain anchors at the top of the face and at the P1 belay.

schedule.label: Back at the car
schedule.detail: Retrace the approach trail down through the boulder field and forest.

days.objective: Climb the North Face (5.6, 3 pitches) and return to the car

itinerary.totalNote: A long single day car-to-car: roughly 7-11 hours depending on party size and snow conditions, with ~2,500 ft of gain over about 6 miles round trip — no camping involved.

itinerary.cal: Since the Monte Cristo road/bridges are washed out, virtually all current parties bike the first 4.2 miles; the north-facing col holds steep snow well into summer, and the moat below the summit gully gets progressively harder to cross later in the season (worse by late July/August).

days.note: From Barlow Pass (2,360 ft) bike or hike the washed-out mining road 4.2 miles to the Monte Cristo townsite, then follow the Glacier Basin trail 2.5 miles past Glacier Falls and behind Mystery Hill to camp in upper Glacier Basin (~4,500 ft). Bikes cut the flat road section to well under an hour and are what most current parties use since the road/bridges washed out.
days.title: Bike & backpack in to Glacier Basin camp

schedule.label: Leave Barlow Pass
schedule.detail: Bike the old mining road toward Monte Cristo; road/bridge washouts mean most parties walk bikes through 1-2 short sections.

schedule.label: Reach Monte Cristo townsite
schedule.detail: Stash bikes here (~2,760 ft) and switch to foot travel.

schedule.label: Arrive Glacier Basin camp
schedule.detail: Trail climbs past Glacier Falls, rounds Mystery Hill, then eases into the basin around 4,500 ft.

days.objective: Reach high camp in upper Glacier Basin

days.note: An alpine-start day: talus and steep snow (to ~45°) lead up the center gully to the North Col, then a short traverse, moat crossing, and ~75 ft summit gully (a few mid-5th-class moves, rope/belay commonly used) gain the summit ridge. Descent reverses the route — downclimbing or rappelling the short chimney — before breaking camp and hiking/biking all the way back to the trailhead.
days.title: North Col route to the summit, then out to the car

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Early start to have firm snow on the col approach and avoid afternoon rockfall/soft-snow issues.

schedule.label: Reach the North Col (~6,760+ ft)
schedule.detail: Steep snow up to ~45° through the gully above the lower cliff bands; helmets on.

schedule.label: Cross the moat and climb the summit gully
schedule.detail: ~75 ft gully, often with a short belay; near the top move onto Class 2-3 ledges or take the mid-Class 5 rock to bypass an overhanging block.

schedule.label: Summit (7,136 ft)
schedule.detail: Typical summit time for a pre-dawn start; views of Kyes, Cadet, and the Monte Cristo group.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Downclimb or rappel the chimney (inspect any fixed anchors), reverse the moat crossing and col descent.

schedule.label: Break camp and hike/bike out
schedule.detail: Pack up Glacier Basin camp, retrace the trail to Monte Cristo, then bike the road back to Barlow Pass, typically arriving at the car by early evening.

days.objective: Climb the North Col route and descend all the way to Barlow Pass

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, ~16-mile round trip with about 4,800 ft total gain — the standard way organized/club parties do this climb given the technical col, moat crossing, and washed-out approach road, though strong/fast parties do climb it car-to-car in a single long (10-14 hr) day using bikes for the approach.

road.name: Mountain Loop Highway (FR 20) to Barlow Pass, then the closed/gated former road to the Monte Cristo townsite
road.status: Paved and open to Barlow Pass; permanently closed to vehicles beyond due to Sauk River washouts (2003, 2006) — foot/bike only for the remaining ~4 miles to Monte Cristo.
road.driveNote: From Granite Falls, drive about 31 miles east on the Mountain Loop Highway (passing the Verlot Public Service Center at roughly mile 11) to the Barlow Pass trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Snow can keep Barlow Pass itself gated or impassable into late spring; check Mount Baker-Snoqualmie NF road status before driving.

itinerary.cal: Road (FS 3160) and upper snow patches typically clear by mid-summer; best conditions are roughly July through September.

days.note: A short, roadside scramble done entirely car-to-car in a half day. An easy, well-used boot path climbs steeply to Church Lake in well under an hour, then fainter tread continues up rolling alpine meadows and a ridge toward Point 6066 before a final short class 2-3 scramble gains the true summit. Most parties are back at the trailhead by early-to-mid afternoon.
days.title: Church Lake to Bearpaw Mountain summit

schedule.label: Leave FS Road 3160 trailhead
schedule.detail: High-clearance vehicle recommended for the last stretch of gravel road.

schedule.label: Reach Church Lake
schedule.detail: Steep but short established trail; a common turnaround for hikers just visiting the lake.

schedule.label: Gain the ridge near Point 6066
schedule.detail: Tread fades above the lake into open meadows and talus; route-find up the ridge.

schedule.label: Scramble to the summit
schedule.detail: Final ~100m to the true summit is class 2-3 scrambling on exposed rock.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge and boot path back toward Church Lake.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Total round trip roughly 4-5 hours including a summit break.

days.objective: Tag the Bearpaw Mountain summit (6,091 ft) via Church Lake and the ridge/scramble above

itinerary.totalNote: A short single day: roughly 4-5 hours car-to-car, about 3.7 miles round trip with 1,300 ft of gain, including a short class 2-3 scramble to the true summit.

itinerary.cal: North Cascades NP requires a backcountry camping permit for the basin camp; Easy Pass trailhead (SR-20) is only accessible once the North Cascades Highway opens for the season, typically late April to early November.

days.note: Hike the well-graded Easy Pass Trail to the 6,550 ft pass, then leave the trail and sidehill traverse west across scree, talus, and grassy benches at roughly 6,600-6,800 ft to the basin camp south of Mesahchie Peak. Only two workable flat tent sites exist in the basin, so it can be worth arriving mid-afternoon to claim one.
days.title: Approach to basin camp below Mesahchie

schedule.label: Leave Easy Pass trailhead
schedule.detail: 3.6 mi, ~2,700-2,800 ft gain of maintained trail.

schedule.label: Reach Easy Pass (6,550 ft)
schedule.detail: Leave the maintained trail here.

schedule.label: Sidehill traverse to basin
schedule.detail: Cross-country scree/talus/grass traverse at ~6,600-6,800 ft; about an hour of sidehilling once past the pass, plus route-finding time.

schedule.label: Make camp
schedule.detail: 6,600 ft basin south of Mesahchie; set up and scout tomorrow's approach to the col.

days.objective: Reach the 6,600 ft basin camp south of Mesahchie Peak

days.note: From camp, climb loose talus to the small col/pass below Katsuk, then work up the complex system of gullies, ramps, and slabs of the Southwest Gully to just below the mushroom-shaped summit block. The final class 4 summit block is short but exposed and is usually the crux both ways. Many parties link Katsuk with neighboring Mesahchie the same day via the connecting gullies along Ragged Ridge, turning this into a longer full-day traverse.
days.title: Summit day: Katsuk (and often Mesahchie)

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light alpine-start pack; climb toward the col below Katsuk.

schedule.label: Reach col/pass below Katsuk
schedule.detail: Loose rock approach from camp, roughly 800-1,000 ft of gain.

schedule.label: Ascend the Southwest Gully
schedule.detail: Class 3 scrambling on very loose rock through the gully/ramp system to the base of the summit block.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Exposed class 4 scramble up the final summit block.

schedule.label: Descend to summit block base, then reverse
schedule.detail: Downclimb the exposed class 4 block first (the most consequential part of the descent), then reverse the loose gully.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Rest, or continue on to Mesahchie if energy and weather allow.

days.objective: Climb Katsuk Peak via the Southwest Gully

days.note: Reverse the Day 1 traverse and descent: sidehill back to Easy Pass, then descend the maintained trail to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Easy Pass trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip covering ~12 miles round trip and ~2,900 ft of net gain to the basin camp, with a short but slow (loose, exposed class 3-4) summit day on Katsuk from camp; most parties tag neighboring Mesahchie Peak the same day via the connecting gullies.

itinerary.cal: Best mid-July through September when snow bridges over the Cascade/Middle Cascade Glacier crevasses and the summit gullies are stable; Cascade River Road (FR-15) and the Cascade Pass TH typically open by early-mid summer depending on snowpack.

days.note: Hike the maintained Cascade Pass trail (3.7 mi) to the pass, then leave trail up Mixup Arm and across the Cache Glacier to Cache Col, dropping to camp near Kool-Aid Lake / Red Ledge on the Ptarmigan Traverse side. Real parties cover this in 4.5-6 hours depending on pace and snow conditions on the glacier traverse.
days.title: Approach to Kool-Aid Lake / Red Ledge camp
days.objective: Establish camp near Kool-Aid Lake (~6,200 ft)

days.note: The long, complex day: cross the Middle Cascade Glacier to the Spider-Formidable col, then work south and west through a maze of ledges, gullies, and short Class 4 slabs to the summit, descending the same way (often with 1-2 short rappels off loose rock). Routefinding at the col and on the upper ledges is the crux of the day — parties that nail it are back at camp well before dark; parties that don't can be out well past dusk.
days.title: Summit push via Spider-Formidable col and the south face

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Kool-Aid Lake, cross toward the Middle Cascade Glacier.

schedule.label: Reach Spider-Formidable col (7,320 ft)
schedule.detail: Common nav-error spot — the correct line goes south/west, not down the steep western side.

schedule.label: Traverse south-face ledges/gullies
schedule.detail: Class 4 slabs and exposed ledges, sometimes snow-covered; a 30m rope is useful for protecting the trickiest step and for short rappels.

schedule.label: Summit (8,325 ft)
schedule.detail: A well-executed day reaches the top notably earlier than this if the col and ledges go smoothly.

schedule.label: Reverse the route to the col
schedule.detail: Rappel the steepest, loosest sections rather than downclimb.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Trip reports document parties returning anywhere from early evening to as late as 11:30 PM with headlamps after routefinding trouble.

days.objective: Climb Southeast Ledges/South Face to the 8,325 ft summit and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the Day 1 approach: back over Cache Col, across the Cache Glacier and Mixup Arm, and down the Cascade Pass trail to the car. Typically 6-6.5 hours at a normal pace.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Cascade Pass Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip covering roughly 20-22 miles round trip with about 6,000-6,600 ft of cumulative gain; Day 2 is the long, technical crux day and can run 8-16 hours depending on routefinding. Strong parties sometimes compress this to 2 days with an even longer single summit day.

road.name: Cascade River Road (Forest Road 15)
road.status: Paved to about mile 10, then gravel with potholes and washboard to its end at mile 22.3 (Cascade Pass Trailhead, 3,600 ft). The June 2026 vehicle closure at milepost 20 (Eldorado) for storm/flood repairs has been lifted; the park's road-conditions page, updated July 3, 2026, lists the road open.
road.driveNote: No RVs, large trailers, or vehicles over 22 feet on the upper, narrower gravel section.

itinerary.cal: Cascade River Road below the Cascade Pass trailhead has washed out in several recent seasons, adding 2-6 miles of road walking each way when unrepaired; check NPS North Cascades road-conditions alerts shortly before your trip, and plan for July-September for stable glacier travel and snow-free rock on the summit block.

days.note: From the Cascade River Road trailhead (add 2+ miles of road walking if the seasonal washout below the trailhead hasn't been repaired), climb through forest and meadow to Cascade Pass, then continue up over Cache Col into the basin near Kool-Aid Lakes. This is the heaviest pack day of the trip with a full load of camp and glacier gear.
days.title: Approach to Cache Col / Kool-Aid Lakes
days.objective: Cross Cascade Pass and Cache Col, establish first camp

days.note: Rope up for glacier travel: cross the Red Ledges, the Middle Cascade Glacier, and the Spider-Formidable col, then drop to Yang Yang Lakes before climbing to a high camp at Le Conte-Sentinel Col, directly below Sentinel Peak's west face. This is the technical crux of getting into position and typically the longest day of the trip.
days.title: Glacier traverse to high camp at Le Conte-Sentinel Col
days.objective: Reach Le Conte-Sentinel Col (7,300 ft) high camp

days.note: Drop packs and climb Sentinel's west face: ascend a steepening snow ramp to about 7,400 ft, take a ledge system left/north past cliff bands, then finish on low 5th-class rock steps to the west ridge and the summit. Many parties tag class-3 Old Guard Peak from the same col before descending to a lower camp at Yang Yang Lakes.
days.title: Summit Sentinel + Old Guard, move camp down

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Drop overnight gear at the base of the west face snowfield.

schedule.label: Top of snow ramp, onto the rock
schedule.detail: Snow ramp steepens to roughly 7,400 ft, then a ledge leads left across the face.

schedule.label: Summit Sentinel Peak
schedule.detail: Low 5th-class steps and a short gully gain the west ridge; walk it to the top.

schedule.label: Reach Old Guard-Sentinel col
schedule.detail: Descend and traverse to the base of Old Guard Peak.

schedule.label: Summit Old Guard Peak
schedule.detail: Class 3 scramble on the northwest side; parties often top out by early-to-mid afternoon.

schedule.label: Arrive Yang Yang Lakes
schedule.detail: Roughly a 2-hour descent from the col with full packs to the lower camp.

days.objective: Climb Sentinel Peak (8,257 ft) and Old Guard Peak, descend to Yang Yang Lakes

days.note: Retrace the route from Yang Yang Lakes back over Cascade Pass to the Cascade River Road trailhead (plus the road walk if it's still washed out). Mostly downhill but with the final climb back over the pass before the long descent to the car.
days.title: Exit to trailhead
days.objective: Hike out via Cascade Pass to the road
