itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day glacier backpack, roughly 34 miles and 8,500 ft cumulative gain round trip, with high camps at Cache Col/Kool-Aid Lakes and Le Conte-Sentinel Col; strong parties compress this to 3 days by pushing all the way to the col on day 1.

road.name: Cascade River Road (north approach) / Suiattle River Road, FSR 26 (south approach)
road.status: Cascade River Road is open: its Pincer Two Fire closure at MP 8 (Marble Creek), in place from July 23, 2024, was lifted on September 20, 2024, and the park's road-conditions page, updated July 3, 2026, lists the road open — check current NPS road-condition alerts before a trip. Suiattle River Road (FSR 26) is closed to vehicles at about MP 4 under a long-term Forest Service closure order (No. 06-05-26-03, effective April 2, 2026 through January 1, 2028) following atmospheric-river flood damage; Grade Creek (FSR 2640), Tenas Creek (FSR 2660), Green Mountain (FSR 2680) and Forest Road 25 are closed as well. The Downey Creek trailhead is normally still reachable on foot or bike from the MP 4 closure point, adding roughly 16 miles each way (about 32 miles round trip) of road walking/biking, but the Forest Service's Miner's Fire order (06-05-26-17) closes the Downey Creek Trailhead and Downey Creek Trail #768 from August 15 through December 31, 2026, unless rescinded sooner.
road.driveNote: Verify current status at nps.gov/noca (Cascade River Road) and the MBS National Forest alert page (Suiattle River Road) before driving out, as road status is subject to change.
road.seasonalGate: Cascade River Road is additionally gated for winter each year around MP 20 (Eldorado)

itinerary.cal: The CJ Couloir is best climbed early-season while still consolidated snow — by mid/late summer the Sill Glacier breaks up and it gets discontinuous and rockier; also verify Cascade River Road is open to the trailhead and get a North Cascades NP wilderness permit for the overnight bivy.

days.note: From the Cascade Pass trailhead (verify Cascade River Road status first — it washes out periodically), walk back to the hairpin, scramble down, cross the creek, and bushwhack about 15 minutes to the base of the CJ Couloir. Climb roughly 3,400 ft of snow/ice — best done in the cold pre-dawn hours when it's frozen and rockfall risk from Johannesburg is lowest — to reach the C-J col and bivy on the snow there.
days.title: Approach and CJ Couloir to a col bivy

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Alpine start to be on the couloir while it's still frozen.

schedule.label: Reach base of CJ Couloir
schedule.detail: After the hairpin, creek crossing, and brush bushwhack.

schedule.label: Climb the CJ Couloir
schedule.detail: ~3,400 ft of snow/ice; fast light parties do it in ~3.25 hrs, expect 4+ with overnight packs.

schedule.label: Top out at C-J col
schedule.detail: Find a bivy site on the snow near the col.

schedule.label: Rest and rack up at camp
schedule.detail: Rehydrate and nap through the heat of the day; sort gear for tomorrow's pitches.

days.objective: Reach the Cascade-Johannesburg col via the CJ Couloir before the day warms

days.note: Traverse from the col to the base of Cascade Peak's NW Chimney in the moat and climb the roughly 3-pitch route (loose crux crack, then a cleaner 5.8 chimney, then a short loose pitch and simul-climbing to the summit). Rappel the route back to the moat, return to the col, break camp, then reverse the CJ Couloir and hike out — a long, full day.
days.title: NW Chimney to the summit, then out

schedule.label: Leave col camp
schedule.detail: Light rack for the climb; some parties cache overnight gear at the col and grab it on the way down.

schedule.label: Start climbing NW Chimney
schedule.detail: From the moat below the col; loose crux crack pitch first.

schedule.label: Reach the summit
schedule.detail: After the 5.8 chimney pitch and a final loose/simul pitch.

schedule.label: Finish rappelling back to the col
schedule.detail: ~3 rappels down the route, building gear anchors as you go.

schedule.label: Break camp, reverse the couloir
schedule.detail: Descend the CJ Couloir; snow is softer and rockfall risk higher than the morning ascent, so move deliberately.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: ~12 hrs car-to-car-again on day 2.

days.objective: Climb the East Ridge/NW Chimney and descend all the way to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day round trip: ~3,400 ft of snow/ice up the CJ Couloir to a col bivy on day 1, then a long ~12-hr day 2 combining 3 technical pitches (5.8 chimney) with a full descent back to the car — about 4,200 ft total gain and 11+ miles round trip.

itinerary.cal: Cathedral Rock Trailhead's access road is rough gravel best driven with high-clearance/4x4; the route is typically climbed June-September once the Cathedral Pass trail and Daniel Glacier snow are in reasonable shape.

days.note: From the Cathedral Rock Trailhead (~3,350 ft), climb steadily via Squaw Lake and over Cathedral Pass (~5,600 ft) before dropping slightly to camp at Peggy's Pond (~5,560 ft). Trail is well-graded switchbacks up to the pass, then a rougher/fainter path along the basin to the pond.
days.title: Approach to Peggy's Pond
days.objective: Backpack in to high camp at Peggy's Pond

days.note: Alpine start from Peggy's Pond, ascend on trail/snow toward the SE ridge and onto the Daniel Glacier to reach the Middle and West Summits (~2,400 ft gain from camp). Most parties are back at camp by mid-afternoon, break camp, and continue the ~5.5 mile, 2,700 ft descent out to the trailhead the same day, finishing in the evening.
days.title: Summit push and hike out

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start from Peggy's Pond, light packs for the summit push.

schedule.label: Reach base of Daniel Glacier
schedule.detail: Rope up / gear up for glacier travel if crevasses are open.

schedule.label: Summit (West Peak)
schedule.detail: Real trip reports of the adjacent SE-ridge route show parties topping out on all three summits around 1:00-1:15 PM.

schedule.label: Back at Peggy's Pond
schedule.detail: Break camp and repack for the hike out.

schedule.label: Trailhead
schedule.detail: Full descent of Cathedral Pass trail back to the car.

days.objective: Climb the Daniel Glacier / SE Slopes to the Middle and West (true) Summits, then hike all the way out

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day/1-night trip: ~15 miles round trip with about 5,100 ft total gain; many parties extend to 3 days by adding a rest/weather day or side trips to Cathedral Rock, Tuck & Robin Lakes, or the Jade/Marmot Lakes basins.

itinerary.cal: Best late June through September once the Longs Pass approach and rock are snow-free; the Teanaway River Road trailhead is usually accessible by early June.

days.note: From the Longs Pass Trailhead, climb over Longs Pass (6,200 ft), drop to the Ingalls Creek basin, then climb back up talus and slab to a flat bivy spot near 'Table Rock' at treeline below Sherpa's west side. Most parties take 6-7 hours with overnight and rock gear.
days.title: Approach to treeline bivy
days.objective: Reach camp near 'Table Rock' (~7,400 ft) below the West Ridge

days.note: Leave camp before dawn, scramble to the base of the ridge, then climb 5-6 pitches (5.4 with a crux that feels more like 5.5) to the summit block. Reverse the ridge by rappel, then descend all the way back over Longs Pass to the trailhead — a long 12-14 hour day.
days.title: Climb the West Ridge, descend, hike out

schedule.label: Leave bivy
schedule.detail: Head for the base of the West Ridge

schedule.label: Rope up
schedule.detail: Begin the 5-6 pitch ridge, mostly class 3-4 with 5.4 sections

schedule.label: Reach the crux pitch
schedule.detail: Hand-crack/chimney pitch, feels closer to 5.5

schedule.label: Begin the descent
schedule.detail: Rappel the summit block, reverse the ridge

schedule.label: Back at the car
schedule.detail: Hike out over Longs Pass, often finishing by headlamp

days.objective: Summit via the West Ridge and return to the car

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day round trip: ~14.5 miles and ~4,300 ft gain total, with day 2 a long 12-14 hour push from bivy to summit and back to the car.

itinerary.cal: Best climbed July-September once the Chilliwack River crossing has dropped and the Bear Creek ford and approach gullies are manageable. The page is built on the US approach over Hannegan Pass; a North Cascades National Park wilderness permit is needed for every night past the pass, and the Bear Creek camp has been closed since the 2021 fire, so plan the first night elsewhere on the Chilliwack River Trail.

days.note: From the Hannegan Pass Trailhead climb about 4 miles to Hannegan Pass, then drop east past Boundary Camp into the Chilliwack valley, bearing right at the park boundary onto the Chilliwack River Trail. Continue past U.S. Cabin camp, cross the Chilliwack River by the cable car, and camp near the Brush Creek junction, about 12 miles from the car.
days.title: Hannegan Pass to Brush Creek

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Hannegan Pass Trailhead, about 3,100 ft.

schedule.label: Hannegan Pass
schedule.detail: About 4 miles and 2,000 ft up; the rest of the day loses height.

schedule.label: Camp near Brush Creek
schedule.detail: About 12 miles in, on the Chilliwack River Trail.

days.objective: Reach a Chilliwack River Trail camp near Brush Creek

days.note: Follow the Chilliwack River Trail about 5 more miles down-valley to the Bear Creek confluence (the camp there is closed). Ford Bear Creek and climb steep, brushy timber and then huckleberry and slide alder east to the meadows above Ruta Lake, then traverse below Points 6592 and 6822, crossing a rock rib, to the saddle camp at 6,480'. The long off-trail climb makes this the hardest approach day.
days.title: Brush Creek to the high camp

schedule.label: Bear Creek confluence
schedule.detail: Leave the maintained trail and ford the creek.

schedule.label: Arrive high camp
schedule.detail: Saddle at 6,480' on the NW ridge past Ruta Lake, below Points 6592/6822.

days.objective: Reach the 6,480' saddle camp on Bear's NW ridge

days.note: Descend a gully from camp to the toe of the North Buttress, then climb the glacier-couloir/buttress line to the summit before reversing the descent gully back to camp. This is the long day of the trip — most of it spent on 5th-class rock with some 3rd/4th-class terrain low and high on the route.
days.title: Summit via the North Buttress

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Descend the approach gully toward the toe of the buttress.

schedule.label: Rope up at base of buttress
schedule.detail: Glacier couloir gains the start of the technical climbing.

schedule.label: Top out / reach summit
schedule.detail: Sustained 5th-class pitches on the buttress lead to the 7,931' summit.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: 3rd/4th-class descent gully reverses the morning approach.

days.objective: Climb the North Buttress and tag the 7,931' summit

days.note: Reverse the traverse to the meadows above Ruta Lake, descend the brush and timber to re-ford Bear Creek, and walk back up the Chilliwack River Trail to camp near Brush Creek (or push on toward U.S. Cabin or Copper Creek camp to shorten the last day).
days.title: High camp to Brush Creek
days.objective: Descend to the Chilliwack River Trail and camp

days.note: Recross the Chilliwack River by the cable car, climb back past Boundary Camp to Hannegan Pass, and descend the last 4 miles to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out over Hannegan Pass
days.objective: Return to the Hannegan Pass Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 5-day trip from the Hannegan Pass Trailhead: two approach days to a 6,480' saddle camp, a big 10+ hour summit day on the North Buttress, and two days back out - roughly 45 miles round trip with about 12,000 ft of gain and the same loss.

access.fees: $10/person/night + a flat $6 nonrefundable reservation fee (charged mid-May–early Oct only; free the rest of the year). No separate climbing fee — North Cascades NP entrance itself is free.
access.notes: 60% of sites (Boston Basin/Eldorado/Sulphide Glacier/etc.) are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Leave No Trace; follow park backcountry camping rules in this remote zone.
access.permit: Backcountry/wilderness permit required for overnight camping in North Cascades National Park; check current regulations.
access.closures: Access roads and trails (e.g., Hannegan) may have seasonal gates or washouts.
access.land_manager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass / Interagency pass at trailheads

overnight_permit.what: North Cascades National Park wilderness permit, required once past Hannegan Pass into the Chilliwack valley — quota, not free
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov, especially for the popular Copper Ridge/Chilliwack corridor; the park increasingly issues reserved permits by email after a mandatory safety video rather than an in-person pickup. The short stretch on the Mount Baker-Snoqualmie side above Hannegan Camp needs a separate, free, self-issue Mount Baker Wilderness permit at the trailhead.

itinerary.cal: Phelps Creek Road (FS 6211) is rough gravel and best climbed July-September once the scree ramp and stream-bed crux are snow-free.

days.note: Hike the Phelps Creek Trail then break off onto the Leroy climbers' path, which steepens sharply (around 1,200 ft/mile) into Leroy Basin. Parties report going through several liters of water on this leg in afternoon heat; camp in the trees away from the busier lakeside sites.
days.title: Approach to high camp

schedule.label: Leave Phelps Creek trailhead
schedule.detail: ~3,500 ft; well-graded trail for the first ~3.5 miles.

schedule.label: Turn off onto Leroy climbers' path
schedule.detail: About 1.5 hrs from the trailhead to the Leroy High Route junction.

schedule.label: Arrive Leroy Basin camp
schedule.detail: ~6,100 ft; steep final push, plan for a hot, exposed climb with a full overnight pack.

days.objective: Reach Leroy Basin camp

days.note: A long day: cross Leroy Pass and Freezer Pass, drop into the Ice Lakes basin, then traverse a loose, consequential stream-bed crux before gaining the southwest ridge on a scree ramp. The scrambling above is chossy class 3 (feels like low class 4 with the exposure) with several one-at-a-time sections to avoid rockfall.
days.title: Summit push via Freezer Pass and the SW ridge

schedule.label: Wake, leave camp before/at sunrise
schedule.detail: Light packs; leave the overnight gear at Leroy Basin.

schedule.label: Freezer Pass, drop into Ice Lakes basin
schedule.detail: Cross-country traverse, ~500 ft down to the basin.

schedule.label: Stream-bed crux
schedule.detail: Loose clay/scree gully — tricky down-climb and re-ascent, reported as the route's toughest obstacle.

schedule.label: Gain the southwest ridge
schedule.detail: ~400 ft up a scree/talus ramp to the ridge crest.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Class 3-4 ledges and gendarmes on the final push; trip reports place summit arrival early-to-mid afternoon.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the full line; budget 7+ hours round trip from camp.

days.objective: Climb South Spectacle Butte (8,392 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and retrace the Leroy climbers' path and Phelps Creek Trail back to the car.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~21-mile round trip with a long class 3-4 summit day out of a Leroy Basin high camp; ~7,500 ft of cumulative gain, most of it on day 2.

itinerary.cal: Smithbrook Road (FR 6700) is unplowed in winter, adding ~2 miles of snow-road walking each way if attempted before the road opens (typically melts out by early-mid summer); the trail approach described here assumes the road is drivable.

days.note: Start early from the Smithbrook Road trailhead, climb the Smithbrook Trail to the PCT, follow the PCT toward Lake Valhalla, then leave the trail near the southeast ridge saddle to scramble up open boulder and heather slopes to the summit. Descend by reversing the same line, staying low near the lakeshore rather than dropping straight down the steep upper slopes.
days.title: Car-to-car scramble via Lake Valhalla

schedule.label: Leave Smithbrook Road trailhead
schedule.detail: Start up the Smithbrook Trail switchbacks through forest.

schedule.label: Reach the PCT junction
schedule.detail: Turn onto the Pacific Crest Trail heading toward Lake Valhalla.

schedule.label: Leave the trail near the SE ridge saddle
schedule.detail: Above Lake Valhalla, begin scrambling up open boulder/heather slopes.

schedule.label: Reach the summit
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 scrambling near the top; views of Glacier Peak and Stevens Pass.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge and slopes, staying low near the lakeshore.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Total car-to-car time roughly 7.5 hours.

days.objective: Reach the summit of Lichtenberg Mountain (5,844 ft) via the southeast ridge and return

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day car-to-car: roughly 7-8 hours, ~9 miles round trip with about 2,500 ft of gain, no camping involved.

road.name: Smithbrook Road (FR 6700)
road.status: Gravel, generally passable to passenger cars in dry conditions; can be rough/washboarded and may hold snow into early summer.
road.driveNote: 3.1 miles of gravel from Hwy 2 (turnoff ~0.6 mile before milepost 68) to the Smithbrook Trailhead at about 4,000 ft.

itinerary.cal: Best snow-free window is roughly mid-July through September; an Olympic National Park wilderness permit is required for the overnight camps, and some parties extend to 5 days to also tag nearby Mount Steel from a First Divide camp. The North Fork Skokomish Trail and its camps (Camp Pleasant, Nine Stream, Two Bear, First Divide) are closed after the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire, so this plan cannot be followed until the park reopens them.

days.note: From the Staircase Ranger Station (~850 ft) the North Fork Skokomish River Trail climbs gently and steadily through old-growth forest, with several creek crossings, to Nine Stream Camp. This is the easy, graded part of the trip — save energy for the steep push later.
days.title: Approach up the North Fork Skokomish
days.objective: Reach Nine Stream Camp

days.note: A short, steeper day up the valley to a high camp at Two Bear Camp (~3,600 ft), a little over a mile below First Divide. Arriving early leaves time to scout the start of tomorrow's climbers' path before dark.
days.title: Push to high camp below Mount Hopper
days.objective: Reach a high camp at Two Bear Camp

days.note: Climb the main trail to just below First Divide, where the old Mount Hopper Way leaves it; from there it is an unmaintained, brushy, route-finding climb, about 2,400+ ft from camp to the summit in all — steep forest giving way to open slopes near the top. Trip reports flag genuine route-finding difficulty, so budget extra time versus a maintained trail.
days.title: Summit day

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Early start for cool temps on the brushy lower climb.

schedule.label: Reach Way Trail junction
schedule.detail: Begin the steep, unmaintained climbers' path.

schedule.label: Break into open slopes
schedule.detail: Forest gives way to more open terrain; route-finding gets easier to read.

schedule.label: Gain the summit ridge
schedule.detail: Short final scramble to the top.

schedule.label: Summit (6,120 ft)
schedule.detail: Views toward the Sawtooth Range and Lake of the Angels.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Descend the same way, watching for the correct brush corridor.

days.objective: Climb Mount Hopper via the Mount Hopper Way Trail and return to high camp

days.note: A long but mostly gentle, downhill-trending day back down the North Fork Skokomish trail to the car.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Staircase trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day backpack: ~28.4 mi round trip and ~5,300 ft of net gain to the 6,120 ft summit, most of it easy river-valley trail plus one genuinely steep, route-finding summit day on an unmaintained 'way trail'.

itinerary.cal: Accessed via the North Fork Sauk Trailhead because the White Chuck River Road (FR 23) has been closed from milepost 3.7 since March 19, 2025, with no end date given on the Forest Service alert updated June 30, 2026; best conditions are typically July-September once the Gerdine/Cool glacier crevasses are well-bridged.

days.note: From the North Fork Sauk Trailhead, hike through old-growth to Mackinaw Shelter, climb steeply to the PCT at White Pass, then traverse and climb to a rocky camp at Glacier Gap with views south to Rainier.
days.title: Approach to Glacier Gap camp
days.objective: Reach high camp at Glacier Gap (~7,200 ft)

days.note: Alpine start from Glacier Gap, drop to rocky Gerdine Ridge, then rope up on the Gerdine Glacier where it's reached (~8,500 ft), following it to a bend where it merges with the Cool Glacier and climbing to the Disappointment/Glacier Peak saddle and the summit. Move briskly under the rockfall-prone cliffs of Disappointment Peak.
days.title: Summit via Gerdine Ridge / Cool Glacier

schedule.label: Leave Glacier Gap camp
schedule.detail: Crampons on for the descent to Gerdine Ridge.

schedule.label: Rope up at ~8,500 ft
schedule.detail: Climber's trail ends at a gendarme; step onto the Gerdine Glacier.

schedule.label: Merge onto Cool Glacier
schedule.detail: Two small, easily-avoided crevasses at the bend.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Via the Disappointment/Glacier Peak saddle.

schedule.label: Back at Glacier Gap camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the glacier and ridge.

days.objective: Summit Glacier Peak (10,541 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse the full approach back to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip for most parties (~36-37 miles RT, ~9,000-9,400 ft gain); fast/fit or ski-equipped parties have done it car-to-car-plus-camp in 2 days.

road.name: North Fork Sauk Road / Sloan Creek Road (FR 49)
road.status: Rough gravel with washout spots around mile 1 and mile 6; a medium- or high-clearance vehicle is recommended, low-clearance cars may not clear one or both spots.
road.driveNote: From Darrington, drive the Mountain Loop Highway 19.7 mi to Sloan Creek Road (FR 49), turn left, and continue 6.6 mi to the trailhead.

itinerary.cal: The Putvin trailhead sits on FR-25, the Hamma Hamma River road; check Olympic National Forest alerts before going, as this area has been affected by wildfire closures in recent years.

days.note: The Putvin Trail is steep and rough - the headwall below the lake takes hand-and-foot scrambling on roots and rock - so most parties treat it as a half-day in with a full overnight pack. Camp at Lake of the Angels, which also serves as the base for nearby Mount Stone.
days.title: Backpack in to Lake of the Angels camp
days.objective: Set up basecamp at Lake of the Angels

days.note: An early start lets you cache overnight gear at camp and climb light: scramble talus and side-hill terrain up toward the summit ridge, then a short class 2-3 section (rock is notoriously rotten) to the top. After descending to camp, break camp and hike the brutal trail back out the same afternoon - a long but standard weekend pattern for this approach.
days.title: Summit push and hike out

schedule.label: Alpine start from camp
schedule.detail: Light daypacks, overnight gear cached at camp.

schedule.label: Reach base of summit scramble terrain
schedule.detail: Talus, side-hilling, and contouring below the summit ridge on loose, rotten rock.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 finish; take care on the rotten rock near the top.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Down-climb the summit section carefully, then break camp and re-pack for the hike out.

schedule.label: Begin hike out
schedule.detail: Full overnight pack back down the steep, rooted Putvin Trail.

schedule.label: Trailhead
schedule.detail: End of trip.

days.objective: Climb Mount Skokomish (6,434 ft) and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, 1-night weekend trip: roughly 12 miles round trip with about 5,100 ft of cumulative gain, most parties backpacking in on day one and combining the summit push with the full hike-out on day two.

itinerary.cal: Steep, snow-covered slopes and pine-needle duff make this best done in dry summer/early-fall conditions; the Forest Road 49 approach can be rough (high-clearance recommended) and the Glacier Peak Wilderness trailhead is a long drive from the Seattle area.

days.note: A steep, remote day scramble from the North Fork Sauk trailhead: one mile of maintained trail to the old lookout tread, then a climber's path with a short Class 3 ledge section, meadows near Ruby Lake, and a final scramble up the red rock summit massif. No camp is used — parties do the whole thing in a long single day.
days.title: Car-to-car scramble

schedule.label: Leave North Fork Sauk trailhead
schedule.detail: Trailhead sits at ~2,100 ft; long drive in (Darrington + ~7 mi of Forest Road 49), so most parties start at first light.

schedule.label: End of maintained trail (~3,100 ft)
schedule.detail: About 1 mile in; beyond here the route becomes an unmaintained climber's path.

schedule.label: Class 3 ledge section
schedule.detail: A short (~70 ft) steep rock-and-dirt scramble section marks the start of real route-finding; pink ribbons mark a faint boot path above it.

schedule.label: Ruby Lake / meadows
schedule.detail: Path continues through meadows near Ruby Lake toward the base of the summit rock massif.

schedule.label: Summit (6,975 ft)
schedule.detail: Final scramble up the red rock massif; views of Glacier Peak dominate to the northeast.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Descend the same climber's path; loose dirt/needles on the steep sections make the descent slow and slippery — many parties use microspikes or trekking poles for control.

days.objective: Reach the summit of Painted Mountain (Red Mountain) and return

itinerary.totalNote: A long, steep single day: ~8 miles round trip with ~4,875 ft of gain/loss, done entirely car-to-car with no camp.

road.name: Mountain Loop Highway to FR 49 (Sloan Creek Road)
road.status: Open (as of May 2026)
road.driveNote: FR 49 is gravel/dirt and generally passable to passenger cars but can develop potholes and washboarding. A landslide closed the Mountain Loop Highway at milepost 37.5 (blocking FR 49 and North Fork Sauk/Sloan Creek trail access) from around December 2025 until repairs reopened it in mid-May 2026 -- always check current Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alerts before heading out, since washouts recur along this corridor (the Suiattle River Road elsewhere in the forest has also seen long-term closures).
road.seasonalGate: No permanent seasonal gate at this junction, but FR49 can remain snowbound or storm-damaged into early summer in heavy-snow years.

itinerary.cal: Road and trail are typically snow-free and accessible early-to-mid summer through fall; check North Fork Sky road status and expect lingering snow on the glacier/upper ridge into July.

days.note: The near-universal way this route is done: a single long day from the Blanca Lake Trailhead. A good trail leads to Virgin Lake, then travel gets much slower on the faint climbers' path along the south ridge and the loose, ledgy Class 3 ground to the chossy summit block.
days.title: Car-to-car ascent

schedule.label: Leave Blanca Lake Trailhead
schedule.detail: Early start to cross snow/glacier terrain while firm and be off the mountain before dark.

schedule.label: Arrive Virgin Lake (~1.5 hrs in)
schedule.detail: Good maintained trail up switchbacks to this point; from here travel slows a lot.

schedule.label: Drop to Blanca Lake, round it, reach base of Columbia Glacier
schedule.detail: Faint climbers' trail, route-finding required; bring microspikes and ice axe for the glacier/snow.

schedule.label: Top out on Kyes Ridge (~6,400 ft)
schedule.detail: Connect to the standard south ridge; loose, ledgy Class 3 terrain to the summit block.

schedule.label: Summit (7,282 ft)
schedule.detail: Extremely chossy, exposed summit block — move carefully and watch for loose rock on others below.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Reverse the route down; roughly 3 hrs from summit back to the lake and out.

days.objective: Summit Kyes Peak (7,282 ft) via Blanca Lake, Virgin Lake and the Columbia Glacier/South Ridge

itinerary.totalNote: A long single-day car-to-car outing: roughly 9-12 hours, ~12 miles round trip, ~6,000 ft gain — most parties do not camp.

itinerary.cal: Easy Pass Trail is typically snow-free by mid-to-late July; Highway 20 access is seasonal (mid-April to mid-November) and an NPS backcountry permit is required for the Fisher Basin camp.

days.note: Hike the Easy Pass Trail to Easy Pass (~6,600 ft), then descend the trail into Fisher Basin and down the Fisher Creek valley, cross the creek on a log and bushwhack up the east side of Douglas Creek through dense slide alder to a creekside camp (~4,700-4,800 ft) in the upper basin below the Douglas Glacier. Expect blowdown, creek crossings, and possible whiteout conditions near the pass.
days.title: Approach to Fisher Basin camp
days.objective: Reach camp below the Douglas Glacier

days.note: Alpine start as early as 5:30 AM: crampon up the gorged cirque above camp, climb the route's crux — a steep, exposed ~300-ft rock ramp (4th to low-5th class, hard to protect) through a cliff band — to reach the low-angle lower Douglas Glacier, switchback up to ~8,200 ft, then boot-pack the final ~1,000 ft with ice axe and crampons to the summit before reversing the roughly 6,000 ft back to camp.
days.title: Douglas Glacier summit push

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Crampons on for the firm morning snow in the cirque.

schedule.label: Crux rock ramp
schedule.detail: ~300 ft, 4th to low-5th class, hard to protect.

schedule.label: Ascend lower Douglas Glacier
schedule.detail: Switchbacking on low-angle glacier to ~8,200 ft.

schedule.label: Boot-pack last 1,000 ft
schedule.detail: Ice axe and crampons to the summit.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: ~6,000 ft of descent retracing the route.

days.objective: Climb the crux rock ramp and Douglas Glacier to the summit

days.note: Climb back out of Fisher Basin over Easy Pass and descend to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Easy Pass Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, ~28-mile round trip via Easy Pass and Fisher Basin; the crux is a committing, hard-to-protect rock ramp partway up the route on a long (11+ hr) summit day. This is one of Logan's harder standard routes, and parties do turn back at the crux in bad weather or high melt-out.

road.name: North Cascades Highway (SR 20) / Easy Pass Trailhead
road.status: Seasonal - closed in winter
road.driveNote: The Easy Pass Trailhead sits directly off SR 20 (~milepost 151, elev. ~3,700 ft); this route does not use the Colonial Creek/Thunder Creek trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: SR 20 closed in winter

itinerary.cal: Cascade River Road usually doesn't open until late May/June depending on snowpack, and the Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier zone is a high-occupancy North Cascades NP backcountry zone requiring an advance wilderness permit reservation.

days.note: Cross the Cascade River, then climb steep forest and boulder-field trail up Eldorado Creek/Roush Creek basin onto the Eldorado Glacier. Camp on the glacier or moraine, typically 5,600-7,500 ft depending on season and snowline.
days.title: Approach to glacier high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp on the Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier

days.note: Pre-dawn alpine start across the Inspiration Glacier to the base of the East Ridge, then up the exposed, knife-edged summit snow arête to the top. Reverse the same line back to camp.
days.title: Summit day via Inspiration Glacier

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Pre-dawn alpine start.

schedule.label: Onto Inspiration Glacier
schedule.detail: Rope up for glacier travel.

schedule.label: Base of summit ridge
schedule.detail: Start of the knife-edge snow arête.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: 8,872 ft, exposed knife-edge finish.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the glacier and ridge.

days.objective: Reach the 8,872 ft summit via the Inspiration Glacier and knife-edge ridge

days.note: Break camp and descend back across the Cascade River to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Break camp and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: The classic 3-day Eldorado itinerary: hike to a glacier high camp, a pre-dawn summit day across the Inspiration Glacier and knife-edge ridge to 8,872 ft, then hike out (~6,700 ft gain, ~10 mi round trip); strong parties sometimes compress this to 2 days, and very fit teams have done it car-to-car in an 11-21 hr single push.

itinerary.cal: Cascade River Road typically opens in late spring and Cache Col holds consolidated snow well into summer, so most parties do this in July-September when the col crossing is firm but not icy.

days.note: Hike the maintained Cascade Pass Trail to Cascade Pass, then leave the trail and climb cross-country over the Cache Glacier remnant to Cache Col before dropping about a mile to camp at Kool-Aid Lake, a small tarn at ~6,120 ft. This stretch is mostly on snow into midsummer and is the crux of the day more from routefinding/snow travel than distance.
days.title: Approach to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Reach high camp at Kool-Aid Lake

days.note: An early start lets you climb the peak on firm snow before it softens: cross the steep snow band near 7,100 ft and take a gully up to the summit ridge, then follow the ridge past a false summit to the true 7,821 ft top. Back at camp by mid-morning, most parties break camp and hike all the way out the same day rather than adding a third night.
days.title: Climb Hurry-Up Peak, then hike out

schedule.label: Leave Kool-Aid Lake camp
schedule.detail: Early start for firm snow on the col approach.

schedule.label: Reach the summit ridge
schedule.detail: Across the snow band near 7,100 ft and up a gully.

schedule.label: Summit along the ridge
schedule.detail: Scramble past a false summit to the true 7,821 ft top.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Break camp, filter water, repack for the hike out.

schedule.label: Begin the hike out
schedule.detail: Re-cross Cache Col and descend past Cascade Pass.

schedule.label: Back at the trailhead
schedule.detail: Roughly 3,000 ft of net descent from camp to the car.

days.objective: Tag the summit via the South Ridge and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, 1-night trip: about 16 miles round trip with roughly 5,500 ft of total gain, mostly spent covering the Cascade Pass-Cache Col approach rather than the short summit scramble itself.

itinerary.cal: Olympic NP requires a wilderness camping permit (reserved in advance; Low Divide and Seattle Basin are not quota areas); the North Fork Quinault Road has a history of washout closures, so check NPS road status before driving in.

days.note: An afternoon-start hike up the North Fork Quinault River trail through old-growth forest to the first night's camp. Easy grade, mostly flat river-valley walking.
days.title: Hike in to Francis/Elip Creek Camp
days.objective: Reach Francis/Elip Creek Camp

days.note: The longest day of the approach: steady climbing up the North Fork Quinault valley to Low Divide, including a mandatory ford of the river. Parties note a long lunch/swim break at the ford and afternoon heat as the main slow-down factors.
days.title: Push up-valley to Low Divide
days.objective: Reach Low Divide Camp

days.note: A shorter, deliberately easy day to arrive at basecamp with time to rest before the summit push. Trail switchbacks into Seattle Meadows, then cross-country through heather meadows to a gravelly camp rib as high in the basin as possible.
days.title: Climb to Seattle Basin high camp
days.objective: Establish basecamp in Seattle Basin (~4,900 ft)

days.note: The technical crux day: an early start, a scree traverse to the Noyes-Meany col, and a short low Class 5 roped pitch with loose rock but good gear on the final push to the summit. Two rappels and a long scree/talus descent bring the party back to camp after dark.
days.title: Summit day

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Light alpine-start pack; rope and rack carried, camp gear cached.

schedule.label: Reach the Noyes-Meany col
schedule.detail: Ridge saddle gained via scree slopes above camp.

schedule.label: Traverse scree to the Meany ridge
schedule.detail: Loose, exposed cross-country traverse — the slowest non-technical section.

schedule.label: Lead the roped pitch
schedule.detail: Low Class 5.2 rock, loose but with good gear placements; one pitch.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: ~5.6 hrs camp-to-summit.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Two rappels off the summit block plus the long scree descent make for a ~14.5-hr round trip.

days.objective: Climb Mount Meany via the Noyes-Meany col and NE face, return to camp

days.note: A relaxed, later-starting day after the long summit push — sleep in, then descend back through Low Divide toward Sixteenmile Camp with leisurely stream-crossing breaks.
days.title: Descend toward Sixteenmile Camp
days.objective: Reach Sixteenmile Camp

days.note: A long final day retracing the valley trail back to the car, often in showery weather; the biggest mileage day of the trip but on easy, well-graded tread.
days.title: Hike out to trailhead
days.objective: Return to the North Fork Quinault trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 6-day, ~42-mile round-trip backpack (roughly 9,300 ft of cumulative gain and loss) via the North Fork Quinault River and Seattle Basin, with a single long, technical summit day involving a low-5th-class pitch and two rappels.

road.name: North Fork Quinault Road (via North Shore Road)
road.status: Open; the final 4 miles are gravel, narrow and winding, and are not recommended for RVs or trailers.
road.driveNote: From US-101 at Lake Quinault take North Shore Road about 14 miles to the North/South Shore intersection, then North Fork Quinault Road about 4 miles to the trailhead and ranger station. North Shore is the only way in: South Shore Road is closed by a washout at about mile 8 from US-101, with no reopening date on Olympic National Park's alerts page updated August 27, 2026. The Elwha approach via Whiskey Bend is a genuine alternative but is foot and bike only: Olympic Hot Springs Road has been shut to vehicles beyond Madison Falls since November 2017 flood damage, adding roughly 7 miles each way.
road.seasonalGate: May close during winter storms; NPS publishes no fixed gate dates, so check current road conditions before travelling.

itinerary.cal: Only feasible once North Cascades Highway 20 opens over Washington Pass for the season (typically mid-April until a winter closure between mid-November and early December, weather dependent).

days.note: From the Wine Spires pullout on Hwy 20 (~3.7 mi east of Washington Pass), drop steeply down to and cross Early Winters Creek, then climb the well-used climber's trail through timber and talus to the Bench, an established camp at ~6,460 ft with a nearby spring. Stronger parties push on another ~1,300 ft to camp at Burgundy Col itself (~7,800 ft) to shorten summit day.
days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach the Bench camp below Burgundy Col

days.note: From camp, gain Burgundy Col and traverse north along Vasiliki Ridge on scramble terrain to the base of Ares Tower; climb the 4th-class ridge with its short low-5th-class summit step, then rappel back to the ridge. Most parties break camp and descend the full approach back to the car the same day rather than a second night out; strong parties tag The Acropolis and Niki Tower en route.
days.title: Traverse to Ares Tower and out

schedule.label: Break camp / leave the Bench
schedule.detail: Alpine start to be off the ridge before afternoon thunderstorms build.

schedule.label: Reach Burgundy Col
schedule.detail: Cache overnight gear here if camped lower at the Bench.

schedule.label: Reach base of Ares Tower
schedule.detail: Ridge traverse over/around intermediate towers (Acropolis, Niki Tower) on 3rd-4th class terrain.

schedule.label: Summit Ares Tower
schedule.detail: Short low-5th-class step guards the final summit block.

schedule.label: Rappel back to the ridge
schedule.detail: Single-rope rappel off fixed/new anchors reported by recent parties.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Full reversal of the approach, re-crossing Early Winters Creek.

days.objective: Climb Ares Tower via the ridge traverse, then hike all the way out to the car

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip: ~7 mi and ~5,800 ft one-way to the summit, with an established high camp at the Bench (or Burgundy Col) and a long car-to-car summit/exit day.

road.name: State Route 20 / North Cascades Highway
road.status: Seasonal — closed to vehicles in winter
road.driveNote: Unsigned roadside pullout ~3.7 miles east of Washington Pass on SR-20, about 0.7 mile past the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff, with room for roughly a handful of cars. Don't confuse it with the paved, fee-required Blue Lake Trailhead lot a short drive away.
road.seasonalGate: Gated near Diablo Lake to the west and Early Winters to the east each winter; typical reopening is mid-to-late April, but has been delayed into June in heavy-snow or storm-damage years (2026 reopened June 14).

itinerary.cal: Highway 20 (North Cascades Hwy) typically opens in May; the SW gully/talus can still hold snow into July, so most parties go July-September for driest, safest rock.

days.note: An easy, scenic backpack almost entirely on the Pacific Crest Trail from Rainy Pass, over Cutthroat Pass and Granite Pass, then a short side trip up into the Snowy Lakes basin to camp. Trail is well graded and mostly moderate grade; multiple trip reports clock this leg at roughly 5-6 hours with overnight packs.
days.title: Backpack in to Snowy Lakes camp

schedule.label: Leave Rainy Pass trailhead
schedule.detail: PCT north; some parties start midday after driving up from Seattle.

schedule.label: Cutthroat Pass / Granite Pass
schedule.detail: First views of Tower Mountain and Golden Horn from the pass.

schedule.label: Arrive Snowy Lakes, make camp
schedule.detail: Upper Snowy Lake is preferred for views; Lower Snowy Lake camps are also common and closer to the Tower climber's path.

days.objective: Establish camp at Upper or Lower Snowy Lake

days.note: Leave camp with a light day pack for the summit push: cross talus below the west face (can hold snow early season), pass the large cave feature on the climber's path, then work up the loose class 3 gully with a short class 4 slab/exposed step near the top. After returning to camp, break it down and reverse the PCT back to the car — a long but standard single push for fit parties; some groups instead split this into two separate days if they want a more relaxed pace.
days.title: Climb Tower Mountain, then hike out

schedule.label: Leave camp for Tower Mountain
schedule.detail: Day pack, helmet on for the gully — rockfall is a real hazard, especially with parties above.

schedule.label: Reach the cave and gully entrance
schedule.detail: Notable ~25-yard-deep cave along the climber's path is a common landmark/rest stop.

schedule.label: Summit Tower Mountain
schedule.detail: Final moves are class 3-4 over blocks and a short chimney; loose rock throughout the gully.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Break down tent and reload overnight pack.

schedule.label: Depart camp, hike out via PCT
schedule.detail: Reverse Granite Pass / Cutthroat Pass route back to Rainy Pass.

schedule.label: Arrive trailhead
schedule.detail: Some parties use a steeper Swamp Creek bushwhack shortcut to cut this leg short, at the cost of off-trail travel.

days.objective: Summit via the SW gully system and pack out to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, ~23-mile round trip with ~4,200 ft total gain: an easy PCT backpack in to Snowy Lakes camp, then a long summit-and-hike-out day on Tower's loose SW gully. Strong parties sometimes push the whole thing car-to-car in one very long day instead.

itinerary.cal: Best late July through September once high-elevation snow has melted enough for the off-trail ridge sections; requires an Olympic NP wilderness permit (quota + required bear canister) booked by phone with the Wilderness Information Center for the cross-country zones, and the Elwha River Trail exit can be affected by seasonal washouts or a Dodger Point closure that forces a longer alternate route.

days.note: Well-graded trail from the Sol Duc trailhead up through Deer Lake and along High Divide to a camp near Cat Basin, staged at the start of the off-trail traverse. Last easy water and maintained tread of the trip.
days.title: Sol Duc to High Divide / Cat Basin
days.objective: Reach the base of the Bailey Range crest

days.note: Off-trail route-finding begins here: the exposed 'Catwalk' traverse between Cat Peak and Mount Carrie, then sidehilling brushy meadows and gullies down to a beach camp on Stephen Lake.
days.title: The Catwalk to Stephen Lake
days.objective: Cross the Catwalk and flank Mount Carrie

days.note: Climb out of the Stephen Lake basin and traverse post-glacial moraine and meadow terrain to camp in Upper Ferry Basin, with Stephen Peak an optional short side-scramble along the way.
days.title: Stephen Lake to Ferry Basin
days.objective: Push south along the Bailey Range crest

days.note: Loose scree and talus lead over a shoulder near Mount Ferry into what parties often nickname 'Junkyard Basin,' then down to a grassy meadow camp near Bear Pass — the staging point for the Barnes side-trip.
days.title: Ferry Basin to a high camp near Bear Pass
days.objective: Reach the meadow camp below Mount Barnes

days.note: Stash overnight gear in the meadow and go light. Scree and lingering snow patches lead southwest of the peak, then a moderate scree slope and a boot track curl left through brief brush to the summit, with big views of Olympus, Queets, Noyes, and Seattle — often shared with swarms of flying ants in late summer.
days.title: Side-trip: climb Mount Barnes

schedule.label: Leave camp, stash overnight gear
schedule.detail: Cache tents/sleeping gear in the meadow southeast of Barnes and continue with a light daypack.

schedule.label: Scree and snow patches to southwest of peak
schedule.detail: Mixed scree and residual snow, no technical difficulty in late summer.

schedule.label: Boot-track ridge, brief bushwhacking
schedule.detail: Moderate scree slope, then a visible boot track curling left through short brushy sections.

schedule.label: Summit Mount Barnes
schedule.detail: 360-degree views; parties sometimes continue toward Mount Queets from here if conditions and time allow.

schedule.label: Retrace route to gear stash and camp
schedule.detail: Same line in reverse back to the meadow cache.

days.objective: Tag the Mount Barnes summit and return to camp

days.note: A long, punishing grind: down the largely melted-out Elwha Snowfinger gully (steep scree, slabs and an icy snow hump) into the tangled brush and stream crossings of the Elwha Basin ('the maze') to Chicago Camp, then a fast, well-graded push down the Elwha River Trail to the Whiskey Bend trailhead near Madison Falls. Tired parties often split this into two days at Hayes River instead; if the southern trail is fire-closed, exit via Dodger Point, which adds mileage and elevation change.
days.title: Descend the Elwha Snowfinger and out to Whiskey Bend
days.objective: Exit via the Elwha Basin maze and Elwha River Trail

itinerary.totalNote: A 6-day, roughly 55-mile off-trail Bailey Range traverse with 17,000+ ft of cumulative gain; Mount Barnes itself is only a half-day out-and-back scramble tacked onto a high camp near Bear Pass, usually paired with (or offered as an alternative to) Mount Queets, and the trip finishes with a very long exit day down the Elwha.

access.fees: Olympic Wilderness camping: $6 reservation fee plus $8/person/night for ages 16+ (15 and under free), in addition to the standard Olympic NP entrance fee/pass for vehicle access.
access.notes: No separate climbing cost-recovery fee like Mount Rainier’s $82 — only the standard entrance fee and wilderness camping permit apply.
access.rules: Bear-resistant food canisters are required for all overnight stays anywhere in the Olympic Wilderness, including cross-country zones. Rangers will not deny a permit based on a party's stated skill or gear, so honest self-assessment of the off-trail difficulty is essential.
access.permit: Wilderness camping permit required year-round for all overnight stays, reserved through Recreation.gov — but the Elwha Basin/Bailey Range cross-country camping zones are call-in only and must be booked by phone with the Wilderness Information Center, (360) 565-3100, rather than the standard online quota system.
access.closures: The Olympic Hot Springs Road (drive to Whiskey Bend Trailhead) is washed out and closed to vehicles beyond Madison Falls, with no reopening date; it is open to walkers and bikes. The Bailey Range Traverse beyond Cat Basin (which includes the approach to Barnes) was closed during the August 2023 Olympic lightning fires and can be re-closed in future high fire-danger periods; check current fire/trail conditions with the WIC.
access.land_manager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
access.parking_pass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.

overnight_permit.what: Olympic National Park wilderness camping permit, reserved in advance with a nightly per-person fee
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov or by phone with the Wilderness Information Center, and print it from your account; no same-day walk-up sites are held, and Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin and the East Fork Quinault are quota areas.

itinerary.cal: North Cascades Highway (SR-20) over Washington Pass usually opens in April or May and closes with heavy snow, typically between mid-November and early December — prime dry-rock season is June-September.

days.note: Hike the Blue Lake trail to the Y-shaped larch at the base of the Southwest Rib. Climb the rib's first three pitches, go left at the ledge where the two roofs come into view, and climb the three Boving Roofs pitches (5.2, the 5.10b roofs, 5.9) to the top of the rib's Bear Hug pitch. Finish up the rib's last two pitches to the summit — 8 pitches in all — then downclimb part of the South Arete and make 3 rappels to its foot.
days.title: Car-to-car climb

schedule.label: Leave Blue Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: Popular wall — an early start beats other Southwest Rib parties to the base.

schedule.label: Reach the Y-shaped larch
schedule.detail: About 1–1.5 hr of steady uphill approach.

schedule.label: Southwest Rib pitches 1–3
schedule.detail: 5.8+, 5.8, 5.6 to the ledge below the roofs.

schedule.label: Boving Roofs pitches
schedule.detail: Left at the ledge: 5.2, the 5.10b roofs, then 5.9 to the top of the Bear Hug.

schedule.label: Southwest Rib pitches 6–7 to the summit
Descend the South Arete
schedule.detail: Downclimbing, then 3 rappels to the foot of the South Arete; walk back to the larch for anything left there.

days.objective: Climb Boving Roofs to the summit and return to the Blue Lake trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: Plan on at least the full Southwest Rib's day, about 9.5 hr car-to-car: this line climbs 8 pitches to the rib's 7, three of them harder. No published time exists for the variation itself.

itinerary.cal: Ruth Mountain's summit and the Ruth-Icy col lie inside North Cascades National Park, so an overnight wilderness permit (pick up at the Glacier ranger station) is required for the camp; FR 32 to Hannegan Trailhead is typically snow-free and open by mid-to-late June.

days.note: An easy, well-graded trail to Hannegan Pass gives way to a steeper, looser climbers' path up Ruth Arm and a short root/rock gully with scramble moves, then snow/glacier travel up the Ruth Glacier to a flat camp at the notch. Most parties take 5-6 hours with overnight packs and set up before evening.
days.title: Approach to Ruth Glacier notch camp

schedule.label: Leave Hannegan Trailhead
schedule.detail: 3,100 ft; FR 32 road end near Hannegan Campground.

schedule.label: Reach Hannegan Pass
schedule.detail: 5,066 ft, ~4 mi of mellow forest trail with a few easy creek crossings.

schedule.label: Climb the Ruth Arm gully
schedule.detail: Loose rock-and-root gully with a few scramble moves gaining the ridge toward Ruth.

schedule.label: Arrive at Ruth Glacier notch camp
schedule.detail: ~6,600 ft; set up tents and rope up gear for tomorrow's early start.

days.objective: Establish camp at the Ruth Glacier notch (~6,600 ft)

days.note: Drop from camp to the Ruth-Icy saddle, cross the Icy Glacier to the notch below Icy's Northwest Spire, then scramble to the base of the summit gully and climb the 100-ft Class 4 gully to the top. After returning to camp (roughly 8-9 hours round trip), break down camp and hike the full way back out to the trailhead the same day — a long but standard finish to the trip.
days.title: Icy Peak summit push and hike out

schedule.label: Leave camp for Icy Peak
schedule.detail: Descend the loose boot path toward the Ruth-Icy saddle in the dark/early light.

schedule.label: Cross the Ruth-Icy saddle
schedule.detail: ~5,700 ft; about a 900-ft drop from camp, roughly an hour.

schedule.label: Reach the notch below Icy's NW Spire
schedule.detail: ~6,500 ft via talus/slabs and roped Icy Glacier travel; watch the one known crack near the boot path.

schedule.label: Summit Icy Peak
schedule.detail: Northwest summit via ~500 ft of 2nd-3rd class then the 100-ft Class 4 summit gully; the true Southeast summit (7,073 ft) takes more 3rd-4th class scrambling. Helmets on for rockfall.

schedule.label: Back at camp, break it down
schedule.detail: Reverse gully/glacier/saddle (~4-5 hr back from the summit), rappel or downclimb the summit gully off the rock horn anchor, then pack up camp.

schedule.label: Out at Hannegan Trailhead
schedule.detail: Reverse the Ruth Arm gully and Hannegan Pass trail, ~4-5 hr descent with full packs.

days.objective: Climb Icy Peak via the Ruth-Icy col and Icy Glacier, then break camp and hike all the way out

itinerary.totalNote: A classic 2-day, 1-night trip: ~5-6 hrs up to the Ruth Glacier notch camp on day one, then a long ~12-13 hr day two that combines the Icy Peak summit push (Ruth-Icy saddle, Icy Glacier, 100-ft Class 4 summit gully) with breaking camp and hiking all the way out; very strong parties occasionally link it car-to-car in one long (15-20 hr) day instead.

road.name: Ruth Creek Road (FR 32 spur, signed off Hannegan Pass Road)
road.status: Gravel, generally passenger-car passable in season to the road-end Hannegan Trailhead/Campground (~3,100 ft)
road.driveNote: From SR 542 (Mt. Baker Hwy), turn onto FR 32 about 13 mi east of Glacier; bear left onto Ruth Creek Road at 1.3 mi and continue 5.3-5.4 mi to road's end.
road.seasonalGate: Not gated, but the upper road and Hannegan Pass Trail can remain snow-covered into June after a normal-to-heavy winter; check Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF current-conditions/alerts before an early-season attempt.

itinerary.cal: Harts Pass Road (WA-20 to FR-5400) and the Pasayten's cross-country basins often aren't fully snow-free and easy to travel until late June/early July; Eureka Creek crossings can be difficult during peak snowmelt.

days.note: From the Harts Pass/Slate Pass trailhead, cross Slate Pass and descend into the Middle Fork Pasayten drainage, then climb back up to Fred's Lake for the first camp. Full wilderness packs with 4 days of food.
days.title: Hike in to Fred's Lake
days.objective: Reach Fred's Lake camp

days.note: Climb over Fred's/Rolo Pass on the ridge above Fred's Lake, then drop to Eureka Creek and back up into scenic Shellrock Basin, directly below the Carru-Lago-Osceola cirque. A shorter day than Day 1, leaving the afternoon free to scout the route.
days.title: Cross to Shellrock Basin high camp
days.objective: Establish high camp in Shellrock Basin

days.note: Leave camp with light daypacks and climb toward the Lago-Carru saddle, then follow the obvious southeast slope/ridge line - mostly class 2 talus and scree with brief exposed sections - to the summit. Many parties tack on Osceola and/or Lago from the same camp, but a Carru-only push is a shorter, half-day round trip.
days.title: Summit day: Mount Carru

schedule.label: Leave Shellrock Basin camp
schedule.detail: Light daypack; head toward the Lago-Carru saddle.

schedule.label: Reach Lago-Carru col (~7,600 ft)
schedule.detail: Transition onto Carru's southeast slope.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Class 2 scree/talus scramble; views across the Pasayten crest.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the southeast slope line back to the col.

schedule.label: Back at Shellrock Basin camp
schedule.detail: Rest of the day free; some parties extend to Osceola or Lago instead.

days.objective: Climb Carru's southeast slopes and return to camp

days.note: Reverse Days 1 and 2 in a single long push: back over Rolo/Fred's Pass, down through the Middle Fork Pasayten drainage, and over Slate Pass to the trailhead. A full day with full packs.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Harts Pass/Slate Pass trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 4-day Pasayten backpack: ~29-30 miles round trip and roughly 7,500-8,000 ft of cumulative gain, with one long summit day tagging Carru's southeast slopes from a high camp in Shellrock Basin.

itinerary.cal: Lake Constance camping needs an Olympic NP wilderness permit (limited nightly quota via recreation.gov), and the Dosewallips Road washout adds a multi-mile bike/walk before the trailhead each way.

days.note: Bike or walk the washed-out Dosewallips road, then climb the steep 2-mile Lake Constance Trail (~3,300 ft gain) to camp on the north side of the lake.
days.title: Approach to Lake Constance camp
days.objective: Reach camp at Lake Constance

days.note: Climb Avalanche Canyon and the South Chute to the notch, cross the exposed Terrible Traverse snow/scree cirque, then finish up the 3rd-class North Chimney gully that wraps around the north side of the summit block to the true summit. Reverse the whole line back to camp.
days.title: Summit via the North Chimney

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Up Avalanche Canyon and the South Chute.

schedule.label: Reach the notch
schedule.detail: ~1,950 ft above camp.

schedule.label: Cross the Terrible Traverse
schedule.detail: Exposed snow/scree cirque above a large cliff.

schedule.label: Climb the North Chimney
schedule.detail: 3rd-class gully around the north side of the summit block.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: After reversing the full line.

days.objective: Tag the summit via the standard South Chute / North Chimney line

days.note: Reverse the Lake Constance Trail and road walk/bike back to the cars.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Break camp and exit to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, 2-night trip is standard: hike in, a long (~12 hr) summit day via the South Chute and North Chimney, hike out.

itinerary.cal: Whatcom Camp, the trail camp just below Whatcom Pass, and Graybeal Camp on Brush Creek are closed until further notice because of fire-damaged hazard trees, so the Whatcom Pass base camp in this plan needs a different permitted site; every overnight inside North Cascades NP requires a wilderness permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

days.note: From the Hannegan Trailhead, cross Hannegan Pass, drop about 2,500 ft to the Chilliwack River drainage, and climb the Brush Creek Trail to camp at Whatcom Pass. Start early (by 6-7 AM) — a party that left near noon didn't reach camp until 9 PM.
days.title: Trailhead to Whatcom Pass camp

schedule.label: Down to the Chilliwack drainage, pick up Brush Creek Trail
Arrive Whatcom Pass camp
schedule.detail: Camp near the pass (~5,200 ft), with views of Whatcom Peak and Challenger Glacier.

days.objective: Establish base camp at Whatcom Pass

days.note: Head south from camp toward the ridge and scramble the loose, exposed 3rd-class North Ridge to the summit. Some parties find it a quick, fun scramble; others describe it as loose and committing — go early, move carefully on the choss, and give yourself more time than the published description suggests.
days.title: North Ridge summit day

schedule.label: Leave Whatcom Pass camp
schedule.detail: Head south toward the base of the ridge.

schedule.label: Gain the North Ridge crest, begin 3rd-class scrambling
schedule.detail: Loose rock; route-finding is the crux for most parties.

schedule.label: Reverse the ridge back to camp
schedule.detail: Described by one party as 'a chossy nightmare' to downclimb — take care.

days.objective: Climb the North Ridge to the summit and back

days.note: Reverse the approach: down Brush Creek to the Chilliwack, back up to Hannegan Pass, and out to the trailhead. A leisurely exit day took one party 7.5 hours with breaks.
days.title: Out to the trailhead
days.objective: Hike out via Whatcom Pass and Hannegan Pass

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day/2-night out-and-back via a Whatcom Pass base camp: roughly 36 mi round trip (the approach alone runs close to 16 miles each way) with about 7,500-8,000 ft of cumulative gain. The ridge climb itself is short (a few hours round trip from camp) but trip reports disagree sharply on how easy it is, so budget generously.

access.fees: $10 per person plus a $6 nonrefundable reservation fee during the summer fee season (mid-May through early October); no charge the rest of the year. No fee for youth 15 and under.
access.rules: Mandatory moratorium on new fixed anchors within North Cascades NP backcountry (no new drilled bolts/hangers) — use removable/clean protection.
access.permit: Backcountry/wilderness permit required year-round for any overnight stay. Reserve in advance on Recreation.gov (60% of permits) or get a walk-up permit (40% held) at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount or the Glacier Public Service Center for northern trailheads.
access.closures: Hannegan Pass Road (FR 32) has had storm-damage sections in recent years limiting vehicle access near the trailhead — verify current status with the Mt. Baker Ranger District/Glacier Public Service Center before driving out.
access.landManager: North Cascades National Park Service Complex (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
access.land_manager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass at the Hannegan Pass trailhead

overnight_permit.what: North Cascades NP backcountry permit (cross-country zone), fee per person, not free
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov, or get a walk-up permit in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center. Hannegan-side permits can also be picked up at the Glacier Public Service Center on its limited summer days.

itinerary.cal: The upper Mt Baker Highway to Austin Pass typically doesn't open until late June or early July, depending on snowpack, and the trailhead has had weekend-focused access in recent seasons -- check current Forest Service alerts before planning a start time.

days.note: A single, full-day out-and-back: hike the Lake Ann Trail from Austin Pass up to the 4,900 ft saddle above Lake Ann, then scramble over Mount Annette's south ridge and west along the connecting ridge to the Mount Ann summit, and reverse the whole route to descend. No camping is required or typically used.
days.title: Car-to-car scramble to the summit

schedule.label: Leave Austin Pass trailhead
schedule.detail: Standard early start to beat afternoon weather and have a buffer for the ridge's ups and downs.

schedule.label: Reach the saddle above Lake Ann (~4,900 ft)
schedule.detail: Trail hiking on Lake Ann Trail No. 600: drop about 800 ft into the Swift Creek basin, then climb about 1,000 ft to the saddle, roughly 4 miles in all.

schedule.label: Ridge scramble to Mount Ann summit
schedule.detail: Off-trail scrambling along the connecting ridge past Mount Annette's south ridge (~5,500 ft); more undulating terrain than the map suggests, with some exposure.

schedule.label: Summit Mount Ann (5,873 ft)
schedule.detail: Views of Mount Shuksan's Curtis Glaciers; typical turnaround point.

schedule.label: Descend to trailhead
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge scramble and boot path to the saddle, then the Lake Ann Trail back to the car.

days.objective: Reach the Mount Ann summit via the Lake Ann Trail and south ridge scramble

itinerary.totalNote: A standard single-day car-to-car scramble: about 7-9 hours round trip for 10.5 miles and 4,000 ft of gain/loss, with no overnight camp.

road.name: Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) to the Austin Pass / Artist Point trailhead
road.status: paved to the trailhead
road.driveNote: Trailhead is the large paved Lake Ann/Austin Pass parking lot just before Artist Point, about 58 miles / 1.5-2 hr from Bellingham on SR 542; the lot is one of the most popular on the highway and fills early on summer weekends.
road.seasonalGate: Final stretch above the ski area is gated in winter; typically opens late June or early July and closes by mid-October (opened June 10, 2026)

itinerary.cal: Suiattle River Road is frequently washed out or gated well short of the Downey Creek trailhead, adding miles of biking/walking each way not reflected in trail mileage; the SW route is normally in condition July-September once Cub Lake Pass snowfields consolidate (May-June trips are more ski-mountaineering oriented with heavier snow coverage).

days.note: Hike the mostly gentle Downey Creek Trail to Sixmile Camp, then continue up the abandoned, brushy Bachelor Creek Trail to a flat camp near 4,500 ft. Expect slide-alder bushwhacking and a footlog crossing of Bachelor Creek; parties report this day taking most of a full day with full packs.
days.title: Approach to Bachelor Creek
days.objective: Reach forest camp near the Bachelor Creek crossing (Sixmile Camp / Bachelor Flats)

days.note: Climb steep forest and meadow above Bachelor Flats, cross the snow slopes of Cub Lake Pass (~5,700 ft), and drop to Cub Lake or climb onto Itswoot Ridge to camp with views of the Dome/Chickamin Glacier. This is normally the crux navigation day if snow-covered.
days.title: Over Cub Lake Pass to high camp
days.objective: Establish high camp on Itswoot Ridge or in the Cub Lake basin

days.note: An alpine-start glacier day: rope up and cross the Chickamin Glacier to the Dome-Sinister col, then climb the loose southwest gully and scramble the upper west ridge (Class 2-3) to the summit. Reverse the same line back to camp; parties reach the summit anywhere from late morning to early afternoon depending on party speed and whether Dome Peak is tagged the same day.
days.title: Climb Sinister Peak

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Rope up for glacier travel while crossing toward the Dome/Chickamin basin.

schedule.label: Cross the Chickamin Glacier
schedule.detail: Rising traverse with crevasse detours toward the Dome-Sinister col.

schedule.label: Reach the Dome-Sinister col
schedule.detail: ~7,640 ft; begin the southwest gully, reported as loose and unpleasant.

schedule.label: Top out on the upper west ridge
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 scrambling toward the summit block.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: 8,444 ft; roomy summit, views of Dome Peak and the Ptarmigan Traverse.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the gully and glacier crossing.

days.objective: Summit via the Southwest Route and return to high camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse the full approach in one long push: back over Cub Lake Pass, down Bachelor Creek, and out the Downey Creek Trail. Most parties treat this as a single long descent day rather than splitting it again.
days.title: Hike out to trailhead
days.objective: Descend from high camp to the Downey Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day trip: ~33-35 miles and roughly 8,000-9,000 ft cumulative gain round trip, with one long alpine summit day off a high camp near Cub Lake/Itswoot Ridge.

itinerary.cal: Cascade River Road's June 2026 washout gate well below the Cascade Pass Trailhead has been lifted, and the park's road-conditions page, updated July 3, 2026, lists the road open — check nps.gov/noca road conditions again before you go, and pick up your Sahale Glacier/Horseshoe Basin camping permit at the Marblemount Ranger Station since sites can fill on summer weekends.

days.note: From the Cascade Pass Trailhead, climb switchbacks to Cascade Pass (5,400 ft, 3.7 mi) then continue up the Sahale Arm Trail to the permitted Sahale Glacier Camp at 7,600 ft. Most parties treat this as a half-day carry so they're fresh for an early alpine start the next morning.
days.title: Approach to Sahale Glacier Camp
days.objective: Reach Sahale Glacier Camp (7,600 ft) as base for the Horseshoe/Buckner traverse

days.note: Alpine start down off Sahale Arm into Horseshoe Basin, crossing snow/talus past old Davenport Mine relics to the base of Horseshoe's summit block. A short, exposed 5.2 step (rope, light rack, 30-60m) gains the true summit; most parties downclimb or make one short rappel back to the ledge. After returning to camp, break it down and hike the full ~5.7 mi / 4,000 ft back down to the trailhead the same day, making for a long but standard second day.
days.title: Summit push and full exit

schedule.label: Leave Sahale Glacier Camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start to be off the summit block before afternoon weather builds.

schedule.label: Drop into Horseshoe Basin
schedule.detail: Cross snowfield/talus below the Sahale-Buckner col, using old mining remains as landmarks.

schedule.label: Reach base of Horseshoe's summit block
schedule.detail: Scramble Class 3-4 terrain up the snowfield to the final rock step.

schedule.label: Rope up for the 5.2 crux
schedule.detail: Short technical pitch to the true summit; many parties solo-belay or simul with a light rack.

schedule.label: Summit, then downclimb/rappel
schedule.detail: Reverse the crux to the ledge below, then retrace the basin traverse to camp.

schedule.label: Back at Sahale Glacier Camp
schedule.detail: Break camp and continue the ~4,000 ft, 5.7 mi descent to the trailhead, typically finishing by early evening.

days.objective: Climb Horseshoe Peak via Horseshoe Basin, then break camp and hike all the way out

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip is the norm: ~5.7 mi/4,000 ft up to Sahale Glacier Camp on Day 1, then a long ~9-10 hr, ~9 mi summit-and-exit Day 2 with a short roped 5.2 step near the top; very fit parties do climb it car-to-car in a single ~12-16 hr day instead.

itinerary.cal: Best conditions are typically mid-July through early September, once the Cascade River Road is open and the Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier snowpack has consolidated; north-facing pockets can hold firm snow into September.

days.note: From the Eldorado Creek trailhead (2,100 ft, reached via Cascade River Road and an unbridged Cascade River ford/log crossing), hike an unmaintained boot path through forest and brush, then talus and heather slopes, to camp on rock benches at or near treeline on the edge of the Eldorado Glacier. Roush Creek rib (~5,400 ft) and the Eldorado Basin benches (~5,600-6,000 ft) are the usual flat, low-impact camp spots (camping is closed within Eldorado Basin proper).
days.title: Approach to Eldorado Creek Basin
days.objective: Reach a camp near treeline on the Eldorado Glacier apron

days.note: Rope up and climb the Eldorado Glacier onto the broad Inspiration Glacier icecap, then traverse east across the Inspiration Glacier to the rock col just southwest of Klawatti Peak. Many parties detour up Eldorado's short, corniced summit ridge (Class 2, ~1 hr round trip) on the way past. Flat rock benches right at the col make an excellent, wind-sheltered high camp next to the glacier for water.
days.title: Glacier travel to Klawatti col high camp
days.objective: Establish high camp on the rock outcrop at the Klawatti col (~7,800 ft)

days.note: Leave most gear at camp and travel light. Cross the glacier below the face, then either downclimb through or make a short (~30 m) rappel to clear the bergschrund/moat, following with a short Class 4-5 rock pitch and several hundred feet of 40-55 degree snow to the summit ridge. Descend by the same line, reversing the rappel/downclimb, and return to the col camp by early-to-mid afternoon.
days.title: Klawatti Peak summit via SE Face / Klawatti Glacier

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start for firm snow and to be off the face before the sun softens it.

schedule.label: Cross to base of SE Face
schedule.detail: Rope up for the short glacier crossing below the face.

schedule.label: Clear the bergschrund
schedule.detail: Downclimb or make one ~30 m rappel/belayed pitch to get established above the schrund.

schedule.label: Climb the face
schedule.detail: Short Class 4-5 rock section into 40-55 degree snow to the summit ridge.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: 8,485 ft; views across the Inspiration/McAllister icecap to Eldorado, Forbidden, and the Pickets.

schedule.label: Descend to high camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the rappel/downclimb over the schrund and recross the glacier.

days.objective: Climb the Southeast Face to Klawatti's summit (8,485 ft) and return to high camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse the whole approach: descend the Inspiration and Eldorado Glaciers, drop off the glacier at the Roush Creek/Eldorado Basin benches, and pick your way back down through talus and forest to the trailhead. It's a long descent day; parties often push straight through rather than making a fourth camp.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Eldorado Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-4 day glacier trip out of the Eldorado Creek trailhead: roughly 14 miles round trip with about 6,900 ft of net elevation gain from trailhead to summit, most of it glacier travel between two high camps, plus one technical pitch through the SE Face's bergschrund on summit day.

itinerary.cal: Cascade River Road typically opens for the season in late May/June and the upper basin can hold snow into July, so verify current conditions before a bushwhack approach.

days.note: Start on the maintained Cascade Pass Trail, then continue past the pass toward Pelton Basin before dropping off-trail into the Trapper Lake basin. The final descent to the lake is an unmaintained fisherman's path that loses itself quickly and turns into a steep, brushy bushwhack, so budget extra time and daylight for route-finding.
days.title: Approach via Cascade Pass to Trapper Lake camp

schedule.label: Leave Cascade River Road trailhead
schedule.detail: Popular trail, ~3.7 mi and 1,800 ft to Cascade Pass.

schedule.label: Cascade Pass
schedule.detail: Continue cross-country/boot-path toward Pelton Basin.

schedule.label: Enter Pelton Basin area
schedule.detail: Leave the beaten path and start angling toward the Trapper Lake drainage.

schedule.label: Begin bushwhack descent to Trapper Lake
schedule.detail: Steep, brushy, and reportedly longer than it looks; losing and regaining the fisherman's path is common.

schedule.label: Make camp near Trapper Lake
schedule.detail: ~4,170 ft basin below the peak's south side.

days.objective: Reach a basin camp near Trapper Lake

days.note: From the lake camp, work up open slopes and heather/talus benches on the mountain's south side to the summit, then reverse the same line. This is the standard non-technical line up the peak (no pitches), but expect loose rock and possible lingering snow patches depending on season.
days.title: South Slopes summit push

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light alpine-start pack; carry an ice axe if snow lingers on the upper slopes.

schedule.label: Gain the south ridge/upper slopes
schedule.detail: Terrain steepens into looser talus and broken rock benches.

schedule.label: Summit (7,530 ft)
schedule.detail: Views across the Glacier Peak Wilderness / North Cascades NP boundary.

schedule.label: Reverse the South Slopes
schedule.detail: Downclimb the ascent line, watching for loosened rock kicked from above.

schedule.label: Back at Trapper Lake camp
schedule.detail: Rest, refill water, dry gear for the hike out.

days.objective: Climb Trapper Mountain (7,530 ft) via the South Slopes and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the bushwhack back up out of the Trapper Lake basin to the Pelton Basin area, rejoin the Cascade Pass Trail, and hike out over the pass to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Cascade River Road trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 3-day trip (~19 mi, ~6,500 ft round-trip gain) built around a genuine off-trail bushwhack to Trapper Lake — not a car-to-car outing.

itinerary.cal: Snow lingers in the summit gully into July (ice axe/microspikes useful); the Monte Cristo Road washout means most parties bike the 4-mile approach road each way rather than walk it.

days.note: This is a big single-day outing, not a backpack. The Monte Cristo Road has been washed out since the mid-2000s, so the first/last 4 miles each way (Barlow Pass to Monte Cristo townsite) are hiked or, more commonly, biked on a fat-tire/mountain bike to save time. From Monte Cristo, follow the Glacier Basin trail, then leave it to climb through forest and a snow/scree gully to the skyline notch, finishing with class 3-4 scrambling up the south face and west ridge to the 6,810' summit.
days.title: Car-to-car: Barlow Pass to the summit and back

schedule.label: Leave car at Barlow Pass
schedule.detail: Bike the washed-out Monte Cristo Road (ford or log-cross the bridge gap); ~30-45 min by bike vs 80-90 min on foot.

schedule.label: Stash bikes at Monte Cristo, start Glacier Basin trail
schedule.detail: Leave the maintained trail before Glacier Basin proper to angle up toward the south face.

schedule.label: Reach snowline / gully entrance (~5,000')
schedule.detail: Snow can be firm early season - many parties carry an ice axe/microspikes into July.

schedule.label: Through the skyline notch to the summit
schedule.detail: Class 3-4 scrambling on exposed, down-sloping ledges for the final pitch.

schedule.label: Back down to Monte Cristo townsite
schedule.detail: Reverse the south face/west ridge line carefully; early-season snow allows a glissade in the gully.

schedule.label: Bike out to Barlow Pass, car

days.objective: Tag the summit via the South Face-West Ridge and return to the car same day
