itinerary.totalNote: A long but standard single day: ~16 miles and ~4,400 ft gain car-to-car (about 9 hrs of actual climbing per real trip reports, plus the ~8 mi round-trip on the washed-out access road, commonly done by bike).

road.name: Mountain Loop Highway to Barlow Pass, then the gated Monte Cristo Road (foot/bike only beyond the gate)
road.status: Barlow Pass Trailhead itself is on paved, maintained highway; Monte Cristo Road beyond the gate is a rough, washed-out former road open to foot and mountain-bike travel only
road.driveNote: From Granite Falls, follow the Mountain Loop Highway roughly 31 paved miles east (via Verlot, ~11 mi, then ~19.4 more mi) to Barlow Pass Trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Mountain Loop Hwy from Deer Creek to Bedal (which includes Barlow Pass) closes to vehicles in winter, typically early November through mid/late May

itinerary.cal: Requires an Olympic National Park wilderness permit (cross-country nights on the ridge are arranged by phone with the Wilderness Information Center) and is only reasonable snow-free from roughly July through September; check the Elwha road and trail status before committing to dates.

days.note: Walk or ride the closed road from Madison Falls to Whiskey Bend, then follow the Elwha River Trail upstream through old-growth forest past Lillian River, Mary's Falls and Elkhorn. The camps around Hayes River make a sensible first night with a full week's food on your back.
days.title: Madison Falls and Whiskey Bend up the Elwha
days.objective: Camp in the mid-valley, around Hayes River

days.note: Continue up the valley past Camp Wilder to Chicago Camp. The Elwha ford here is the crossing to check before the trip; the main trail turns south for Low Divide, and everything beyond is on the fainter way trail or off-trail.
days.title: Up the Elwha to Chicago Camp
days.objective: Reach Chicago Camp, the last camp on the main trail

days.note: Take the way trail west up the Elwha toward Elwha Basin, past Happy Hollow camp. Beyond it, leave the path and climb north, steeply and through brush and timber, to the crest of the ridge joining Mount Barnes and Mount Wilder. Carry water for the night: the ridge has little.
days.title: Past Happy Hollow and up to the Barnes–Wilder ridge
days.objective: Camp on the ridge between Mount Barnes and Mount Wilder

days.note: With light packs, follow the crest east toward Mount Wilder and on northeast to Dana, finishing with class 2 scrambling to the summit, then return along the ridge to camp. It is a long day for its distance, and Mount Wilder can be taken in on the way back.
days.title: Along the crest to Mount Dana and back
days.objective: Summit Mount Dana (6,213 ft)

days.note: Descend the steep, brushy slope to the Elwha Basin way trail near Happy Hollow, walk back to Chicago Camp, re-ford the Elwha, and continue down the Elwha River Trail to a camp around Hayes River or Elkhorn.
days.title: Down to the valley and back down the Elwha
days.objective: Regain the trail and walk out to the mid-valley camps

days.note: An easy trail walk down the lower Elwha to Whiskey Bend, then the road walk or ride back to Madison Falls.
days.title: Out to Whiskey Bend and Madison Falls
days.objective: Return to the car

itinerary.totalNote: A six-day out-and-back up the Elwha: two days of trail walking to Chicago Camp, a steep off-trail climb from the Elwha Basin way trail to the Barnes–Wilder ridge, a day along the crest to Dana and back, and two days out.

itinerary.cal: The Elwha (Olympic Hot Springs) Road has been closed to vehicles beyond Madison Falls since November 2017 flood damage, adding roughly 7 miles of road-walking/biking each way (about 14 miles round trip) before the Whiskey Bend trailhead is even reached — check current NPS Elwha closure status before planning. Best window is July–September once the Elwha fords and upper slopes are snow-free.

days.note: Easy, well-graded river-valley trail from the Whiskey Bend trailhead through old-growth forest and the Geyser Valley area. Gentle warm-up day with a full multi-day pack.
days.title: Up the lower Elwha valley
days.objective: Reach Mary's Falls Camp

days.note: The biggest mileage day of the trip, continuing up the Elwha River Trail past Elkhorn and Hayes River toward the head of the valley. Camp Wilder sits near the base of Mount Wilder's steep south/east flank, just below Chicago Camp and Low Divide.
days.title: Long push to Camp Wilder
days.objective: Reach Camp Wilder, base camp for the peak

days.note: Leave camp with a light day pack and climb cross-country up steep heather, scree and brushy rock bands on Wilder's south/east aspect — no maintained trail, expect route-finding and Olympic-style bushwhacking low down giving way to open class 2-3 slopes near the ridge and summit.
days.title: Summit day: Mount Wilder

schedule.label: Leave Camp Wilder
schedule.detail: Light day pack, early start to beat afternoon thunderstorm risk and soften brush with morning cool.

schedule.label: Clear treeline brush, gain the ridge
schedule.detail: Steepest, densest bushwhacking is in the lower 1,500 ft; terrain opens onto heather and rock above.

schedule.label: Summit Mount Wilder
schedule.detail: 5,939 ft — views into the Bailey Range and down the Elwha and Queets drainages.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent line; downclimb loose rock bands carefully.

schedule.label: Back at Camp Wilder
schedule.detail: Rest and refill water for the hike out.

days.objective: Climb Mount Wilder and return to Camp Wilder

days.note: Reverse Day 2's route back down the Elwha River Trail. Mostly downhill/flat but long, with tired legs from the summit push the day before.
days.title: Retreat down the valley
days.objective: Return to Mary's Falls Camp

days.note: Easy final morning back down the lower valley trail to the car (or the current end-of-road walk if the Elwha Road closure is still in effect).
days.title: Out to the trailhead
days.objective: Hike out to Whiskey Bend

itinerary.totalNote: A genuine wilderness backpack, not a day trip: roughly 40 trail miles round trip up the Elwha valley to Camp Wilder plus a steep, off-trail summit scramble, typically done in 5 days by parties visiting this remote, rarely-climbed interior Olympics summit — usually as a side trip from Bailey Range/Elwha travel rather than for peak-list credit; Mount Wilder is not on Washington's Bulger List (100 highest peaks), whose lowest-ranked entries sit above 8,300 ft, far above Wilder's 5,939 ft.

itinerary.cal: Boston Basin camping requires an NPS early-access lottery permit; Cascade River Road opening date varies year to year.

days.note: Hike from the trailhead into Boston Basin and camp near 6,400 ft on the peak's east side.
days.title: Approach to Boston Basin camp
days.objective: Establish camp below the peak

days.note: A less-traveled, more remote line on Forbidden's east side; climb mixed snow and rock to gain the upper mountain and the summit, then descend the standard West Ridge notch and couloir back into Boston Basin.
days.title: Northeast Face to summit, descend West Ridge couloir
days.objective: Climb the face and descend the standard couloir

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip: camp in Boston Basin, then an estimated ~11-12 hr day up the Northeast Face and down the standard West Ridge couloir; this route sees little traffic and few published trip reports.

road.name: Cascade River Road to Boston Basin Trailhead
road.status: Open seasonally
road.driveNote: From Marblemount via Cascade River Road to the Boston Basin/climber's trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Gated/snow-covered in winter and spring

itinerary.cal: Boston Basin camping requires winning NPS's early-access permit lottery (~15% odds); Cascade River Road's opening date varies with winter road damage. This is one of the Fifty Classic Climbs of North America, so weekend permits are especially competitive.

days.note: Hike the climbers' path from the trailhead into Boston Basin and camp near 6,400 ft below the peak.
days.title: Approach to Boston Basin camp
days.objective: Establish camp in Boston Basin

days.note: Pre-dawn start up the approach couloir to the West Ridge notch, then ~6 pitches of low 5th-class ridge climbing to the true summit. Reverse the ridge to the notch and descend the couloir back to camp, hiking out the same evening or the next morning.
days.title: West Ridge to summit, descend couloir

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Pre-dawn start up the approach couloir

schedule.label: Climb the ridge
schedule.detail: ~6 pitches of low 5th class to the summit

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Hike out same evening or camp one more night

days.objective: Climb the West Ridge and return to camp

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip for most parties (hike in/camp, then an 8-10 hr technical summit day); very strong parties occasionally push it car-to-car in a single ~17.5-hr day.

itinerary.cal: Best climbed roughly June-August while the Lewis Glacier still holds enough snow for an easy crossing before it softens or thins to bare ice/rock; SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) is gated by snow in winter and typically doesn't open until spring.

days.note: From the Rainy Pass/Maple Pass trailhead, follow the Maple Pass/Heather Pass trail up to Heather Pass, then drop off-trail on snow/talus into the Lewis Lake basin. Most parties camp on a larch bench above the lake to set up for an early glacier start the next morning.
days.title: Approach to high camp above Lewis Lake
days.objective: Reach the larch-bench camp above Lewis Lake

days.note: Leave camp early to cross the Lewis Glacier while it's still firm, gain the ridge notch at about 7,500 ft, down-climb into the West Face cirque, then scramble (exposed Class 3, occasional Class 4) to the summit. Reverse the route back to camp, break camp, and hike out the same day for a long but standard single overnight trip.
days.title: Lewis Glacier, summit push, and hike out

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Cross the Lewis Glacier while the snow is still firm.

schedule.label: Reach the ridge notch (~7,500 ft)
schedule.detail: Top of the glacier approach; bear left along the ridge.

schedule.label: Down-climb ~400 ft into the West Face cirque
schedule.detail: Short exposed downclimb to gain the base of the final scramble.

schedule.label: Summit (8,107 ft)
schedule.detail: Roughly 4.3 hrs of climbing from camp, consistent with typical trip-report timing.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the route; break camp and pack up.

schedule.label: Trailhead
schedule.detail: Hike out the Heather Pass/Maple Pass trail to the car.

days.objective: Climb the Southwest Ridge to the summit, then descend and hike out to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A classic one-night trip: ~11 miles and 5,100 ft gain/loss round trip, with an easy approach afternoon followed by a long (~11 hr) summit-and-hike-out day; strong parties can also do it car-to-car in a single 10-13 hr push.

itinerary.cal: SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) typically opens for the season in mid-to-late April, but this is a high alpine route that often still holds snow into July, matching the route's 'snow/scramble' character; scree/talus conditions firm up by August-September.

days.note: From the Rainy Pass PCT-northbound trailhead, climb steadily to Cutthroat Pass, then roll over Granite Pass and down into Snowy Creek Meadow before a short side-trail climb to a camp on the rocky bench above Upper Snowy Lake. This is the long approach day; most of the trip's mileage is banked here.
days.title: Approach to Snowy Lakes camp

schedule.label: Leave Rainy Pass trailhead
schedule.detail: PCT-northbound trailhead, ~4,900 ft.

schedule.label: Reach Cutthroat Pass
schedule.detail: ~1,900 ft gained, ~6,800 ft.

schedule.label: Over Granite Pass, down to Snowy Creek Meadow
Arrive Snowy Lakes camp
schedule.detail: Rocky bench above Upper Snowy Lake, ~6,900 ft.

days.objective: Reach base camp at Upper Snowy Lake via Cutthroat & Granite Passes

days.note: Head back to Snowy Creek Meadow and up the PCT to Methow Pass, then leave the trail and traverse open terrain to the peak's east ridge. Moderate sand, scree and talus slopes lead to the summit saddle and a short final scramble to the top; reverse the same line back to camp.
days.title: Summit push via Methow Pass

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light day pack; back via Snowy Creek Meadow to the PCT.

schedule.label: Reach Methow Pass
schedule.detail: ~350 ft gained from camp.

schedule.label: Reach the summit
schedule.detail: ~1,850 ft gained off-trail via scree/talus to the east ridge and saddle.

schedule.label: Back down to Methow Pass
schedule.detail: Down-climb the scree/talus to the saddle.

schedule.label: Arrive back at camp
schedule.detail: Total round trip from camp roughly 8 hours.

days.objective: Climb Mount Hardy's southeast slope and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse Day 1's route over Granite and Cutthroat Passes back down to the highway. Downhill and familiar ground makes this noticeably faster than the approach.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Rainy Pass trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A moderate 3-day, ~24-mile round trip with about 5,100-6,000 ft of cumulative gain, based at a Snowy Lakes camp; fit parties sometimes compress the summit push and hike-out into one long Day 2, making it a 2-day trip.

road.name: SR 20 / North Cascades Highway
road.status: Open seasonally only, typically ~May-November; closed by avalanche danger the rest of the year
road.driveNote: Both the Rainy Pass PCT trailhead and the Swamp Creek pullout sit inside the winter closure zone, so the peak is inaccessible by car for roughly half the year.
road.seasonalGate: Gates at Ross Dam (MP 134) and Silver Star (MP 171) close the highway in winter; closure points can move to Newhalem (MP 120) and Early Winters (MP 178) later in the season depending on conditions.

itinerary.cal: Access is via the North Cascades Highway (SR-20), which WSDOT typically closes in winter and reopens mid-spring depending on snowpack — check road status before planning a trip.

days.note: From the trailhead, climb a steep forested trail through the larch bench and on to camp. Most parties camp at the more sheltered larch bench; pushing on to the windier Burgundy Col instead makes for a shorter summit day.
days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach camp at Burgundy Col (~7,800 ft) or the larch bench (~6,400 ft)

days.note: An early alpine start crosses the glacier while the snow is still firm; the crux of the day is the glacier-to-rock transition near the top, where a moat and class 3-4 terrain must be negotiated before a short scramble to the summit. Parties then reverse the route, re-crossing Burgundy Col and finishing with the short but steep 'Heartbreak Hill' back to the trailhead.
days.title: Summit via the Silver Star Glacier, descend to the car

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Head up the snowfield toward the start of the glacier.

schedule.label: Rope up
schedule.detail: Begin the glacier crossing on firm, consolidated snow.

schedule.label: Glacier-to-rock transition
schedule.detail: Steep snow meets a moat and class 3-4 terrain — the technical crux of the route.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Final few hundred feet of scrambling gain the top.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the route back down the glacier and up over Burgundy Col.

schedule.label: Heartbreak Hill to trailhead
schedule.detail: Final short, steep climb-and-descend before reaching the car.

days.objective: Climb the glacier to the summit, then descend all the way to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A standard 2-day trip: overnight at Burgundy Col or the larch bench, then a long summit day (roughly 10-11 hours) that finishes with a full descent to the trailhead; very fit parties can do the whole route car-to-car in one long day.

itinerary.cal: As of the last available report (Sept 2024) the Olympic Hot Springs/Whiskey Bend Road was closed indefinitely to vehicles beyond Madison Falls due to Elwha flood/washout damage, adding roughly 6-7 miles of extra biking/walking each way to reach the Whiskey Bend trailhead — check current NPS road-conditions page before planning.

days.note: Start at Whiskey Bend trailhead (or Madison Falls if the road is still washed out) and follow the Elwha River Trail south through old-growth forest and historic homestead sites. This is a long but gentle-grade trail day to bank miles before the terrain gets rougher.
days.title: Approach up the Elwha River Trail
days.objective: Reach a mid-trail camp (Elkhorn/Stony Point area)

days.note: Continue up the Elwha River Trail past Elkhorn, Hayes River, and Camp Wilder to Chicago Camp, then leave the maintained trail and work up into upper Elwha Basin (the brushy, route-finding terrain locals call "the maze"). Camp gives a shorter summit push the next day.
days.title: Push to a high camp in upper Elwha Basin
days.objective: Establish high camp near Elwha Basin / Dodwell-Rixon Pass approach

days.note: Drop the overnight gear at camp and go light. Climb cross-country up to Dodwell-Rixon Pass, then follow the ridge from the pass to the summit, bypassing a cliff band on a scree traverse, before reversing the entire route back to camp. Mostly Class 2 walking/scrambling with route-finding through brush and moraine.
days.title: Summit push via Dodwell-Rixon Pass

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Light daypack; aim to be over Dodwell-Rixon Pass by mid-morning.

schedule.label: Top of Dodwell-Rixon Pass (~4,760 ft)
schedule.detail: Views open into Queets Basin; leave the pass and start up the ridge toward the summit.

schedule.label: Scree traverse below the cliff band
schedule.detail: Where the ridge cliffs out, drop onto steep, firm scree on the east side and traverse before regaining the crest.

schedule.label: Summit (6,476 ft)
schedule.detail: Class 2 slopes to the top; short weather/photo window.

schedule.label: Back at Dodwell-Rixon Pass
schedule.detail: Begin the long descent back toward the Elwha Basin camp.

schedule.label: Return to high camp
schedule.detail: Long day — budget extra time for brush and route-finding fatigue.

days.objective: Climb the north ridge to the 6,476 ft summit and return to high camp

days.note: Break camp and descend out of Elwha Basin back to the maintained Elwha River Trail, retracing the route past Camp Wilder and Hayes River toward the Elkhorn area.
days.title: Hike back down the Elwha
days.objective: Retrace the approach toward the trailhead

days.note: Finish the descent of the Elwha River Trail back to the trailhead (plus the extra road walk/bike-out if Whiskey Bend Road is still closed to vehicles).
days.title: Exit to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to Whiskey Bend

itinerary.totalNote: A serious 5-day, ~70-mile round-trip wilderness expedition to one of the most remote summits in Washington: two long days of trail approach up the Elwha River to a high camp in upper Elwha Basin, a long cross-country summit push to Dodwell-Rixon Pass and up the ridge from the pass, then two days back out.

itinerary.cal: Suiattle River Road (FR-26) has a history of washouts short of the Downey Creek trailhead, which can add several miles of road walking/biking to the approach - check current WA DNR/USFS status before you go; no permit is required, just a self-issue wilderness pass.

days.note: From the Downey Creek trailhead (~1,450 ft), follow Downey Creek Trail then Bachelor Creek Trail (expect brush and downed trees) to Cub Lake, then continue up talus and snow to a camp on Itswoot Ridge with running water and the first full view of Dome Peak. This leg typically takes 7-9.5 hours depending on trail conditions and pace.
days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach Itswoot Ridge / Cub Lake camp (~6,200 ft)

days.note: An alpine start to cross the basin and gain the Dome Glacier while the snow is firm, then rope up for the crevassed glacier crossing on roughly a 115° bearing to the notch at 8,560 ft, finishing with a short snow slope and a 500 ft rock arête to the summit. Trip reports agree this round trip from camp typically runs 6-8 hours.
days.title: Summit day

schedule.label: Alpine start from camp
schedule.detail: Leave while overnight-refrozen snow is still firm.

schedule.label: Gain the Dome Glacier
schedule.detail: Cross talus/snow basin below Itswoot Ridge to the glacier's toe (~7,600 ft).

schedule.label: Rope up, cross the glacier
schedule.detail: Travel roped on a ~115° bearing, working around crevasses.

schedule.label: Reach the 8,560 ft notch
schedule.detail: Gain the notch just north/west of the true summit.

schedule.label: Snow slope + rock arête
schedule.detail: 300 ft of snow then a 500 ft rock arête to the summit.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Rest, refill water, prep for the hike out.

days.objective: Climb the Dome Glacier to the summit (8,926 ft)

days.note: Reverse Day 1: down off Itswoot Ridge past Cub Lake, then out Bachelor Creek and Downey Creek trails to the car. Parties commonly do this in one long push, sometimes leaving at first light if weather is moving in.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Downey Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day round trip is the norm: ~29 miles and roughly 7,900-8,400 ft of cumulative gain, with one alpine-start summit day from a high camp near Cub Lake/Itswoot Ridge (~6,200 ft); very strong parties have done the whole thing in a single 31-hour push, and some link it into a longer 4-6 day trip by continuing north on the Ptarmigan Traverse over Cache Col.

itinerary.cal: Access note: since 2021 the Alpental Community Club has closed its private roads to climbers, so parties must use the newer non-established talus approach; climb June-October (west face gets full afternoon sun, so an early start beats the heat).

days.note: From the Alpental/Snow Lake trailhead, make a rising traverse up talus to the base of the West Face, then follow diagonal ramps and a short gully system through mostly 3rd/4th class terrain with one ~30-ft low-5th-class crack/face crux near the top. Descend north past the middle and north summits toward the Cave Ridge saddle and back to the trailhead.
days.title: Car-to-car: talus approach, West Face gullies, summit

schedule.label: Leave Alpental/Snow Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: Park at the Snow Lake TH (~3,120 ft); use the non-established talus approach that avoids the private Alpental Community Club roads.

schedule.label: Reach base of talus cone / start of face
schedule.detail: Rising traverse up talus to the north side of the West Face.

schedule.label: Class 4 gully and ramp system
schedule.detail: Scramble/low-5th terrain leading toward the summit gully.

schedule.label: Crux: ~30 ft low 5th class crack/face
schedule.detail: Short technical section, then eases back to 4th class to the top.

schedule.label: Descend past the north summit toward the Cave Ridge saddle
schedule.detail: Walk off back toward the Snow Lake trailhead.

days.objective: Summit Guye Peak via the West Face

itinerary.totalNote: A single, roadside day: about 6-7 hrs car-to-car for ~2,000 ft gain, with one short low-5th-class crux near the summit.

itinerary.cal: River fords near Hardscrabble Horse Camp are safest in lower, warmer-afternoon water (July-Sept) or via an early-morning firm-snow crossing; check MBS National Forest alerts, as FS-56/Middle Fork Rd access to the Dingford Creek TH has a history of washout closures that add road-walking miles.

days.note: Drive FS-56 to the Dingford Creek/Dutch Miller Gap trailhead (check current road-closure point) and follow the Dutch Miller Gap Trail up the Middle Fork Snoqualmie valley — a gradual first 4.5 miles followed by a steeper final push — to a camp near Hardscrabble Horse Camp. Most parties camp here rather than pushing further, since the peak's approach begins with an unbridged river ford.
days.title: Approach to Hardscrabble camp
days.objective: Reach camp near Hardscrabble Horse Camp / the river ford

days.note: Ford the river, ascend boulder/gully terrain to about 5,200 ft, then follow the key snow gully up to the Point-5,841 pass — parties describe steep snow in the final 200-300 ft where an ice axe (and often crampons/microspikes) is needed, plus a bergschrund/moat near the top that sometimes requires dropping into the moat and traveling beneath the snow for a short stretch. From the pass a short class 3-4 ridge scramble and some talus lead to the summit; some parties tag Big Snow Mountain via the connecting ~5,760 ft pass as a bonus, but the standard plan returns straight to camp.
days.title: Burnt Boot Peak via the North Route

schedule.label: Break camp, ford the river
schedule.detail: Early crossing for firmer snow and lower water; estimated timing.

schedule.label: Ascend boulder field and gully to ~5,200 ft
schedule.detail: Mixed boulder and brush terrain below the gully proper.

schedule.label: Enter the key snow gully toward the pass
schedule.detail: Steep snow in the last 200-300 ft; ice axe required, crampons/microspikes recommended.

schedule.label: Top out at Point-5,841 pass
schedule.detail: Bergschrund/moat crossing may be needed near the top of the gully.

schedule.label: Summit Burnt Boot Peak
schedule.detail: A short class 3-4 ridge scramble and talus from the pass to the summit.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the route; descending gully snow softens through the day.

days.objective: Climb Burnt Boot Peak (6,483–6,540 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and retrace the Dutch Miller Gap Trail back down to the trailhead/road.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day backpack: ~7.5 mi/~1,400 ft each way to camp near Hardscrabble Horse Camp, bookending a ~4.3-mile, ~3,600 ft round-trip summit day via the north gully.

itinerary.cal: NPS backcountry permit required (issued at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center); the Depot Creek FSR approach from the BC side needs a high-clearance 4x4 and is best done July-September once the road and upper glacier/saddle are clear.

days.note: From the Depot Creek Road trailhead (BC side, ~2,350 ft), hike past Monument 65 and up through old-growth forest and brush to Depot Creek Falls, then continue to Lake Ouzel (~5,700 ft). This is notoriously slow, bushwhacky terrain despite the modest mileage — expect roughly 6-9 hours for this leg.
days.title: Approach to Lake Ouzel

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Depot Creek Road parking, ~2,350 ft.

schedule.label: Monument 65
schedule.detail: Border marker; +500 ft.

schedule.label: Depot Creek Falls
schedule.detail: ~1,600 ft cumulative gain.

schedule.label: Arrive Lake Ouzel camp
schedule.detail: ~5,700 ft, ~3,550 ft cumulative gain.

days.objective: Reach the Lake Ouzel bivy/camp

days.note: Short but steep carry above Lake Ouzel over ledgey rock onto the toe of the Redoubt Glacier, roping up for the flat, low-crevasse-hazard glacier crossing to a rock-outcrop camp on the saddle. Many parties use this as a half-day and rest/prep gear in the afternoon.
days.title: Move to Redoubt Glacier saddle high camp
days.objective: Establish high camp at ~7,150-7,400 ft

days.note: A long roped traverse of the Redoubt Glacier (visibility can drop to ~50 yards in cloud) leads to the base of the NE ridge headwall, where two pitches of low 5th class rock gain the ridge crest before class 3-4 scrambling to the 8,407 ft summit. "Easy" is relative — this is a full, long day with real exposure and route-finding.
days.title: Summit push: Northwest Spire (Easy Mox)

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Roped travel across the Redoubt Glacier.

schedule.label: Reach ridge crest
schedule.detail: Via the headwall's low 5th class rock, ~900 ft gained.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: 8.9 hr from camp; final scrambling to the 8,407 ft top.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge and headwall, downclimbing/rappelling as needed.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: ~5.3 hr descent.

days.objective: Climb the Northeast Ridge to the NW (Easy Mox) summit and return to high camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse the full approach in one long push — down off the glacier, past Lake Ouzel, Depot Creek Falls and Monument 65 back to the road. Some parties split this into two days if the crew is tired or the crossings are running high.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Depot Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 4-day trip (strong parties compress to 3): roughly 21-24 miles round trip with ~6,000-7,000 ft of cumulative gain to the 8,407 ft summit, with two long, slow approach/exit days bracketing a hard Class 4-5 glacier-and-headwall summit day from a Redoubt Glacier saddle camp.

road.name: Chilliwack Lake Road / Depot Creek Road (British Columbia, Canada)
road.status: gravel forest service road, rough with erosion beyond ~2.5 km; unmaintained climbers' trail beyond road end
road.driveNote: No US road reaches this peak directly. The standard approach drives north into Canada on Chilliwack Lake FSR and Depot Creek Road, then walks a climbers' trail back across the international border to Redoubt Glacier — the Mox Peaks are one of the few Cascades objectives approached this way.
road.seasonalGate: Seasonal snow and brush limit the approach window; the road has also seen periodic washouts/landslides.

itinerary.cal: Dosewallips Road has been closed to vehicles since a 2002 washout (foot/bike only past the closure), adding several miles each way beyond older trip reports' mileage.

days.note: From the Dosewallips Road washout, bike or walk the closed road to the unsigned Lake Constance climbers' path, then climb it steeply to camp at Lake Constance. Expect steady, unrelenting switchbacks gaining most of the day's elevation in the final 2-3 miles.
days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach camp at Lake Constance

days.note: An alpine start on firm snow up a broad couloir into a narrow, moat-lined snow defile, then a steep discontinuous snow finger gaining the East Ridge. A short Class 3-4 rock step gains the ridge, and from there it's a Class 2-3 scramble on loose-to-solid pillow basalt to the summit. Descend by reversing the same line, down-climbing/rappelling the rock step and glissading or plunge-stepping the gully where snow allows.
days.title: Summit day: South Gully-East Ridge

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start to catch the snow while firm.

schedule.label: Enter the South Gully
schedule.detail: Broad couloir narrowing into a moated snow defile.

schedule.label: Top of the snow finger
schedule.detail: Exit onto the East Ridge by a short Class 3-4 rock step; stow snow tools if rock takes over.

schedule.label: East Ridge scramble
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 scrambling on pillow basalt along the crest to the true summit.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Northeast summit, 7,672'.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Down-climb/rappel the rock step, descend the gully.

days.objective: Climb to the Northeast summit (7,672') and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse the approach, dropping back down toward the Dosewallips River trail and out to the trailhead (or bike cache, given the road washout closure). Mostly downhill and straightforward after the technical day prior.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Descend to the Dosewallips trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip covering roughly 16 miles round trip and about 6,000 ft of gain to the 7,672' NE summit; strong, fast parties sometimes compress the approach and hike-out into a single day for a 2-day trip, or combine it with Mount Constance or Warrior Peak from the same camp.

itinerary.cal: Lake Constance camping needs an Olympic NP wilderness permit (limited nightly quota via recreation.gov), and the Dosewallips Road washout adds a multi-mile bike/walk before the trailhead each way.

days.note: Bike or walk the washed-out Dosewallips road, then climb the very steep 2-mile Lake Constance Trail (~3,300 ft gain) to camp at the lake. Carry the rope and rack for the next day's technical climbing.
days.title: Approach to Lake Constance camp
days.objective: Reach camp at Lake Constance with a rock rack

days.note: Hike up Avalanche Canyon to Crystal Pass at the base of the arête, then pitch out (or simul-climb the lower ledges) roughly 5 pitches of mostly class 3-4 rock with a few low-5th-class steps to the summit ridge. Most parties do NOT reverse the arête to descend — instead they downclimb the standard south-side terrain (past the notches near the Finger/Terrible Traverse) back into Avalanche Canyon, which makes for a long, complex descent.
days.title: Climb the West Arête

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Up Avalanche Canyon toward Crystal Pass.

schedule.label: Rack up at the base
schedule.detail: Reach the start of the arête near Crystal Pass.

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: Pitch 1 around a small tower and up a crack with fixed webbing onto the arête.

schedule.label: Top out on the arête
schedule.detail: Reach the summit ridge crest; short Class 2-3 to the true summit.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Via the long south-side downclimb, not the arête.

days.objective: Climb the Grade III West Arête (5.4-5.5) to the summit

days.note: Descend the Lake Constance Trail and road-walk/bike back to the cars.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Break camp and exit to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, 2-night trip: hike in, one long technical summit day (~13 hr including the complex south-side descent), hike out — matches the published two-days-hiking, one-day-climbing plan for this route.

road.name: Dosewallips River Road (FS 2610)
road.status: Washed out / gated short of the former trailhead - verify current status
road.driveNote: Road-walk required to reach the Lake Constance trail

itinerary.cal: Twin Lakes Rd (FS 3065) can be rough or seasonally gated below the lakes, and the gully often holds snow into July, favoring an ice axe/microspikes for early-season attempts.

days.note: From the Twin Lakes trailhead, follow the High Pass trail north over Low Pass and High Pass, then leave the trail a short way past High Pass and traverse/descend slightly into the basin below Larrabee's south face. Scramble scree and boulders to a gully system at ~6,900 ft (take the right-hand of two narrow chutes), climb loose rock to gain the south ridge, then follow the ridge crest (favoring the west side) to the summit. Descend by reversing the route — the loose, chossy rock makes the descent nearly as slow as the ascent, and a helmet is considered mandatory due to rockfall.
days.title: Twin Lakes to summit and back, car-to-car

schedule.label: Leave trailhead area
schedule.detail: Twin Lakes Rd is rough/rutted and sometimes gated below the lakes; if impassable, park near Yellow Aster Butte TH, adding ~2.3 mi each way and ~1,500 ft of climbing on the walk in.

schedule.label: Twin Lakes, start High Pass trail
schedule.detail: Head north past the lakes toward Low Pass then High Pass.

schedule.label: Leave trail, enter south-face basin
schedule.detail: A short way past High Pass, traverse and drop slightly into the basin facing Larrabee's south side.

schedule.label: Ascend the gully
schedule.detail: At ~6,900 ft find the two narrow parallel chutes; take the right-hand one, staying climber's right on better rock, to broken terrain and the ridge crest.

schedule.label: Summit (7,865 ft)
schedule.detail: Follow the ridge, favoring the west side, to the top.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Reverse the full route; loose rock makes downclimbing the gully slow and rockfall-prone.

days.objective: Summit Mount Larrabee via the South Ridge gully

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day car-to-car: roughly 8 miles round trip with about 4,200 ft of gain, typically 7-9 hours including a slow, loose descent; strong parties have done it in 6, casual parties closer to 9-10.

itinerary.cal: Requires biking ~6-7 mi of a gated logging road each way; best done once the approach talus/ridge snow has melted out, roughly July-September.

days.note: Standard single-day outing: bike the gated Middle Fork Nooksack logging road, hike a rough climbers' path to the Orsino Creek basin, then scramble Class 2-3 up the West Ridge crest to a short 5th-class step just below the summit block that most parties bypass by traversing right (south) off the crest; parties who stay on the crest may rope up and rappel it. Reverse the same line to descend.
days.title: Car-to-car: West Ridge

schedule.label: Leave trailhead on bikes
schedule.detail: Ride the quarry/logging road toward the North Twin trail junction.

schedule.label: Stash bikes, start hiking
schedule.detail: Overgrown climbers' path through forest toward Orsino Creek.

schedule.label: Orsino Creek basin
schedule.detail: Best water source on the route; filter here before the dry ridge.

schedule.label: Gain the West Ridge crest
schedule.detail: Begin sustained Class 2-3 scrambling on solid olivine.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Short rappel/5th-class step ~400 ft below the top; some parties rope up here.

schedule.label: Back at bikes, ride out
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge and descent path; arrive trailhead by evening.

days.objective: Summit South Twin Sister (7,004 ft) via the West Ridge

itinerary.totalNote: A long but standard single day: ~11-12 hrs car-to-car, ~21 mi round trip (including the bike approach) and ~6,100 ft gain, with an optional short rappel near the top only if the ridge crest is followed.

road.name: FR 38 (Middle Fork Road) via Mosquito Lake Road off WA-542
road.status: Gravel Forest Service road, rougher toward its end; FR 38 sustained washout damage in the December 2025 Whatcom County floods and has been closed to vehicles at milepost 7 by a washout since 27 July 2026, with no end date given on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026 — vehicle access beyond the damage point is not advised (foot/bike travel only). Confirm current drivable distance with the Mt. Baker Ranger District before your trip.
road.driveNote: From WA-542 just past milepost 16, take Mosquito Lake Road ~4.8 miles, then FR 38 south to the Middle Fork Nooksack River bridge/gate area, where the old logging/quarry-road approach to the Twin Sisters basin begins.

itinerary.cal: Artist Point road (WA-542) typically doesn't open until snow clears, usually in mid-to-late June; the route is usually snow-covered well into early summer.

days.note: A short, popular half-day outing above treeline. From the Artist Point trailhead (~5,100 ft), switchback up a short cliff band onto the broad Table Mountain plateau, then walk the open tableland west with big views of Mt. Baker, Ptarmigan Ridge, and the Chain Lakes basin to a pair of tarns mirroring Mt. Shuksan - the standard turnaround. Strong parties can continue on unmarked, looser scramble terrain toward the high point or down toward Chain Lakes, but most hikers simply retrace their steps.
days.title: Artist Point to Table Mountain plateau (car-to-car)

schedule.label: Leave Artist Point trailhead
schedule.detail: Parking area at ~5,100 ft; a Northwest Forest Pass is required.

schedule.label: Top of switchbacks
schedule.detail: Gain ~400 ft up the cliff band; views open over Heather Meadows.

schedule.label: Reach the plateau rim
schedule.detail: Mt. Baker, Ptarmigan Ridge, and Chain Lakes basin come into view.

schedule.label: Twin tarns / standard turnaround
schedule.detail: Mt. Shuksan reflections; most parties turn back here (2.6 mi RT).

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Reverse the trail; total outing under 2.5 hrs for most hikers.

days.objective: Reach the twin tarns viewpoint below Mt. Shuksan; optional scramble to the true summit

itinerary.totalNote: A short, popular half-day scramble: roughly 1.5-2.5 hrs car-to-car for the standard 2.6 mi round trip to the tarns, ~725 ft gain - not an overnight trip.

itinerary.cal: FR 2361 to the Upper South Fork Skokomish trailhead is closed to vehicles Oct 1-Apr 30; the trail beyond Sundown Lake is essentially unmaintained (heavy blowdown, faint tread, easy to lose) and dry beyond Camp Bellevue, so this is best done July-September after snow/blowdown clears, carrying/caching all water for the final push.

days.note: From the Upper South Fork Skokomish trailhead, climb the South Fork Skokomish River Trail over Sundown Pass to Sundown Lake, then pick up the primitive, largely unmaintained Six Ridge Trail over Six Ridge Pass to McGravey Lakes. Parties describe near-constant route-finding through overgrown meadows, faded cairns, and repeated ridge undulations; camp near McGravey Lakes (about 10 miles) or Camp Bellevue (nearly 13 miles), the last reliable water before the peak.
days.title: Approach to high camp near McGravey Lakes / Camp Bellevue
days.objective: Reach a high camp below Mount Olson via Sundown Pass and the primitive Six Ridge Trail

days.note: From camp, sidehill the faint Mount Olson Way Trail across broken, exposed ground to a small tarn at the base of the peak, then scramble roughly 1,000 ft up steep meadow and heather (55-60 degrees in spots, hands-on rock, rated class 3 in the published description) to the summit block. Descend the same way back to camp.
days.title: Summit push via the Mount Olson Way Trail and boot path

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Start along the faint Mount Olson Way Trail toward the peak.

schedule.label: Reach the tarn below Mount Olson
schedule.detail: Steep, faint side-hill traverse over a ridge/saddle to the small tarn at the peak's base.

schedule.label: Start the boot path
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 scramble up steep meadow and heather on the SE-facing slope.

schedule.label: Summit (5,289 ft)
schedule.detail: Curve around a heather bench near the top to the true summit; views across the interior Olympics.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the boot path and ridge back down to the tarn.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the Mount Olson Way Trail traverse to camp.

days.objective: Climb Mount Olson (5,289 ft) via the tarn and SE-face boot path

days.note: Reverse the Six Ridge / Sundown Pass approach back to the car. It's mostly net downhill, but the primitive tread, brush, and repeated ridge undulations still make it a full day.
days.title: Hike out to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to the Upper South Fork Skokomish trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A rugged ~3-day round trip via Sundown Pass and the primitive Six Ridge/Mount Olson Way Trail, with a high camp near McGravey Lakes/Camp Bellevue and a steep class 2-3 scramble to the 5,289 ft summit — not a car-to-car day trip.

road.name: South Fork Skokomish Road (Forest Roads 23 and 2361) to the Upper South Fork Skokomish Trailhead
road.driveNote: From Shelton: US 101 north ~6 mi, west on Skokomish Valley Road ~5.3 mi, then FR 23, staying on it past the FR 2353 junction, and right onto FR 2361 for about 5 mi to its end at the trailhead; FR 2361 is closed to vehicles Oct 1-Apr 30. This is a different drainage from the Hamma Hamma Road approach (used for Mount Skokomish/Mount Stone); verify current road status before driving.

itinerary.cal: The Canyon Creek bridge on the access road (Tupso Pass Road / FR 41) is washed out and the road is closed to vehicles beyond that point -- this adds roughly 9 miles each way (about 18 miles round trip) of road walking or biking if you can't drive to the trailhead; check MBS National Forest road status before you go. Late Aug-Oct gives the driest trail and least snow on the summit slope.

days.note: From the Saddle Lake Trailhead, climb through old-growth forest past Saddle Lake and up into the alpine meadows of Goat Flats, the standard camp for a Three Fingers trip. Bears frequent the area, so hang or canister your food.
days.title: Hike in to Goat Flats camp
days.objective: Reach Goat Flats camp

days.note: Leave camp early for the push over Tin Can Gap and across the glacier to Camp Saddle: a steep snow slope (ice axe, crampons advisable even late season) followed by a rock scramble and a short rebarred ladder up to the 1930s fire lookout cabin. After the summit, break camp and hike the ~4.5 miles back out.
days.title: Summit push and hike out

schedule.label: Leave Goat Flats camp
schedule.detail: Light packs for the summit push; leave the rest of camp set up.

schedule.label: Reach Tin Can Gap
schedule.detail: Start of the steep snow slope; axe and crampons on if icy.

schedule.label: Ladder pitch to the lookout
schedule.detail: Exposed final scramble up rebarred ladders; sure footing required.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: 1930s lookout cabin, 6,854 ft.

schedule.label: Back at camp, break down tents
schedule.detail: Full packs on for the hike out.

days.objective: Tag the South Peak lookout, then pack out to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, 1-night trip: ~4.5 mi and 3,000 ft up to Goat Flats camp on day one, then a long summit-and-hike-out day (~7.7 mi) with the final snow slope, rock scramble, and rebarred ladder to the historic lookout.

road.name: Tupso Pass Road (FR 41)
road.status: Permanently closed to vehicle travel beyond the Canyon Creek bridge (~mile 8.5)
road.driveNote: Park at the vehicle closure at the Canyon Creek bridge; from there it's roughly 9 more miles of road walking or mountain biking to the Tupso Pass trailhead at the end of the road
road.seasonalGate: Vehicle gate at Canyon Creek bridge is a standing closure, not seasonal, pending any Forest Service repair

itinerary.cal: The Teanaway approach road is typically snowed in until early-mid June.

days.note: From the Esmeralda/Ingalls trailhead, climb over Longs Pass and drop into the Ingalls Creek valley to camp within striking distance of the couloir. A moderate half-day approach for most parties.
days.title: Approach to Ingalls Creek camp
days.objective: Reach a camp near the base of the Cascadian Couloir

days.note: An early start up the couloir's scree/snow gains the false summit and then the true summit in 5-8 hours for most parties; the route is reversed back through camp and out the same day for a long finish.
days.title: Summit via the Cascadian Couloir and exit

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: 7-8 hrs from camp is typical for an average-fitness party

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Break camp

days.objective: Climb the couloir to the false and true summits, then return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A moderate 2-day trip: roughly 8,100+ ft of cumulative gain/loss (the profile crosses Longs Pass twice) over about 12-13 mi round trip; strong parties do it car-to-car in a single long day instead.

road.name: North Fork Teanaway Road / FR 9737 to Esmeralda Trailhead
road.status: Paved for the first several miles, then unpaved forest road for roughly the final 9 miles; normally passable to 2WD high-clearance vehicles in summer.
road.seasonalGate: Not gated, but snow can block the upper miles into late May or June in heavy-snow years.

itinerary.cal: North Cascades NP requires a wilderness camping permit for the Eldorado/Inspiration zone (self-register or reserve ahead in peak summer); route is typically snow-covered and glacier travel is safest June–early Sept before crevasses open up, and Cascade River Road (gated, rough) must be snow-free.

days.note: From the Cascade River Road trailhead (~2,100 ft), cross the river on a log/boulder crossing and follow the climbers' path through timber into Eldorado Creek Basin, then continue up boulder fields and onto the glacier to a flat camp near the rocks at the Eldorado-Inspiration Glacier saddle. Most parties rope up once on glacier ice for the final stretch.
days.title: Approach to Inspiration Glacier high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp on the Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier (~7,500 ft)

days.note: A long alpine day: contour the upper Inspiration Glacier to Klawatti Col, continue along Klawatti's north ridge on the McAllister Glacier, then make a rising traverse to the Klawatti-Austera col, which requires a short rappel (~75 ft, old fixed anchor) down onto the Klawatti Glacier. Traverse high and left across the Klawatti Glacier, drop packs and crampons, and scramble broken 3rd/4th class rock (with a short low-5th-class step on the true summit's NE side) to the top; most parties stop at the easier 3rd-class sub-summit since the true summit's final 30 ft is loose. Reverse the whole traverse to camp, including a belayed pitch of steep rock (up to 5.6) to regain the Klawatti-Austera col from below.
days.title: Glacier traverse and summit push

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start on the glacier while snow is firm.

schedule.label: Reach Klawatti Col
schedule.detail: Easy, fast glacier travel across upper Inspiration Glacier.

schedule.label: Klawatti-Austera col
schedule.detail: Rising traverse on McAllister Glacier; rappel ~75 ft to the Klawatti Glacier.

schedule.label: Summit (or sub-summit)
schedule.detail: Drop packs, scramble broken rock; extended break to dry gear and eat.

schedule.label: Regain Klawatti-Austera col
schedule.detail: Belayed pitch of steep rock (up to 5.6) climbing back up from the Klawatti Glacier.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the glacier traverse; total day roughly 11-13 hours.

days.objective: Traverse Inspiration Glacier → Klawatti Col → McAllister Glacier → Klawatti-Austera col → Klawatti Glacier to the Austera summit and back to camp

days.note: Pack up and retrace the approach back down through the glacier, boulder fields, and timber to the Cascade River Road trailhead, typically arriving by early-to-mid afternoon.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Break camp and descend to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 3-day glacier trek rather than a technical climb: roughly 18 miles round trip with ~7,000+ ft of cumulative gain across three glaciers and two cols, including a short rappel and a belayed 5.6 pitch to regain the Klawatti-Austera col; very fit parties have done it car-to-car in a single ~12.5-hour push, but a 2-3 night camp at the Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier is the standard way most parties do it.

itinerary.cal: Cascade River Road usually doesn't open until late May/June depending on snowpack, and the Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier zone is a high-occupancy North Cascades NP backcountry zone requiring an advance wilderness permit reservation.

days.note: From the Eldorado Creek trailhead (~2,100 ft), climb steep forest and boulder-field trail, cross the Eldorado Glacier's lower ice, and gain the broad Inspiration Glacier bench. Camp near 7,500 ft (or lower, at Eldorado Creek/Roush Creek basins in leaner snow years).
days.title: Approach to glacier high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp on the Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier

days.note: Alpine start to catch the couloir's snow/ice in firm morning condition. Simul-climb or short-pitch the couloir's 2-3 long pitches (up to WI2-3), top out near the summit ridge, then descend the East Ridge knife-edge and cross the Inspiration Glacier back to camp.
days.title: NW Couloir summit push

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start for firm snow/ice in the couloir.

schedule.label: Reach couloir base
schedule.detail: Rope up, switch to crampons/tools.

schedule.label: Begin climbing
schedule.detail: 2-3 long pitches of snow/ice, simul-climbed or short-pitched depending on conditions.

schedule.label: Top out couloir
schedule.detail: Join the upper mountain near the summit ridge.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Via East Ridge / Inspiration Glacier descent.

days.objective: Climb the NW Couloir to the 8,872 ft summit and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and retrace the approach back down to the Eldorado Creek trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Break camp and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip: a day up to glacier high camp, a day climbing the NW Couloir's 2-3 pitches to the 8,872 ft summit, and a day hiking out (~6,700 ft gain, ~10 mi round trip); very fit ice-climbing parties sometimes do it car-to-car in a single 11-21 hr push instead.

road.name: Cascade River Road
road.status: Open seasonally; gravel
road.driveNote: From Marblemount drive Cascade River Road to the Eldorado Creek trailhead; parking is limited.
road.seasonalGate: May be gated by snow or washouts into early summer

itinerary.cal: Route is dry-season rock only; Hwy 20 (North Cascades Highway) is gated by snow in winter and typically doesn't open until mid/late spring, so plan for a June-September window.

days.note: This is a standard single-day alpine rock outing out of Washington Pass, not an overnight trip. Parties hike the Blue Lake Trail and climber's path into the basin below the Liberty Bell group, scramble to the base, climb 4-5 pitches of sustained 5.8-5.9 up the corner/dihedral system, then descend via a bolted rappel line straight back to the packs.
days.title: Car-to-car: Northwest Corner (Boving-Pollack)

schedule.label: Leave Blue Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: Early start is typical to beat afternoon thunderstorms and other parties to the route.

schedule.label: Reach base of route
schedule.detail: ~1.5 mi on the Blue Lake Trail, then the well-worn climber's trail into the basin and a short scramble to the start.

schedule.label: Start climbing (P1, 5.8 corner)
schedule.detail: 5 pitches, mostly sustained 5.9 with a burly 3-4" crack higher up; some parties link to 4 pitches.

schedule.label: Top out
schedule.detail: ~3.5 hrs of climbing for a fit, competent party.

schedule.label: Begin bolted rappels down the West Face
schedule.detail: About six single-rope rappels on bolts land back at the packs; a 70m rope is more comfortable than a 60m.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Retrace the climber's trail and Blue Lake Trail to the car.

days.objective: Climb the 5-pitch NW Corner and be back at the car same day

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day car-to-car: roughly 7-8 hours round trip, about 2,600 ft of total gain over ~5.2 miles, no camping involved.

itinerary.cal: Entiat River Road (FR-51) can be gated or snowed-in below Cottonwood Camp trailhead in early season, adding several miles of road walking/biking to the approach.

days.note: Hike the Entiat River Trail from the Entiat River (Cottonwood Camp) trailhead up-valley to camp near 5,100 ft in upper Entiat Meadows, below the south face of Buckskin. Trail is in good shape early on but gets brushy with downed timber from the 2015 Wolverine Fire past Candy Creek, and mosquitoes can be thick in the meadows.
days.title: Approach to Entiat Meadows camp
days.objective: Reach camp in upper Entiat Meadows

days.note: From camp, climb the rib/gully closest to camp on the south side (least brush, most direct line) rather than the old trail on the east ridge, gaining about 3,000 ft to the summit. Descend the same way through scree and slick heather; afternoon thunderstorms are a real hazard on this exposed south face, so plan to be off the summit by early-to-mid morning.
days.title: Summit day: Southwest Slopes

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start to beat afternoon thunderstorms.

schedule.label: Reach base of south gully/rib
schedule.detail: Begin the ~3,000 ft climb on scree and heather.

schedule.label: Summit (8,127 ft)
schedule.detail: Watch for building cumulus; don't linger if weather looks unstable.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the gully/rib route.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Rest of the day free for a layover or an early start on the hike out.

days.objective: Climb Buckskin Mountain (8,127 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the Entiat River Trail back to the trailhead. The lower valley can get hot in the afternoon, so an early departure from camp helps avoid the worst heat between Snow Brushy and Aurora Creeks.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day backpack is the standard way to climb Buckskin: ~35.6 mi round trip on the Entiat River Trail plus a ~3,000 ft, ~6 mi summit day from Entiat Meadows camp; very fit parties have done the whole thing car-to-car in one very long day (~30 mi, 5,000+ ft, mostly done at night with a bike shuttle on the trail).

road.name: Entiat River Road (County Rd 19 -> FR 51 at mile 27 -> unpaved FR 5100 at mile 34)
road.status: Paved to about mile 34, then gravel FR 5100 to the trailhead; single-lane sections with pullouts near the old washout/burn area. Closed: the Little Giant Fire closure (Okanogan-Wenatchee order 06-17-07-2026-40, in effect since September 3, 2026 and through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner) closes Entiat River Road 5100 and the Entiat River Trail #1400. Check with the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest before you go.
road.driveNote: 37.3 miles from the town of Entiat (reached via US-97A) to the Entiat River Trailhead at 3,150 ft - this is a standard drive-to trailhead, not boat/ferry access.
road.seasonalGate: Winter gate near the Entiat Sno-Park (~mile 25); reopening date varies by year, sometimes into May.

itinerary.cal: Snow lingers on the approach into June (patches from ~4,600 ft, solid snowpack by ~5,500 ft per late-May/June reports); check Copper Glance Road (FR-5130/Eightmile Creek Rd) conditions before driving in.

days.note: Hike the Copper Glance Trail up along Copper Glance Creek, crossing a broken bridge, to a camp at ~6,600 ft on a knoll near a seasonal tarn (some parties camp instead at Copper Glance Lake a bit further on). Trail is bare at the start with snow patches showing up higher in early season.
days.title: Approach to Copper Glance Basin camp
days.objective: Reach camp on the knoll near the seasonal tarn in Copper Glance Basin

days.note: Leave camp early for the ridge; most parties tag West Craggy first by mid-morning, then continue to Big Craggy's summit, before retracing the route back to camp (~7.4 hr round trip). The southeast slope has loose, rubbly scree with some rockfall danger in the last 500 ft below the summit. After returning to camp, pack up and hike the 3.3 mi back down to the trailhead.
days.title: Summit push (Big Craggy + West Craggy) and hike out

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light day-pack for the summit push, headed up toward the connecting saddle.

schedule.label: West Craggy summit
schedule.detail: ~2.6 hr / 1,800 ft from camp; reached by mid-morning.

schedule.label: Big Craggy summit
schedule.detail: ~5.6 hr from camp via the connecting saddle and southeast ridge scree.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: ~7.4 hr round trip for both summits.

schedule.label: Break camp, start hike out
schedule.detail: Full pack back down Copper Glance Trail.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Reverse the ~3.3 mi / 2,800 ft descent.

days.objective: Climb Big Craggy (and typically West Craggy via the connecting saddle), then break camp and hike back to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day overnight trip for most parties: ~3.3 mi / 2,800 ft up to a Copper Glance Basin camp on Day 1, then a ~7.4-hour round-trip summit push (commonly tagging West Craggy too via the connecting saddle) plus the hike out on Day 2 — roughly 11-12 mi and 5,600 ft total; strong parties instead do the whole thing car-to-car in one long day (~11-12 mi, ~5,600 ft if adding West Craggy).

road.name: West Chewuch Road (County Rd 1213) to Forest Road 5130 (Eightmile Creek Road)
road.status: gravel, narrow/single-lane in spots
road.driveNote: From Winthrop, take West Chewuch Road (County Rd 1213) north about 9 miles, then turn left onto FR 5130 (Eightmile Creek Road) for about 12.5 miles northwest along Eightmile Creek to the small signed Copper Glance Trailhead pullout on the right (3,800 ft). Passable to most cars in season, but call the Methow Valley Ranger District for current washout status before a trip.
road.seasonalGate: Not gated, but typically snow-blocked from late fall through late spring; realistic access is roughly June-October depending on snowpack.

itinerary.cal: The Suiattle River Road (FR 26) has had washout closures in recent years and the Milk Creek Trail itself has been in disrepair for a decade-plus — verify both before planning this approach; this is a technical route (rope, ice screws, pickets) best done with a fit, experienced party.

days.note: Drive the Suiattle River Road to its end, then follow the Suiattle Pass Trail to a bridge over the Suiattle River and pick up the PCT southbound, covering most of the ~16-mile approach on day one.
days.title: Approach toward Milk Creek basin
days.objective: Get most of the way to the northwest-side base camp

days.note: Finish the PCT approach to a base camp in the East Fork Milk Creek basin on the mountain's north/northwest side, staging for the ridge climb.
days.title: Reach base camp
days.objective: Establish base camp in the East Fork Milk Creek basin

days.note: Climb Frostbite Ridge over the Rabbit Ears (a class-3 downclimb of roughly 150 ft) and steep snow/ice sections to the summit, then descend the non-technical Sitkum Glacier to a different camp on the west side — this is a traverse, not an out-and-back.
days.title: Frostbite Ridge to the summit, descend to a western camp

schedule.label: Leave base camp
schedule.detail: Long day ahead; alpine start.

schedule.label: Rabbit Ears notch
schedule.detail: Class-3 downclimb of ~150 ft off the top of the ridge; steep 45-50° snow/ice sections nearby.

schedule.label: Reach western camp
schedule.detail: Down the Sitkum Glacier to a Boulder Basin-area camp; long day, often finishing in the evening.

days.objective: Summit Glacier Peak (10,550 ft) via Frostbite Ridge, descend the Sitkum to a Boulder-Basin-area camp

days.note: Hike out on the PCT south to White Pass and down the North Fork Sauk Trail to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead — logistically a point-to-point trip requiring a car shuttle or long road walk back.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to a trailhead (different from the approach)

itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day traverse (~30-32 miles, ~9,200 ft gain) — long approach in from Milk Creek, technical ridge climbing with a class-3/ice crux, and a descent to a different trailhead than the one you started from.

road.name: North Fork Sauk Road / Sloan Creek Road (FR 49)
road.status: Gravel, with rough and washed-out sections; medium or high clearance is recommended and a low-clearance car may not clear them.
road.driveNote: From Darrington, follow the Mountain Loop Highway about 16.3 miles to Sloan Creek Road (FR 49), then about 6.6 miles to the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead. The White Chuck Road (FR 23) approach from the north is a different start and is closed at milepost 3.7.
road.seasonalGate: The Mountain Loop Highway's Deer Creek to Bedal section is gated through the winter and typically reopens in mid-May; FR 49 can hold snow into early summer in heavy years.

itinerary.cal: Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) typically isn't fully snow-free/passable until mid-June, and the route holds snow into summer, so most ascents happen late June through September.

days.note: From the Chiwawa River / Trinity trailhead (2,800 ft), follow Chiwawa River Trail #1550 along the old Red Mountain mining road, passing the Buck Creek and Chiwawa Basin trail junctions around 4,800 ft. The lower trail is brushy/overgrown in summer; expect a long, steady climb through forest into open basin terrain for camp.
days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp near 5,900-6,300 ft on the old Red Mountain mining road

days.note: From camp, cross crusty morning snow slopes up to the broad saddle near 7,200 ft between Chiwawa and Fortress, then work up the southwest snowfield/talus with a short Class 2-3 ledge traverse to the summit ridge. Many parties tag Fortress Mountain's Class 3-4 east ridge from the same col on the same day.
days.title: Summit day: Chiwawa Mountain via SW snowfield

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Cross firm morning snow before it softens.

schedule.label: Reach Chiwawa-Fortress saddle (~7,200 ft)
schedule.detail: Broad, gently inclined snow ramp leads to the col.

schedule.label: Southwest snowfield and ledge traverse
schedule.detail: Class 2+ ledges round the south rib onto the SW slopes.

schedule.label: Summit (8,459 ft)
schedule.detail: Typical summit arrival on a full-value day.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Descend the same snow/talus line; glissade where safe.

days.objective: Climb Chiwawa Mountain (8,459 ft) and return to high camp

days.note: Retrace the Red Mountain mining road/Chiwawa River Trail back down through the brushy lower miles to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Chiwawa River trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-3 day trip for most parties: ~19-20 miles round trip with roughly 5,700 ft cumulative gain/loss; camp sits near 5,900-6,300 ft on the old mining road, with a long (7+ hr) summit push on day two. Very strong parties have done it car-to-car in a single ~14-16 hr day.

itinerary.cal: Boston Basin sites are won through NPS's early-access wilderness permit lottery (roughly 15% odds for the May 15-Oct 10 season); Cascade River Road is gated and its opening date varies year to year with winter damage/snowpack.

days.note: Hike the climbers' path from the Cascade River Road trailhead through forest and boulder fields into Boston Basin, camping near 6,400 ft in the basin below the peak. An easy afternoon to sort gear and rack for the next day.
days.title: Approach to Boston Basin camp
days.objective: Establish camp in upper Boston Basin

days.note: Alpine start from camp, gain the East Ridge and follow ~8 pitches of low 5th-class rock to the true summit, then reverse over the summit block and downclimb/rappel the West Ridge to its notch and couloir back into Boston Basin. A full traverse avoids reversing technical terrain but makes for a long day.
days.title: East Ridge to summit, descend West Ridge (full traverse)

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start on the east side of the peak

schedule.label: Gain the East Ridge
schedule.detail: Start of the 8-pitch ridge climb

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Traverse to the true (west) summit

schedule.label: Begin West Ridge descent
schedule.detail: Downclimb/rappel to the West Ridge notch and couloir

schedule.label: Hike out (or camp a 2nd night)
schedule.detail: Most push out same day; some stay over and hike out the next morning

days.objective: Climb the East Ridge and descend via the West Ridge notch and couloir

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip: ~4 hrs / 2,800 ft hiking in to a Boston Basin camp, then a long 12-14 hr day climbing the East Ridge (8 pitches) and descending the West Ridge for a full ridge traverse, ~5,200 ft total gain.

itinerary.cal: Best done July-September once the Porkbelly Ridge brush and upper ridge are snow-free; the drivable end of Bacon Creek Road can vary year to year with washouts, sometimes adding extra road-walking to the approach.

days.note: From the end of Bacon Creek Road (~850 ft) the route leaves the last road tread almost immediately and grinds straight up Porkbelly Ridge — trip reports call it one of the brushiest ridges in the range, with no consistent boot path despite published mentions of one. Push through brush, timber, and steep duff to a camp near treeline below Berdeen Peak, saving the summit scramble for fresh legs the next morning.
days.title: Bushwhack up Porkbelly Ridge to high camp
days.objective: Reach a camp in the basin below Berdeen Peak's east ridge

days.note: Finish the climb to the East Ridge and scramble to the summit (mostly Class 3, with one or two Class 4 moves near the top), then reverse the ascent line all the way back down through the Berdeen Lake basin and the Porkbelly Ridge brush to Bacon Creek Road. It's a long combined summit-and-exit day, but downhill travel through already-broken brush moves noticeably faster than the way in.
days.title: Summit push and full hike out

schedule.label: Break camp
schedule.detail: Many parties stash overnight gear near camp and climb light before returning to pack out.

schedule.label: Gain the East Ridge crest
schedule.detail: Terrain steepens to steep, mossy Class 3 scrambling.

schedule.label: Summit Berdeen Peak (6,420 ft)
schedule.detail: One or two Class 4 moves near the top; views into the Mystery Ridge/Pickets high country.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Break down camp fully and shoulder the overnight pack for the exit.

schedule.label: Re-enter the Porkbelly Ridge brush
schedule.detail: Steep, slow descent through timber and brush back toward the road.

schedule.label: Back at Bacon Creek Road trailhead
schedule.detail: End of the drivable/walkable road at ~850 ft.

days.objective: Tag Berdeen Peak (6,420 ft) via the East Ridge, then reverse the entire route to the car

itinerary.totalNote: A serious 2-day backpack rather than a dayhike: ~14 miles round trip, most of it off-trail through one of the North Cascades' notoriously brushy ridge bushwhacks, with Class 3 (one or two Class 4 moves) scrambling on Berdeen Peak's East Ridge near the top.

road.name: Bacon Creek Road (Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF)
road.driveNote: Leaves WA-20 about 6 miles northeast of Marblemount near Bacon Creek (milepost ~112) and dead-ends at roughly 850 ft elevation. A 2018 rockslide near the 4.7-mile mark narrowed the road to high-clearance vehicles only (repair status unconfirmed) — check current Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF conditions before the drive. The road is also closed by fire: the Forest Service's Electric Fire order (06-05-26-19) closes Bacon Creek Road (FR 1060) from SR 20 to NF 1064, and NF 1064 itself, from September 2 through October 31, 2026, unless rescinded sooner.

itinerary.cal: This is a snow/ice couloir climbed mostly January-April, and into May or even June in big snow years, before it melts out; Longmire/Stevens Canyon Road gates can restrict start and end times (observed as open ~9:30am-4pm in some shoulder-season reports), so plan the day around the gate schedule.

days.note: Park at the Reflection Lakes pullout and approach via Stevens Canyon Road/Tatoosh Creek to the base of the obvious center couloir on Lane Peak's north face (roughly 45-75 min). Climb the couloir on 40-45° snow through its three short steps (the crux is an ~25 ft step near the top), pop out into the sun at the notch, and make the short scramble to the summit. Most parties descend a non-technical line (often the south-face Classic Route) rather than rappelling back down the couloir.
days.title: Car-to-car climb of the Zipper couloir

schedule.label: Leave Reflection Lakes pullout
schedule.detail: Aim to be moving early; the Longmire/Stevens Canyon gate can have restricted hours in shoulder season.

schedule.label: Reach the base of the couloir
schedule.detail: Rope up and gear up for the three mixed/ice steps if conditions warrant.

schedule.label: Top out into the sun at the notch
schedule.detail: Matches trip-report timing of roughly 75 minutes couloir to couloir-top.

schedule.label: Reach the summit
schedule.detail: Short scramble from the notch.

schedule.label: Descend the non-technical south side
schedule.detail: Walk off via the Classic Route line rather than rappelling, conditions permitting.

schedule.label: Back at the car
schedule.detail: Total field time typically 5-6.5 hours.

days.objective: Climb the Zipper to the east-ridge notch and tag the summit

itinerary.totalNote: A single, moderate day: roughly 6 hours and 2,000 ft of gain car-to-car, done well within a morning by most parties.

road.name: Narada Falls parking lot (Paradise road) / Stevens Canyon Road
road.status: Narada Falls lot is plowed and open year-round; Stevens Canyon Rd itself is not plowed in winter
road.driveNote: In winter/spring conditions, park at Narada Falls and travel the closed road/off-trail to Tatoosh Creek; once Stevens Canyon Rd opens for summer, Reflection Lake offers a shorter approach.
road.seasonalGate: Stevens Canyon Rd typically opens to vehicles late June and closes with the first significant snowfall, usually early-to-mid October

itinerary.cal: Climb after snow has melted off the upper ledge traverse (typically mid-summer through fall); most parties bike the 4-mile Monte Cristo road since it's gated to vehicles.

days.note: From Barlow Pass, most parties mountain-bike the gated Monte Cristo road to save time, then hike Forest Trail #708 over Poodle Dog Pass to Twin Lakes. It's a mellow, scenic approach day with time to swim or fish once camp is set.
days.title: Bike & hike to Twin Lakes camp
days.objective: Reach the Twin Lakes basin and set up camp

days.note: Leave camp with a light day pack, stash overnight gear partway up, and climb the West Spur past loose ledges and a short snow patch to a single 4th-class crux move that gains the southwest face. After the summit, retrace the full route back to camp, out to Poodle Dog Pass, and bike the old wagon road to the car — a long day.
days.title: Summit via West Spur, hike all the way out

schedule.label: Depart Twin Lakes camp
schedule.detail: Head out after breakfast toward Columbia's west ridge with day gear.

schedule.label: Stash overnight gear
schedule.detail: Cache packs on a flat ledge to move faster for the summit push.

schedule.label: Traverse loose ledges
schedule.detail: Cross loose ledges and a patch of snow below the cliff band south of the summit block.

schedule.label: 4th-class crux
schedule.detail: A single 4th-class move gains access to the southwest face — the technical crux of the route.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Top out on Columbia Peak, roughly 3 hours above camp.

schedule.label: Back at the car
schedule.detail: Retrieve stashed gear, hike out over Poodle Dog Pass, and bike the wagon road back to the trailhead.

days.objective: Climb Columbia Peak and return to the trailhead same day

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, ~21-mile round trip with roughly 4,900-5,000 ft of total gain: an easy approach day into Twin Lakes camp followed by a long (9-10 hr) summit day that finishes by hiking and biking all the way back to the car.

road.name: Mountain Loop Highway to Barlow Pass Trailhead, then the gated Monte Cristo Road (non-motorized)
road.driveNote: Paved the full 34 miles from Granite Falls to Barlow Pass Trailhead. Beyond the trailhead, the Monte Cristo Road is gravel, gated, and closed to motor vehicles — hike or bike the 4 miles to the townsite. Alternate approach to Blanca Lake: from Index, take Index-Galena Road/FR 63 roughly 13.8 miles paved plus 2 miles gravel to the Blanca Lake Trailhead. That road has been closed to vehicles between mileposts 10 and 14 since December 2025 flood damage, with no repair timeline, and the Beckler Road/Jack Pass detour is closed too (Forest Service alert of June 30, 2026), so the Blanca Lake Trailhead cannot be reached by car; check with the Skykomish Ranger District, (360) 677-2414, before you go.

itinerary.cal: Best conditions are July-September once the approach brush has dried out and the glacier still has manageable snow cover; road washouts on FR-1570 add mileage regardless of season.

days.note: From the FR-1570 pullout walk the brushy, washed-out roadbed almost 2 miles to its end, then climb the steep climbers' trail more than two miles through old growth onto Kindy Ridge and the saddle south of Point 5116, near 4,800 ft. From there the way to Buckindy goes south off trail through the Buckindy Range high country: slow, up-and-down travel that takes most parties two or three days to reach a camp in the basins at the head of Kindy Creek, below Buckindy's north side.
days.title: Approach over Kindy Ridge toward the head of Kindy Creek
days.objective: Reach a camp at the head of Kindy Creek below Buckindy's north side (two or three days from the car)

days.note: An early roped start across the glacier to dodge crevasses in firm morning snow, then a push to the base of the summit block for Class 4 scrambling to the top. The return reverses the same line, staying roped through the crevassed sections back to camp.
days.title: Summit day via the Kindy/Goat Creek Glacier

schedule.label: Leave camp, rope up
schedule.detail: Cross onto the glacier while snow is still firm and crevasse bridges are cold.

schedule.label: Cross crevassed sections of the Kindy/Goat Creek Glacier
schedule.detail: Weave between visible crevasses; some parties place pickets on steeper firn.

schedule.label: Reach base of summit block
schedule.detail: Stash rope/glacier gear where the route transitions to rock.

schedule.label: Class 4 scramble to summit
schedule.detail: Short, exposed scrambling to the true summit.

schedule.label: Begin roped descent
schedule.detail: Downclimb the summit block, re-rope for the glacier.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Off the glacier and back to the basin camp.

days.objective: Climb Buckindy's north side glacier and Class 4 summit block

days.note: Break camp and reverse the approach: back north through the high country to the Kindy Ridge saddle, then down the steep climbers' trail and the brushy roadbed to the FR-1570 pullout. Like the way in, this usually takes more than one day.
days.title: Hike out over Kindy Ridge
days.objective: Return over Kindy Ridge to the car

itinerary.totalNote: A remote multi-day trip: two or three days of mostly off-trail travel each way over Kindy Ridge and the Buckindy high country, with one roped glacier-and-Class-4 summit day from a camp below the north side.

road.name: Cascade River Road to FR-1570 (Kindy Creek Road)
road.status: FR-1570 is a rougher, seasonally maintained spur off Cascade River Road; high-clearance recommended
road.driveNote: About 14.2 miles east of Marblemount on Cascade River Road to the FR-1570 junction, then roughly 2 miles up FR-1570 to a small parking pullout/old trailhead
road.seasonalGate: No fixed winter gate on this spur, but access is snow- and washout-dependent — check current Mt. Baker Ranger District road status before driving

itinerary.cal: The North Fork Entiat River Road (#5606) has had washout/blowdown closures in past seasons well below the historical trailhead, sometimes adding ~5 miles and 1,500 ft of road-walking each way — check current Forest Service road status before the trip.

days.note: From the North Fork Entiat River trailhead (~3,950 ft), hike the North Fork Entiat trail through old burn/blowdown, cross the creek on a rough log/plank crossing around mile 4-5, then climb through meadows to an established camp in the larch basin near the Pyramid Creek trail junction. Most parties arrive by mid-to-late afternoon and set up before dark.
days.title: Approach to larch-basin camp
days.objective: Reach the ~6,800-6,900 ft basin camp beneath Cardinal/Emerald

days.note: Leave camp with a light pack, climb through the basin to the ~7,800 ft bench below Emerald's southeast slopes, then pick a way up the ridge/gully system (loose class 2-3 rock, trending climber's-right near the top) to the summit. Many parties tag nearby Saska Peak on the same outing since it shares the approach bench, but Emerald alone is a half-day round trip from camp.
